2027: APC doesn’t want opposition candidates to campaign anywhere - Galadima
items.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Buba Galadima, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government of creating obstacles for opposition politicians ahead of the 2027 general elections. Galadima alleged that opposition candidates were being prevented from freely campaigning across the country, claiming that some were attacked whenever they visited certain areas. He made the allegations during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Tuesday, where he discussed the political environment ahead of the 2027 elections. “There are blocks put in the path of the opposition. This APC and its government does not want any opposition person to campaign in any part of the country, as they are stoned wherever they go. They also want to make life impossible for those opposite them,” he said. Galadima questioned whether such an environment could be described as democracy, arguing that democratic governance should guarantee political freedoms, including the right to campaign, speak and move freely. “So, why should we call it democracy? We can just as well call it fascism, or dictatorship, or monarchy. They can’t claim to be democrats and not imbibe the tenets of democracy, which is free choice, free speech, free movement, and that is in the constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. The NDC chieftain, however, blamed citizens for allowing what he described as restrictions on political activities to continue. “But all this they are doing is because we citizens have allowed them to do so,” Galadima said. He also questioned the enforcement of campaign spending limits, citing the cost of political advertising and billboards across the country. According to him, the Electoral Act limits campaign spending by political parties to N10 billion, but the cost of erecting billboards in some states could make compliance difficult. “Do you know how much they are asking for one billboard in Abuja? In Imo, it is N1 billion. One billboard, not the whole state. Just to fix one billboard, you pay N1 billion,” he said. Galadima argued that the cost of campaign billboards across the states could exceed the statutory spending limit. “So, if you have to pay every state one billion, and you pay 37 states, which is 37 billion naira, including Abuja, did you run foul of the Act or not? So, why can’t somebody say anything?” he asked. The post 2027: APC doesn’t want opposition candidates to campaign anywhere - Galadima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Messi retires with goal, assists as Argentina beat Benin 3-0
items.description: Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday, bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance for the former world champions in Buenos Aires. In a perfectly scripted finale, the 39-year-old widely regarded as the greatest football player in history signed off with his 126th international goal in front of 85,000 supporters as Argentina cruised to a 3-0 victory over Benin. Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring. But the match was a footnote to the occasion itself, which saw Messi savoring the adulation of the Monumental Stadium crowd one last time for an event which had been billed as ‘The Last Tango’. “It was a huge source of pride for me to defend this jersey for more than 20 years,” Messi told fans in a post-match address. “Not coming anymore is going to be deeply painful. I swear I’d like to play for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you.” Messi though said he had no regrets about his decision to retire, citing Argentina’s grueling World Cup campaign, which took place as his late father was seriously ill, as a factor. “Even though I want to be here all my life, I feel that this is the moment. The last World Cup was too much, everything I had to live through,” said Messi. Beforehand, Messi wiped away tears as the bus carrying him and his Argentina team-mates made its way through crowds of wellwishers en route to the stadium. Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box. Shortly before kick off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word “Gracias” (Thank You) above the football superstar’s No.10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval. Messi welled up again as Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana sang the national anthem beside a banner which read — “The Malvinas are Argentine” — the same banner held aloft by players after their 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England. The match was halted in the 10th minute — in tribute to Messi’s famous shirt number — for a minute-long ovation to the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star. He crowned the occasion with a goal from the penalty spot in the 71st minute. ‘Gave it my all’ At the final whistle a drone show lit up the night sky above the stadium, showing Messi’s image and thanking the eight-time Ballon D’Or-winner for his career. Messi’s farewell came two and a half months after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss. “I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote at the time. Before Tuesday’s game, the University of Buenos Aires awarded Messi an honorary doctorate in a ceremony at the Argentine Football Association (AFA) headquarters. Messi, who has in the past spoken of his regret at not studying more, expressed pride at the distinction. “To be able to say that I am an honorary doctor!,” he joked. Outside the Argentina Football Association headquarters, fans unfurled a huge Argentine flag with his image inscribed “The joy of my life.” Former Barcelona team-mate Neymar paid tribute to the departing champion on X. “It’s not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more,” he said. Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated. Messi’s departure comes four years after his greatest triumph in international football, leading Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup to end the country’s 36-year wait for a third title, cementing his status as Diego Maradona’s heir. “I believe Messi gave everything, absolutely everything, so it doesn’t bother me at all that he’s leaving. He has more than earned it, let him enjoy himself, let him rest,” Cecilia Adriano, 52, told AFP. During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina won one World Cup, were runners-up twice (Brazil 2014 and North America 2026) and were also crowned Copa America champions in 2021 and 2024. items.title: Why Nigeria’s digital economy lack strong female flavour
items.description: …How cost of data, smartphones, lack of digital skills exclude women …Just 35% used internet, compared with 52% of men – GSMA report …Only 14.8% of rural females have Internet access – NBS By Juliet Umeh For many Nigerian women, owning a smartphone should be a gateway to opportunity -digital banking, online shopping, e-commerce, remote work, online learning and government services. But for some, the smartphone in their hands remains little more than a device for making and receiving calls. Nigeria’s digital economy is expanding rapidly, yet millions of women are still struggling to cross the gap between owning a phone and being able to use technology meaningfully. The 2025 GSMA Mobile Gender Gap Report found that 91 percent of adult women in Nigeria owned a mobile phone, but only 47 percent owned an internet-enabled phone. Just 35 percent used mobile internet, compared with 52 percent of men. The implication is stark: the challenge is no longer simply connecting women. It is ensuring that they can afford smartphones and data, acquire digital skills, obtain identity documents and confidently use online services. ‘I have a smartphone but don’t know what it can do’ At a business centre in Aba, Abia State, Mrs Abigail Maduka has witnessed the problem repeatedly. She said women with expensive smartphones still come to her shop to perform simple transactions they could handle themselves if they had the skills. “I have many women with big phones who do not even know what their phone is capable of doing aside from receiving calls,” she said. Maduka said some women regularly visit her centre to recharge their electricity: “The truth is that they don’t even have the idea that it is what they can do on their phone to start with. They don’t know they can download the app and do it on their own,” she said. The dependence, she added, is sometimes so severe that women call her at night asking her to recharge their electricity. “Many people are with smartphones but the only thing they know is just to answer calls, that’s all,” Maduka said. Her experience exposes an important distinction: phone ownership is not the same as digital inclusion. ‘Educated illiterate’ Sarah Nwokeoma, not her real name, a senior staff member of the Secondary Education Management Board, Aba Zonal office, said the problem is particularly noticeable among older women working in rural schools. She described some as “educated illiterate” – women who have formal education but lack the digital skills required in today’s workplace. Nwokeoma recalled a female principal of a rural secondary technical school who struggles with basic digital tasks. “She does not even know her right from her left. She is still living in the past. They have been cheated all the time,” she said. According to her, the woman sometimes depends on others to perform tasks she should handle herself. “Even what they are supposed to do on their own, people will charge them to do it for them and junior staff will just be insulting them because they don’t know what they are expected to do,” she said. Some women, she added, travel from rural communities to cities simply because they cannot access information sent digitally. “There are some things they may be expected to do with their phone but because they are not internet savvy, they will even enter a bus from the village school where they are and come to the city to receive information already passed on a platform or in the mail,” she said. The problem, therefore, is not always literacy. It can be digital confidence and practical skills. The cost of staying connected Mrs Bukola Olawale, secretary of women fellowship in a Methodist Church in Nigeria, said financial limitations prevent some women from even owning smartphones. “A lot of our members don’t have an Android phone and when I send a message on the platform, I normally assume that everybody is on the same page,” she said. She has had to send important information by SMS to women who cannot access the digital platform. “However, it is not illiteracy that is the cause but lack of financial power,” Olawale explained. Even women who own smartphones can struggle with data costs. “Most times, some of them do say that they are always offline because they can’t afford data,” she added. The experience mirrors findings from the World Bank and GSMA, which identify affordability and digital skills among major barriers to women’s internet use. GSMA’s 2025 report also found that women in low- and middle-income countries were 14 percent less likely than men to use mobile internet. Rural women face a double disadvantage NBS data further show how geography compounds the problem. The National Bureau of Statistics’ General Household Survey Panel Wave 5, conducted in 2023/24, found mobile-phone access of 66.0 percent for males and 66.8 percent for females, showing virtually no national gender difference in phone access. Internet access, however, was much lower: 21.6 percent for males and 21.1 percent for females. The urban-rural gap was considerably wider. Internet access was 38.7 percent for urban males and 37.8 percent for urban females, compared with only 15.5 percent for rural males and 14.8 percent for rural females. This means a rural woman can face several barriers simultaneously such as poor connectivity, inadequate electricity, expensive smartphones, data costs and limited access to digital training. Nigeria’s data boom — but who is benefiting? Nigeria’s growing appetite for mobile data shows how deeply the internet has become embedded in everyday life. But national growth can conceal unequal participation. While digitally connected Nigerians use the internet to trade, work remotely, learn, make payments and access services, women who cannot afford regular data may remain offline or depend on intermediaries. That dependence has economic consequences. For a trader, it can mean losing customers who shop online. For a teacher, it can mean missing an official instruction sent through a digital platform. For a small business owner, it can mean losing access to digital payments or online markets. For an unemployed woman, it can mean missing a remote-work opportunity. Financial inclusion is also at stake The digital divide is closely linked to financial inclusion. EFInA’s 2023 Access to Financial Services survey found that financial inclusion in Nigeria rose to 74 percent, from 68 percent in 2020, while formal financial inclusion reached 64 percent. Yet women continue to experience significant disparities. EFInA’s Women’s Economic Empowerment analysis found persistent gender disparities in financial inclusion and highlighted women’s continued reliance on informal financial services. The organisation has warned that digital financial services can fail to close the gap if products are not deliberately designed around the realities of excluded women. This is important because digital finance increasingly requires a smartphone, data, identity verification and the confidence to navigate applications. A woman lacking any of these can remain financially excluded even when a digital service is technically available to her. Identity creates another barrier Nigeria’s digital economy is also becoming increasingly identity-dependent. Banking, telecommunications and government services increasingly require identity verification through systems such as the National Identification Number and Bank Verification Number. For women who lack documentation or struggle to reconcile identity records, these requirements can become another hurdle. Digital identity is important for security and inclusion, but its benefits will only be realised if women can obtain and use their identities without depending on intermediaries. Starting with girls Stakeholders say closing today’s digital gender gap must also begin with preparing girls for tomorrow’s economy. At the 13th Girls in ICT Day celebration in Lagos, Convener and CEO of eBusiness Life Communication Limited, Mrs Ufuoma Emuophedaro, urged girls not merely to consume technology but to create it. “Do girls use technology? Yes! But that is not all we want. Apart from using, we want them to create technology,” she said. Head, Cybersecurity and Compliance Advisory, Digital Encode, Bisola Oladejo, identified limited STEM education, inadequate access to internet and ICT gadgets, gender bias, low funding and cyberbullying among factors limiting girls’ participation in ICT. She called for deliberate government initiatives and stronger partnerships with NGOs and the private sector. The message is supported by global evidence. GSMA says affordability, digital skills and safety remain major barriers to women’s meaningful mobile-internet use. Beyond owning a smartphone For Atiku Ibrahim from Zamfara State, the digital divide is painfully personal. His mother does not own a smartphone because she cannot afford one. “If I want to reach her and speak with her, I call my sister,” he said. “Most women in my place don’t have smartphones. Most of them can’t afford it and when they buy for them, they’ll not be able to operate it,” he added. For women like his mother, digital exclusion determines who they can communicate with, what information they receive and whether they can access services independently. The solution, therefore, cannot be reduced to putting smartphones into women’s hands. Nigeria needs affordable devices, cheaper and reliable connectivity, practical digital-skills training, accessible identity systems, safer online spaces and financial services designed around women’s realities. The real measure of digital transformation should not be how many Nigerians own phones. It should be how many women can use those phones to earn, save, borrow, trade, learn, access government services and make decisions independently. Until that happens, Nigeria’s digital economy may continue to grow, while millions of women remain locked outside its most valuable opportunities. items.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 7, 2026
items.description: The Nigerian naira weakened against the United States dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, while the local currency strengthened at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The dollar traded at about ₦1,362 in the parallel market, up from ₦1,357 recorded on Tuesday, according to the latest market data. At the official NFEM window, the naira appreciated to ₦1,331.50 per dollar from ₦1,332.90 recorded in the previous session. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the movement represented a ₦1.40 appreciation in the value of the naira at the official market. The latest figures widened the gap between the official and parallel markets to ₦30.50 per dollar, compared with ₦24.10 recorded on Tuesday. The development came as activity in the official foreign exchange market increased sharply. NFEM interbank turnover rose by 334.8 per cent to $313.6 million from $72.12 million in the previous session, according to the latest market data. The parallel market rate, however, may vary depending on location, dealer and transaction size. As of October 7, the dollar therefore sells for approximately ₦1,362 in the parallel market, while the latest NFEM rate stands at ₦1,331.50 per dollar. The movement in both markets continues to reflect changing foreign exchange liquidity and demand as businesses, investors and consumers monitor developments in the naira market. items.title: Nigeria Air Force crashes timeline
items.description: A Nigerian Air Force plane carrying 25 military and civilian passengers crashed in Ondo State on Monday, killing all on board. The accident was one of Nigeria’s worst air disasters in recent years. Read Also: Video: Ondo crash Air Force pilot dies 2 weeks after wedding Here are some major air crashes involving the Nigeria Air Force, which has one of the strongest militaries on the continent. 1980 A Fokker F27 aircraft travelling from Lagos to the neighbouring island nation of Sao Tome crashed in Forcados in southern Delta state on May 26, killing all 30 people aboard. It was carrying a Nigerian delegation comprising government officials, army officers and journalists when it came down. 1992 A Lockheed C-130H Hercules transport plane crashed and killed all 159 passengers aboard in Ejigbo, Lagos, shortly after taking off from Lagos airport on September 26. Most of the passengers were military officers. 1997 A Dornier Do 128 plane used for training crashed and killed all three officials on it about three kilometres from the runway of the Kaduna airport on February 24. 2000 All six people on a Dornier Do 128 plane were killed when it crashed while approaching the runway at the Warri airport in oil-rich Delta state on October 26. 2006 An 18-seater Dornier 228 military transport plane carrying 15 senior army officers and three crew members crashed in Benue State on September 17. Three people survived the crash. 2015 A Dornier 228 plane went out of control shortly after taking off from a military air base in Kaduna and crashed into a house in a military cantonment, killing all the seven aboard. 2019 An attack helicopter providing support for troops fighting a jihadist insurgency in northeastern Nigeria crashed and killed all five people on board on January 2. 2021 On February 21, seven air force officials died when a Beechcraft King Air crashed en route Abuja airport after suffering engine failure on its way to central Niger state, where it was to go on a reconnaissance flight ahead of a mission to free kidnapped schoolgirls, according to the Nigeria Air Force. 2021 A Beechcraft King Air crashed in bad weather in May while trying to land at northern Kaduna state airport. All 11 people on board, including Lieutenant General Ibrahim Attahiru, then commander of the country’s army, died in the crash. Vanguard News The post Nigeria Air Force crashes timeline appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Plane Crash: Victim visited mother on birthday before trip
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — One of the victims of Tuesday’s ill-fated Air Force aircraft that crashed in Igbokoda, Ondo State, Flight Lieutenant M. Akintoye, reportedly visited his mother on Monday to celebrate her birthday before departing for Lagos. Akintoye’s visit to his mother, Professor Emily Akintoye, a staff member of Benson Idahosa University, Benin City, turned out to be their last encounter. A source close to the Air Force also disclosed that the aircraft’s co-pilot, Flight Lieutenant I. S. Bako, got married a few weeks ago. Flags were flown at half-mast at the Air Force military base and the Air Force Military Hospital in Benin City in honour of the victims. Recounting Akintoye’s final visit, a source close to the family said he and other personnel had stopped over in Benin City after attending a programme. “On Monday, which was his mother’s birthday, he rushed home in one of their Air Force vehicles to wish her a happy birthday and inform her that they were on their way to Lagos. A few hours later, news of the disaster broke,” the source said. The source said the tragedy had devastated the family and senior military officers, given the number of personnel involved in the crash. “Everybody is devastated, including senior officers, because of the number of personnel involved in the disaster. His mother is obviously in distress, and it is a bad day to celebrate his birthday. “This is something that would stay with her for life. Whenever it is her birthday, she will remember the tragic death of her son,” the source added. The post Plane Crash: Victim visited mother on birthday before trip appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PM Shehbaz says terrorism in KP ‘must be stopped at any cost’ in meeting with Amir Muqam
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said rising terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa “must be stopped” at any cost. He made the remarks during a meeting with Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). During the meeting, views were also exchanged on matters related to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), the PMO said. “It is our desire that KP should also develop like other parts of the country,” the premier was quoted as saying. “We regard with appreciation the sacrifices of the people of KP against terrorism,” he added. The federal minister also briefed the prime minister on ongoing matters and progress in AJK and GB, the statement said. The prime minister directed that effective measures be continued to ensure the welfare, development and provision of basic facilities for the people of AJK and GB. He said the development of AJK and GB and the prosperity of their people were among the government’s priorities, according to the statement. PM Shehbaz on Tuesday expressed dismay over the “unfortunate events” in AJK in recent months, adding that, however, the law took its course. The government and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 refugee seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly, which resulted in violence-marred protests across the region. KP has also been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) On Tuesday Security forces killed five terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan. On October 2, security forces killed seven terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan.

items.title: Israelis mark three years since Hamas attack that set off Gaza assault
items.description: By Steven Scheer JERUSALEM, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Israelis will on Wednesday mark three years since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, triggering a military assault that destroyed much of Gaza, where conditions remain dire despite a year-old ceasefire that is meant to halt the war for good. The attacks, during which militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages to Gaza, marked the deadliest day in Israel's history. Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza, health authorities there say.

items.title: Commune de PÔ : Un arbre tombe sur un usager de la route et le blesse .
items.description: Un grave incident s’est produit ce mardi 6 octobre 2026, aux environs de 16 heures, au niveau du feu tricolore situé à proximité du Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Pô. Alors qu’une pluie s’abattait sur la ville, un tronc d’arbre s’est brusquement détaché et est tombé sur un usager qui circulait à moto. L’homme, grièvement blessé, s’est retrouvé coincé sous les branches. Alerté, le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Pô s’est rendu sur les lieux. Une tronçonneuse a été utilisée pour dégager la victime, qui a ensuite été évacuée au CMA de Pô par le PDS. Selon les premières informations, sa vie ne serait pas en danger. La victime est un agent de la Direction provinciale de la Culture du Nahouri. Cet incident relance une fois de plus la question de l’état de certains arbres anciens présents dans la ville de Pô, dont certains présentent un risque pour les usagers et les riverains. Il y a quelques semaines, un autre arbre était déjà tombé au niveau de la Maison de la femme, blessant plusieurs personnes qui s’y trouvaient. Face à la répétition de ces incidents, la question de la sécurisation des espaces publics et de l’identification des arbres présentant un danger se pose avec acuité. Camarade Président de la délégation spéciale, il est peut-être temps d’agir afin de prévenir d’autres accidents. Source : les infos du Sud L’article Commune de PÔ : Un arbre tombe sur un usager de la route et le blesse . est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Security forces kill 13 terrorists in North Waziristan IBO: state media
items.description: Security forces eliminated thirteen terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources. Pakistan TV said security forces “killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan, as operations against militant groups continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision”. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. A day earlier, in another North Waziristan IBO, security forces killed five terrorists, state media said. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). On October 2, security forces killed seven terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan. On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in KP’s Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Sept 28, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan. On Sept 26, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier that month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

items.title: Scandale au Cameroun : Un homme surprend sa femme enceinte de sept mois et son amant dans un motel
items.description: Une affaire d’infidélité présumée a provoqué un vif émoi et nécessité l'intervention de la police le samedi 3 octobre au quartier Banguè, dans l’arrondissement de Douala V. Alerté par son propre frère qui se trouvait par hasard sur les lieux, un ingénieur de 40 ans a surpris son épouse — une coiffeuse de 33 ans enceinte de sept mois — en galante compagnie dans une chambre de motel. Pris de panique à l'arrivée du mari, l'amant s'est grièvement blessé à la tête en tentant de s'échapper par la fenêtre. Ce qui devait être une simple journée de travail s'est transformé en un véritable vaudeville dramatique le samedi 3 octobre dans le quartier Banguè, situé dans l'arrondissement de Douala V. Au cœur de cette affaire : un couple marié, deux enfants de six et quatre ans, et une grossesse de sept mois qui n'a pas empêché une escapade extraconjugale mouvementée. Tout commence en journée par un échange téléphonique ordinaire entre les époux. Sarah T., 33 ans, propriétaire d'un salon de coiffure à Bonamoussadi, informe son conjoint, Laurent Blaise T., ingénieur de 40 ans en service sur la place portuaire, qu'elle se sent fatiguée et compte quitter son travail plus tôt. Invoquant une « envie » de femme enceinte, elle exprime le désir de manger du soya . Soucieux du bien-être de sa compagne, son mari lui transfère immédiatement la somme de 25 000 F CFA par dépôt d'argent mobile, avant de l'informer qu'il rentrera tardivement en raison d'une réunion d'affaires à Akwa. Le scénario bascule en fin d'après-midi, vers 17h30. Le frère cadet de Laurent Blaise T., venu au quartier Banguè près du secteur « Fin goudron » pour un rendez-vous galant personnel dans un motel, aperçoit sa belle-sœur entrer dans l'établissement au bras d'un autre homme. Conscient de la gravité de la situation, le jeune homme tente de joindre son aîné à plusieurs reprises avant de lui laisser un message vocal explicite l'invitant à le rejoindre en urgence en moto. S'excusant auprès de ses partenaires d'affaires à Akwa, Laurent Blaise T. laisse son véhicule sur place pour éviter les embouteillages et se rend immédiatement à Banguè à moto. Pensant initialement que son épouse a été victime d'une agression, il découvre avec stupeur son frère posté devant l'entrée du motel. Se glissant dans les couloirs à l'insu du réceptionniste, le mari repère la chambre indiquée et en défonce la porte avec la furie d'un ouragan. À l'intérieur, Sarah T. et son amant, un prénommé Ferdinand, sont surpris au lit. Tétanisé par la colère du mari, l'amant tente d'échapper à la confrontation en se ruant vers la seule issue visible : une fenêtre. Dans sa précipitation, Ferdinand se cogne violemment la tête contre les rebords de l'ouverture trop étroite, se provoquant un saignement abondant. Bien que grondant de rage, le mari ne commet aucune violence physique envers l'amant. Alerté par le fracas de la porte et le tumulte, le réceptionniste prévient les forces de l'ordre, qui arrivent rapidement sur les lieux. Face aux enquêteurs venus rétablir l'ordre, Sarah T. invoque un malaise. Les deux amants ont été conduits chacun dans une formation sanitaire pour y recevoir des soins, Ferdinand étant placé sous surveillance policière durant sa prise en charge médicale. Déjà père de deux enfants de six et quatre ans, Laurent Blaise T. a d'ores et déjà annoncé son intention d'exiger un test ADN dès la naissance du nourrisson afin de vérifier la paternité de l'enfant. items.title: Mother of four and Jasikan teacher among new Telecel M’ahitti Promo winners
items.description: Since its launch in June this year, the Telecel M’ahitti Promo has brought economic hope to thousands of people across Ghana. More than GH¢2 million has been awarded through one GH¢1 million monthly prize, as well as daily and weekly prizes In the final week of September, Anita Addo, a mother of four, Kumasi-based entrepreneur and Telecel customer of just over a year, received her weekly prize. After the M’ahitti Promo launched, she began receiving SMS messages about it and eventually opted in, although she had little expectation of winning. When she received the call announcing her win, she initially dismissed it. Unsure whether it was genuine, she visited a nearby Telecel office, where the Executive Head confirmed that she was indeed a winner. The GHC 20,000 prize has come at an important time for her family, as the new school year has just begun. Her eldest child recently gained admission to university, and she also needs to pay fees and provide school supplies for her other children. “This is an answer to my prayers. I had no idea how I was going to pay the fees and provide all their other school necessities. I am very grateful to Telecel, and I encourage everyone to participate in its promotions because they are genuine,” she said. In the Oti Region, Leslie Johnson Adams, a Jasikan-based teacher and Telecel customer of about 10 years, could not hide his joy when he received GH¢20,000 in his Telecel Cash wallet. Like many weekly winners, he was initially in disbelief, as he had never won anything of this kind. “It felt as though I was dreaming because I have been praying for funds to install a solar power system in my home on the outskirts of Jasikan. This win is indeed a blessing,” he said. Reflecting on the prize’s impact, Leslie urged Telecel to continue initiatives that provide customers with meaningful financial support. “Telecel should continue running promotions like this because people face real challenges, and gestures such as these go a long way towards helping them,” he added. Executive Head for the Eastern, Oti and Volta Regions, Alex Kwapong, said: “Seeing the Telecel M’ahitti Promo change lives every week brings us immense joy. This is the value we aim to deliver to our customers through the promotion. We still have two monthly GH¢1 million prizes to award, along with many more weekly and daily prizes.” The two latest wins add to the growing number of customers who have benefited from the promotion since its launch. To date, one customer has won the GH¢1 million monthly prize, with two more monthly winners yet to emerge. More than 30 weekly winners have each received GH¢20,000. More than 6,000 customers have each won the daily GH¢100 prize. With about four weeks remaining, customers can still participate at no cost by opting in through the Telecel Play app or by dialling *500#. The promotion is regulated by the National Lottery Authority (NLA) on the Caritas platform.

items.title: International Youth Shakers Conclave 2026 set to bring global young leaders to London
items.description: The International Youth Shakers Conclave & Awards 2026 is set to bring together young professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives, ministers and changemakers from across the world for a major youth-focused gathering in London. The event is scheduled for Saturday, November 15, 2026, at the Praise Dome, Aldersbrook Baptist Church, 2 Dover Road, Wanstead, London. The gathering is being hosted by the Global Youth Network of The World Conference of Mayors, International Praise Centre (IPC London) and Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations (RAIN). This year’s event is being convened by David Raphaelle Kwaku Antwi, popularly known as Author Ralph Antwi, Founding President of Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations, and Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong of IPC London. The organisers say the initiative is focused on raising a generation of young people equipped to make an impact in their communities and beyond. The theme for this year’s Conclave is “Celebrating Youth People Leading Change and Older People Changing Youth.” The event is expected to attract participants from the United Kingdom, Ghana, Nigeria, Europe, North America and other parts of the world. It will feature keynote sessions, leadership discussions, business networking and other engagements focused on youth development and leadership. Youth Shakers Awards A major highlight of the event will be the Youth Shakers Awards, which will recognise young people making an impact across various fields. The awards will celebrate individuals in areas including ministry, business, education, creative arts, technology, community development and leadership. Speaking ahead of the event, convener Author Ralph Antwi said the initiative was designed to go beyond a one-day programme. “We are not just organising a programme; we are nurturing a movement. We believe in this generation. We have seen what happens when you give a young person faith, a platform and a push — they will shake their world. On November 15th in London, history will be made.” Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong said IPC London was pleased to host the gathering of young people and leaders. “IPC London is honoured to open our doors for this global harvest of young giants. London will be a meeting point for purpose, power and possibilities.” The organisers are inviting young people, professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives and other stakeholders to participate in the event. Event Details Event: International Youth Shakers Conclave & Awards 2026 Date: Saturday, November 15, 2026 Venue: Praise Dome, Aldersbrook Baptist Church, 2 Dover Road, Wanstead, London E12 5EA Conveners: David Raphaelle Kwaku Antwi (Author Ralph Antwi) and Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong Host: International Praise Centre in collaboration with Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations

items.title: Gov’t is committed to addressing teachers’ conditions of service, deprived-area allowance – Education Minister
items.description: Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister of Education, on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to resolving outstanding grievances of teachers, including the payment of promotion arrears and the implementation of the deprived-area allowance. He noted that the Government had initiated processes to address the concerns raised by the teacher unions and improve conditions of service in the education sector. Mr Iddrisu gave the assurance at this year’s Ghana Teacher Prize to commemorate teachers and recognise their contribution to national development. He said the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, with the support of the Ministry of Finance, would engage the teacher unions on their expired collective agreement on conditions of service. He said the Government was committed to fulfilling its manifesto pledge on the payment of a deprived-area allowance to teachers serving in underserved communities. The education minister said discussions were ongoing to validate the data on deprived schools and communities to determine who qualified for the allowance and ensure its effective implementation. “We are sure that there is absolute government commitment to the manifesto pledge on the deprived-area allowance. What we need to do is validate the data, then we can begin the process of implementation,” he said. The Minister said the Government had also committed resources to clear outstanding promotion arrears to teachers. The Ghana Education Service, in collaboration with the relevant institutions, had been tasked to validate the records of teachers who had been promoted but were yet to receive their new salary grades and associated arrears, he explained. Mr Iddrisu said the exercise was expected to cover more than 51,000 teachers, adding that the Government would make the necessary financial arrangements to settle the outstanding arrears. The minister commended teachers for their contribution to the development of the country, describing them as the “architects” of every profession. “We all owe it to the teacher. No profession is possible without the teacher, and for that reason, we recognise you and celebrate you,” he said. The education minister disclosed that President John Dramani Mahama had approved a new integrated model for basic education infrastructure. He said the model would bring key basic education facilities together within a single development to ensure more efficient use of resources and improve access to quality education. Under the proposed model, a basic school complex would include kindergarten, primary and junior high school facilities, as well as laboratories, libraries and information technology facilities. He said the Government had directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies to ensure that new basic education infrastructure reflected the integrated model. Mr Iddrisu said the initiative was part of efforts to address infrastructure deficits in the education sector, particularly the large number of schools without electricity. He cited data indicating that about 10,750 schools across the country were still without electricity, affecting approximately three million children. He said the government would work to mobilise resources through the appropriate funding mechanisms to reduce the infrastructure deficit and ensure that pupils and teachers had access to better learning environments. Mr Prosper Tachie, the President, Ghana National Association of Teachers,called for the empowerment of teachers in three key areas; legal authority, professional confidence, and economic security. He said teachers needed the legal authority to perform their professional responsibilities, including maintaining discipline in schools, while also having the confidence and financial security to meet their basic needs. He cited a World Bank report on the global teaching profession published in May 2026, which emphasised the importance of teachers to the skills development of the global workforce.

items.title: GoldBod’s structure encouraging galamsey – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has raised concerns about the structure of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), arguing that the current system does not sufficiently distinguish legally mined gold from gold linked to illegal mining. Speaking during an engagement with the Christian Council, Mr Afenyo-Markin questioned the regulatory framework governing GoldBod and gold aggregators, warning that the absence of clear distinctions could create incentives for galamsey. “The way GoldBod has been structured, it is rather encouraging the illegal mining activities we have in our country. Because you see, currently GoldBod does not have a regulation that draws a distinction between regularly mined gold and galamsey gold. So it is like whatever the aggregators bring, we will buy. But are there some regulations to guide aggregators? Now, everybody is mining. Galamsey has gotten out of hand,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin also warned about the environmental consequences of illegal mining, particularly the threat to Ghana’s forests and water bodies. He singled out the Atewa Forest as an area that could face further degradation if stronger measures are not taken. “If we are not careful, Atewa forest will not be there for us again,” he cautioned. The Minority Leader further raised concerns about the increasing cost of treating contaminated water, saying the scale of pollution was affecting the ability of some water treatment plants to operate effectively. “I once chaired the Ghana Water Limited Board. The report coming from Ghana Water is that not only is it becoming more expensive to treat the water, but the extent of contamination of our water bodies is such that some treatment plant cannot even function,” he said. He called for stronger oversight of gold trading and aggregation to ensure that efforts to formalise the gold sector do not undermine the broader fight against illegal mining.

items.title: Tullow starts selling Jubilee, TEN crude to Ghanaian refineries
items.description: Tullow Oil has begun selling crude from its Jubilee, Tweneboa, Enyenra, and Ntomme (TEN) fields to refineries in Ghana, in a move aimed at supporting domestic refining. The company says the first cargo was sold earlier this year to Sentuo Oil Refinery. Tullow Chief Financial Officer Richard Miller disclosed this during a virtual meeting with investors on the company’s half-year results. He was responding to a question on efforts to encourage more Jubilee crude to be refined locally. Mr Miller described the development as a significant achievement for Ghana’s oil sector. “This is a fantastic achievement looking at what has happened in Ghana’s oil sector over the years,” he said. He explained that the sale was conducted purely on a commercial basis. Mr Miller also said mechanisms had been put in place to ensure a favourable refinancing package to support the initiative. He praised the government for initiatives to improve refinery operations in Ghana, describing the development as “a fantastic achievement.” Mr Miller also highlighted the growing role of Sentuo Oil Refinery in Ghana’s crude market. “Sentuo Oil has become one of the prolific buyers of crude not only from Tullow Oil alone but also from other partners on Ghana’s oil fields,” he said. The development comes as Tullow expects to increase its crude liftings for the year. Tullow Targets 14 Cargoes in 2026 In its half-year results, Tullow said it expects to lift 14 cargoes in 2026. Eleven of the cargoes are expected from the Jubilee field, while three will come from the TEN fields. The revised outlook represents an increase of two Jubilee cargoes compared with the company’s initial guidance issued in November 2025. Tullow delivered six cargoes during the first half of the year and plans to lift a further eight cargoes in the second half. The company also expects the measures currently being implemented to improve its performance and support a stronger turnaround by the end of the year. The sale of Jubilee crude to a local refinery provides another commercial channel for Ghana’s domestically produced crude and strengthens the link between upstream production and domestic refining.

items.title: Local Government Service authorises rationalisation, redistribution of staff
items.description: The Local Government Service (LGS) has authorised the rationalisation and redistribution of staff across Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to address disparities in staffing levels and improve efficiency in local government administration. Professor Lord Kwaku Mensah, the Head, Local Government Service, who announced this, said the exercise would move staff from overstaffed MMDAs to areas where there were shortages based on staffing norms, competencies, positions and operational needs. He said the exercise was not intended as a form of punishment but to ensure that the right number of personnel with the required competencies were available at the right places to improve service delivery. Professor Mensah announced this when he engaged staff of the Northern Regional Coordinating Council (NRCC) in Tamale on Monday as part of his working visit to the region. He also visited Savelugu, Sagnarigu and the Tamale Assemblies to engage their staff members, obtain first-hand information on their operations, working conditions, achievements and challenges. The engagement at the NRCC was attended by staff from various Ministries, Departments and Agencies, who took turns to share operational challenges and concerns with the Head of the Service. Prof Mensah said the decision to rationalise staffing followed observations of uneven distribution of personnel across MMDAs where some had more staff than required while others lacked the minimum number of officers needed to operate effectively. He cited Tamale Metropolitan Assembly as an example saying it could have about 17 budget officers under the staffing norms while some districts might not have the minimum four administrative officers required. He said Regional Coordinating Directors had consequently been instructed to begin the process of moving officers to areas where their services were needed in accordance with the rules and conditions of service. He said officers, who had stayed in particular locations beyond the required period, could also be posted to other areas including headquarters or outside their current regions as part of the workforce planning and rationalisation process. He urged staff to comply with official postings warning that failure to do so could attract consequences under the Service’s rules and scheme of service. Professor Mensah said decisions on postings, promotions, deployment and resource allocation would be guided by reliable personnel and operational data to reduce perceptions of bias, favouritism and nepotism. He said the Service was developing web-based Local Government Service Operational Tools to digitise human resource and operational processes and provide real-time data to support management decisions. He said the accuracy of information supplied by Human Resource units at the regional and assembly levels would therefore be critical to the success of the system. He said the Service was also focused on professionalising its workforce by promoting discipline, ethical conduct, punctuality and adherence to institutional procedures. Professor Mensah expressed concern about lateness and absenteeism, saying observations from his recent visits to three MMDAs showed staff attendance levels of about 30, 45 and 50 per cent respectively at the times he visited. He urged Coordinating Directors and Heads of Department to strengthen supervision and ensure that staff were not merely physically present at work but were productive and responsive to their assigned responsibilities. He cautioned staff against disregarding reporting lines and supervisory authority and said weak departmental leadership and poor adherence to institutional hierarchy could undermine coordination and service delivery. He reminded staff to observe professional dress codes and desist from reporting to work in inappropriate attire. Professor Mensah also raised concerns about alleged attempts by some Human Resource officers to alter dates of birth in official records to extend the working lives of staff. He said the integrity of personnel records was essential for effective human resource planning and warned that officers involved in altering official records could face administrative, disciplinary and legal consequences. He urged staff to desist from active frontline partisan politics, saying public servants were required to maintain political neutrality and ensure continuity in public administration regardless of changes in government. On staff development, he said the Service was targeting a minimum of 40 hours of training for every staff member annually, adding that the Service was considering the use of a Learning Management System to facilitate online training, self-tutoring and assessments while reducing the cost of continuous professional development. He said training opportunities, including short courses, conferences and job-class association programmes should be better structured to improve staff competencies. He said management would also introduce a more coordinated calendar for job-class association conferences to reduce the pressure such programmes placed on the resources of RCCs and MMDAs. Mr Ali Adolf John, Northern Regional Minister appealed to the Management of the Service to consult the RCCs before transferring officers, whose services were considered valuable to the region. Professor Mensah said he had no difficulty working with officers currently serving in the region and wanted effective public servants to be retained where their experience and understanding of the local government system could contribute to development. He said officers were public servants and should work with the government of the day irrespective of their political backgrounds while also emphasising need for discipline and effective performance. He commended Professor Mensah for undertaking the tour of the region to familiarise himself with the actual working conditions of officers and the operations of the various MMDAs

items.title: PURC assures consumers of working to ensure quality services in Northern Region
items.description: The Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) has assured consumers in the Northern Region that it is working to ensure that they receive appropriate quality of service and tariffs that are necessary to sustain the utility system. Dr Shafic Suleman, the Executive Secretary, PURC, who gave the assurance, said: “Our core mandate is to protect the interests of the Ghanaian consumer, and we are doing just that.” Dr Suleman gave the assurance in an interview with journalists in Tamale after leading a delegation from the PURC to visit the utility service providers in the region. The visit formed part of the PURC’s efforts to assess the operations of the utility service providers and ascertain how investments made following the latest tariff review were addressing the concerns of consumers. The visit took the delegation to Nawuni and Dalun in the Kumbungu District to assess the state of infrastructure of the Ghana Water Limited and its operations as well as held a meeting with Management of Northern Electricity Distribution Company Limited in Tamale on its operations. Dr Suleman assured consumers that protecting their interests remained a core mandate of the PURC while also ensuring that the interests of investors in the utility sector were protected. He said following the approval of a nine per cent tariff adjustment at the beginning of this year, the utility service providers were expected to undertake investments to improve service delivery to consumers. He said in view of that the PURC was closely monitoring the utility service providers to ensure that tariff-supported investments translated into improved quality and reliability of services to consumers. He emphasised that “We are monitoring some of the investments to see whether or not the utilities are taking those investments to the benefit of the Ghanaian consumer.” Dr Suleman said reliable water supply was one of the major challenges facing consumers, especially during the dry season in the region adding while water production had increased in the region, other projects would soon come onboard to improve the situation.

items.title: Ghana develops US$4.28bn water financing framework
items.description: Ghana is developing a US$4.28 billion financing framework to address critical water-sector investment needs and strengthen climate resilience. The framework, being developed under the National Water Investment Programme, is intended to guide priority investments, mobilise public and private financing and improve water resources management. ‎Mr Edwin Kissi Afosah-Anim, Deputy Director of the Water Management Directorate of the Water Resources Commission (WRC) and Ghana’s Focal Point for the Green Climate Fund (GCF), disclosed this at a stakeholders’ validation workshop in Accra. He said the programme would strengthen the country’s capacity to identify and prioritise critical water investments, mobilise financing and establish a clear pathway for implementation. Mr Afosah-Anim said it would also help align water-sector investments with national climate and development priorities. He said the validation workshop provided an opportunity for stakeholders to review the proposed investment plan, financing strategy and implementation arrangements. Mr Afosah-Anim said inputs from participating institutions would help identify gaps, address emerging issues and improve the final programme. He urged stakeholders to actively participate in the process. ‎”The quality of the final programme will depend greatly on the depth of our participation and the value of the inputs we provide,” he said. Mr Afosah-Animsaid countries in the Global South, including Ghana, faced significant challenges in mobilising financing for water and climate-related investments because of high debt burdens, limited fiscal space and complex donor engagement processes. ‎Sector estimates indicate that Ghana requires about US$1.7 billion annually to achieve universal access to water and meet sustainability targets by 2030. Mr Afosah-Anim said financing for water and climate initiatives should extend beyond government resources, with stronger public-private collaboration needed to bridge funding gaps. “We are also looking at the private sector to support what we do at the Water Resources Commission. “We have increasingly engaged civil society organisations and non-governmental organisations to undertake certain activities where public resources may be limited. They provide funding while we contribute technical expertise, enabling us to combine efforts to address some of these financing challenges,” he said. Ms Eunice Inkum, Principal Economic Officer at the Ministry of Finance and Green Climate Fund representative, said the US$4.28 billion requirement could not be financed by the government alone. She urged stakeholders to use public resources more effectively to leverage additional financing through stronger engagement with development partners and climate finance institutions. Ms Inkum also advocated blended finance and, where appropriate, increased private-sector participation. ‎She said the validation process would help strengthen Ghana’s project pipeline and ensure that proposed investments were aligned with national development priorities and realistic within the country’s financing environment. ‎The National Water Investment Programme is expected to provide a framework for identifying priority investments, mobilising financing and strengthening implementation to improve water security and climate resilience.

items.title: Christian Council calls for protection of mission schools’ religious identity‎
items.description: The Christian Council of Ghana (CCG) has called for reforms to protect students’ religious freedoms while preserving the legitimate ethos of mission-founded schools.‎ ‎The Council said the reforms should safeguard freedom of thought, conscience, belief and religion without undermining the right to education or the identity of mission-founded institutions.‎ ‎The Most Rev. Dr Paul Kwabena Boafo, Immediate Past Presiding Bishop of The Methodist Church Ghana, made the call at an Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) forum in Accra on proposals in the Constitutional Review Committee’s report. ‎He said Article 25 of the 1992 Constitution guaranteed the right to education, while Article 21 guaranteed freedom of thought, conscience, belief and religion.‎ ‎The Most Rev. Dr Boafo said mission schools had contributed significantly to Ghana’s educational development, particularly in promoting literacy and civic formation, but as publicly funded institutions, they were required to uphold constitutional guarantees.‎ ‎He said the CCG welcomed the CRC’s proposal to strengthen protection against religious discrimination in admission, boarding, discipline, student leadership and participation in school activities.‎ ‎The Most Rev. Dr Boafo said educational institutions should, however, be allowed to maintain their distinctive religious character and practices, provided these did not infringe students’ constitutional rights. ‎He said the Council supported education as a national development priority and urged clear constitutional rules governing the relationship between religious freedom and education.

Mahama holds discussions with India’s External Affairs Minister
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has held discussions with India’s Minister for External Affairs, Dr Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, on strengthening Ghana-India relations, with a focus on trade, investment, rail development, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. A statement issued by Ghana’s Presidency said the meeting also explored opportunities to deepen economic cooperation and advance a more equitable global order that rejects unilateralism and the abuse of nations. President Mahama highlighted growing trade between Ghana and India, noting that Ghana’s exports to India have risen from about $3 billion to nearly $7 billion, while Ghana continues to benefit from Indian agricultural machinery, automobiles, and buses. On pharmaceuticals, President Mahama reaffirmed Ghana’s openness to partnerships that support local drug and vaccine production, in line with the health sovereignty objectives of the Accra Reset. Dr Jaishankar conveyed warm greetings from Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu, and said both leaders expect the comprehensive partnership between Ghana and India to be given greater concrete shape through new avenues of cooperation. The meeting forms part of ongoing efforts to deepen the longstanding Ghana-India partnership, including cooperation in infrastructure, ICT, health, trade, and investment.

items.title: Even when you cough, they come after you — Abanga accuses Mahama govt of criminalising free speech
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser Abanga Fuseini Yakubu has accused the government of creating an environment in which citizens are increasingly afraid to criticise those in power. He alleged that comments made on social media are attracting the attention of state security agencies, arguing that the development is contributing to growing frustration among young people. Mr Abanga claimed that the government’s approach to critics amounted to a restriction of free expression and warned that such actions could deepen public dissatisfaction with the administration. “This government whatever you do, they will come after you. Even on social media, there are certain words if you dare use them, tomorrow EOCO will come and pick you up,” he said. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express programme on Tuesday, October 6, Mr Abanga said the situation had reached a point where people could no longer freely express their views about government without fear of repercussions. “Free speech is now criminalised to the point that one cannot even criticise the government,” he stated. He cited the arrest of a woman allegedly linked to a social media account as an example of what he described as the government’s intolerance of criticism. He maintained that young people were particularly unhappy about what he sees as the shrinking space for dissent. Mr Abanga urged the government to reconsider its approach to criticism and allow citizens to express their views without fear of intimidation or arrest.

items.title: Mondial 2026 : La FIFA a comploté contre le Burkina Faso pour favoriser la qualification de la République démocratique du Congo
items.description: Alors que le Burkina Faso croyait son rêve mondialiste définitivement éteint sur le terrain, des documents internes de la FIFA consultés par le journal Le Monde révèlent une réalité explosive : les juristes de l'instance internationale avaient conclu que le gardien congolais Lionel Mpasi n'était pas éligible lors des éliminatoires du Mondial 2026. Selon l'analyse juridique même de la FIFA, l'application stricte des règles disciplinaires aurait dû disqualifier la République démocratique du Congo et attribuer au Burkina Faso la place en barrage africain. Pourtant, aucune sanction n'a été prononcée, laissant aux Étalons un sentiment amer d'injustice sportive. Pour le public burkinabè et les supporters des Étalons, la campagne des éliminatoires du Mondial 2026 s'était achevée sur une immense amertume sportive. Mais les récentes révélations publiées au début du mois d'octobre 2026 par le quotidien Le Monde apportent un éclairage saisissant et scandaleux sur les coulisses administratives du football mondial. Les services juridiques de la FIFA avaient en effet déterminé, dès le mois de mars 2026, que le gardien de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Lionel Mpasi, n'avait pas la qualité légale pour disputer les rencontres éliminatoires. Né en France et ancien international français chez les jeunes — comptant au moins cinq sélections et une participation à la Coupe du monde U17 en 2011 —, Lionel Mpasi devait impérativement finaliser une procédure de changement d'association auprès de la FIFA pour porter le maillot congolais. Bien que la Fédération congolaise de football (FECOFA) ait entamé les démarches en 2021, la procédure n'a jamais été formellement achevée. Malgré cela, le portier a étrenné sa première sélection le 1ᵉʳ février 2022 et a gardé les cages congolaises lors des matchs décisifs des éliminatoires, notamment lors du barrage contre le Nigeria et du barrage intercontinental face à la Jamaïque. Pour le Burkina Faso, les conséquences de cette irrégularité administrative sont monumentales. L'article 19 du Code disciplinaire de la FIFA stipule clairement qu'un match disputé avec un joueur inéligible entraîne la perte du match par forfait et une amende. Dans leurs simulations internes, les juristes de l'instance faîtière ont estimé que l'annulation des résultats de la RDC pour cause d'inéligibilité aurait « perturbé » le tableau africain, propulsant directement le Burkina Faso à la place de la RDC pour disputer le barrage africain. Si ce barrage n'assurait pas une qualification automatique au Mondial — les Étalons devant encore franchir l'obstacle du barrage africain puis du barrage intercontinental —, il leur rouvrait légitimement les portes de la compétition. Or, la FIFA a choisi de ne prononcer aucune sanction sportive contre la sélection congolaise. Cette passivité est d'autant plus révoltante pour le football burkinabè qu'un précédent strict avait été établi quelques mois plus tôt. En septembre 2025, la Fédération sud-africaine avait été immédiatement sanctionnée pour avoir aligné un joueur inéligible, Teboho Mokoena, contre le Lesotho : défaite par forfait (3-0) et 10 000 francs suisses d'amende. Dans le cas de la RDC, bien que la FIFA ait identifié la faute d'office et que ses juristes aient préconisé des sanctions financières, des suspensions ou un retrait de points sur la campagne 2030, aucune mesure n'a été appliquée pour les éliminatoires du Mondial 2026. Même si la réclamation déposée le 28 novembre 2025 par le Nigeria avait été déclarée irrecevable en mars 2026 pour des raisons formelles et de délai, le règlement offrait à la FIFA la possibilité d'une auto-saisine disciplinaire. Des documents indiquent que le président de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, ainsi que le secrétaire général, ont été informés des éléments sensibles du dossier. Les liens professionnels entre le patron du football mondial et Véron Mosengo-Omba, ancien secrétaire général de la CAF devenu président de la FECOFA en mai 2026, alimentent désormais les interrogations. Même si la FIFA rejette catégoriquement toute idée d'intervention politique en affirmant l'autonomie et l'indépendance de ses organes juridictionnels, le préjudice moral et sportif subi par le Burkina Faso demeure entier. Les Étalons ont été privés d'une opportunité majeure que l'application stricte du droit sportif devait leur accorder. Alors que la RDC conserve officiellement sa qualification, le Burkina Faso attend toujours d'avoir des explications claires sur les raisons pour lesquelles la FIFA a préféré ignorer les recommandations de ses propres juristes au détriment de l'équité sportive. L’article Mondial 2026 : La FIFA a comploté contre le Burkina Faso pour favoriser la qualification de la République démocratique du Congo est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Another crisis creeps up at Pims
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) is on the verge of another crisis as supplies of free medicines for inpatients and other items might be discontinued due to procurement issues. The situation has become worse as not a single tender has been signed during the last six weeks, a senior officer said. However Executive Director (ED) Pims Prof Dr Tanwir Khaliq, who took charge of the post on Tuesday, said he had taken up the issue and would show zero tolerance when it came to providing facilities to patients. A senior doctor of the hospital, requesting anonymity, said issues of procurement of different supply items were increasing. Free medicine supply to inpatients likely to be discontinued any time “In Pims medicines and injectables are given free of cost to all indoor patients and for that continuous supply of medicines has to be ensured. However tenders could not be approved during the last six months due to which supplies have been stopped and the available stocks are rapidly depleting,” he said. It is worth mentioning here that after the fire incident at Pims, in which 14 newborn babies had died on August 26 and later the 15th baby also passed away, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice and suspended as many as eight officers. The additional charge of ED was given to head of the National Institute of Health (NIH), Dr Mohammad Salman. On Oct 5 even Dr Salman was removed and the additional charge of the post was given to Prof Dr Tanwir Khaliq, who is vice chancellor of Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University (SZABMU), Islamabad. A senior doctor of the hospital, requesting anonymity, said files of tender were piling up as they were not being signed. “Similarly most members of the purchase committee have some other jobs to do as heads of departments, therefore they take least interest. Absence of an ED had further aggravated the situation. So I can say that a new crisis is in the making and suggested that the new management focus on the purchases of medicines,” the doctor said. An officer who is in the finance department, wishing not to be named, said there were some reasons behind the emerging crisis. “It has to be understood that the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) only accepted authorised signatures and whenever officers were changed it took a fortnight to authorise new signatures,” he said. When asked that the signature of director finance should be considered as authorised signature, he said documents of approval by the ED were also required for the transactions. “As per my information, some of the stocks are available and we are trying to address the issue at the earliest,” he said. ED Pims Prof Dr Tanwir Khaliq, while talking to Dawn , said he came to know on Tuesday that the tenders had not been approved for the last over one month. “I have directed to expedite the documentary process and informed all departments that there will be zero tolerance on facilities provided to patients. Doctors can suffer but patients cannot be allowed to suffer,” he said, claiming that the issue will be resolved within days. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Mahama Ayariga proposes bank-adopted streets as part of stronger public-private partnership
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has proposed the renaming of selected streets to reflect the spirit of cooperation between Ghana’s banking sector and society. According to the Minister, the initiative is intended to make public spaces symbols of the relationship between financial institutions and the communities they serve. Mr Ayariga made the proposal during an engagement with Heads of Banks, where he shared his vision of building a more cooperative society in which institutions and citizens contribute to national development. He said the proposal goes beyond changing street names, urging banks to adopt selected streets and support their maintenance and beautification. “When a bank adopts a street, it is not merely cleaning a road; it is investing in the dignity of our people and the pride of our communities,” Mr Ayariga said. He stressed that the initiative should not be viewed as an additional burden on banks but as a partnership between the banking sector and government. The Minister assured the bank heads that his Ministry would work with them to establish a fair, transparent and sustainable framework for the initiative.

items.title: NPP will impose $500m bail bond on NDC offenders if we return to power — Abanga
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, has threatened to introduce a $500 million bail bond for alleged offenders associated with the NDC if the party returns to power. He accused the current administration of using state institutions to intimidate young people and critics, claiming that some individuals are being arrested over comments made on social media. Mr Abanga said the situation had heightened frustration among young people, particularly those who believe their freedom to express political opinions is being restricted. “This government whatever you, they will come after you. Even on social media, there are certain words if you dare use them, tomorrow EOCO will come and pick you up, free speech is now criminalised to the point that one cannot even criticise the government,” he said. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express programme on Tuesday, October 6, Mr Abanga contrasted the situation with the Akufo-Addo administration, arguing that critics were able to attack and insult the former President without being arrested. “During President Akufo-Addo’s regime, people could insult him and attack him, but nobody arrested anybody; but today you cough, and they are arresting you,” he stated. He said the NPP would respond differently if it returned to power and warned the government against what he described as its treatment of political opponents. “Whatever they are doing, when we come to power, the bail bond will be $500, and I am promising you as the National Youth Organiser of the NPP, so they should be careful with whatever they are doing,” he said. The comments come amid political disagreements over arrests and prosecutions involving individuals accused of making allegedly offensive or unlawful statements online.

Infraction assimilable à une atteinte à la sûreté de l’État : Gafarou Nignan demande pardon au Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré
items.description: Dans une vidéo diffusée par la Brigade Centrale de Lutte Contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC), l'ingénieur statisticien-démographe et homme politique Gafarou Nignan s'est exprimé au sujet d'une publication controversée diffusée sur sa page Facebook le 27 septembre 2026. Évoquant un écrit rédigé « par mégarde », l'intéressé a formulé des excuses publiques à l'endroit du Président de la Transition, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, et du peuple burkinabè, tout en invitant les usagers des réseaux sociaux à la retenue et au respect des institutions républicaines. Les réseaux sociaux peuvent parfois transformer un écrit impulsif en une affaire judiciaire et sécuritaire d'envergure. L'ingénieur statisticien-démographe Gafarou Nignan , figure également connue du paysage politique national, en a fait l'amère expérience à la suite d'une publication diffusée sur sa page Facebook le 27 septembre 2026 . Dans ce message largement relayé et commenté sur la toile, Gafarou Nignan affirmait que la fin du pouvoir du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré serait « programmée par Allah pour décembre 2026 ». Une assertion aux résonances politiques et sécuritaires immédiates, qui lui a valu d'être entendu par les enquêteurs de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte Contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC) . Confronté à l'impact de ses propos, l'auteur a accepté de s'exprimer publiquement pour clarifier sa démarche et livrer sa version des faits. Devant la caméra de la BCLCC, l'ingénieur a tenu à dégager toute intention malveillante ou projet de déstabilisation derrière son texte. Plaidant l'erreur d'appréciation et la maladresse, il a qualifié son acte de faute personnelle : « Je n'ai aucune intention derrière cette publication […]. J'ai porté atteinte à notre Chef d'État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le faire contre son Chef d'État, tu dois être traité d'apatride. Moi, je l'ai fait par mégarde. » Saisissant cette prise de parole institutionnelle, Gafarou Nignan a présenté ses excuses solennelles au Chef de l'État ainsi qu'à l'ensemble des citoyens burkinabè et aux sympathisants touchés par ses écrits : « Je demande pardon au Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré et à tout le peuple burkinabè. » Au-delà de sa situation personnelle, l'intervention de Gafarou Nignan a pris la forme d'une sensibilisation à destination des internautes sur la portée pénale des publications numériques. Rappelant la gravité de certains propos tenus sur Internet, l'intervenant a souligné que de telles affirmations dépassent le cadre de la simple liberté d'expression et peuvent tomber sous le coup de la loi : « C'est une infraction qu'on pourrait qualifier d'atteinte à la sûreté de l'État. C'est contre la bonne marche de l'État. Donc c'est des choses que je vous demande d'éviter au maximum possible. » Cette affaire vient une nouvelle fois rappeler la vigilance accrue des services de sécurité, notamment la BCLCC et la Police Nationale, quant à l'utilisation responsable des plateformes numériques dans un contexte national où la cohésion et la préservation de l'ordre public demeurent des priorités majeures.
