items.title: L’Iran exerce-t-il toujours un contrôle sur le détroit d’Ormuz ?
items.description: Selon le directeur général de l’entreprise pétrolière Shell, Wael Sawan, les flux pétroliers en provenance du Moyen-Orient s’élèvent désormais à environ 80 % des volumes d’avant le lancement de la guerre israélo-américaine contre l’Iran, le 28 février Mideast Oil Flows Are Near 80 % of Prewar Levels, Shell CEO Says », Bloomberg , 6 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Les données de l’entreprise de Data Intelligence Kpler placent ce niveau à 92 % durant la dernière semaine de septembre. Ces chiffres suggèrent que l'Iran ne parvient plus à réguler le trafic dans le détroit d’Ormuz, comme elle était parvenue à le faire dans les semaines qui avaient suivi le lancement de la guerre. Selon les analystes, la reprise des flux pétroliers est principalement due à trois facteurs : L’escorte des navires commerciaux proposée aux armateurs par l’armée américaine, qui conserve une importante présence dans la région ; L’utilisation de pétroliers-navettes, qui traversent le détroit pour transborder par la suite leurs cargaisons vers d’autres navires dans le golfe d’Oman ; Et le contournement du détroit d’Ormuz via d’autres itinéraires qui contribuent à faire sortir le pétrole de la région, comme l’oléoduc saoudien Est-Ouest, qui donne sur la mer Rouge. Le ministre saoudien de l'Énergie, Abdulaziz ben Salman, a déclaré hier, mardi 6 octobre, que l’oléoduc transportait désormais 5,8 millions de barils par jour, soit légèrement moins que sa capacité maximale de 7 millions de barils par jour. L’infrastructure avait été ciblée le 11 septembre par les Houthis. Le régime iranien, contraint par une pression économique accrue, a multiplié les frappes ces derniers jours afin de tenter de réaffirmer son contrôle sur la voie maritime. Au moins une attaque par jour a été recensée par les United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) depuis vendredi 2 octobre dans le détroit d’Ormuz ou le golfe d’Aden, une zone d’activité houthiste au sud du Yémen. Depuis le 28 septembre, au moins 11 pétroliers ont été attaqués dans le détroit. Si plus de pétrole parvient à sortir du Moyen-Orient, l’instabilité contribue à maintenir le prix du baril de Brent autour des 100 dollars, soit un niveau 50 à 55 % plus élevé par rapport à avant la guerre. De plus, JPMorgan estimait fin septembre que les flux de produits raffinés, comme l’essence et le diesel, restent inférieurs d’environ 40 % par rapport à leur niveau pré-guerre JPMorgan and Goldman See Mideast Oil Flows Near Pre-War Levels », Bloomberg , 30 septembre 2026.'> 2 . L’article L’Iran exerce-t-il toujours un contrôle sur le détroit d’Ormuz ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: TGI de Nouna : Soré Sayouba condamné à 30 ans de prison ferme après avoir tué sa femme et son ami au secteur 4
items.description: Le verdict est tombé ce mardi 6 octobre 2026 au Tribunal de Grande Instance (TGI) de Nouna. Soré Sayouba a été condamné à 30 ans de prison ferme pour les faits liés à l’assassinat de son épouse, Afousétou Soré, et de son ami Daouda Zallé, dans la soirée du dimanche 13 septembre 2026 au secteur 4 de Nouna. Le tribunal lui a également accordé un délai de neuf mois pour le remboursement de certains biens, notamment une moto d’une valeur de 300 000 F CFA appartenant à la victime Daouda Zallé et un vélo estimé à 60 000 F CFA appartenant à Drabo, une autre victime qui avait réussi à échapper à l’agression. Le condamné dispose de dix jours pour interjeter appel. À la barre, Sayouba Soré évoque les causes du drame À la barre, Soré Sayouba a reconnu l’existence de mésententes entre lui et son épouse. Il a toutefois affirmé s’être laissé emporter par la colère au moment des faits. Plus loin dans son témoignage, il a soutenu que sa femme ne lui avait pourtant « rien fait de mal ». Concernant la présence de son ami Daouda Zallé sur les lieux, le condamné a déclaré ne pas l’avoir appelé. Selon lui, son ami serait venu de lui-même et serait arrivé au moment où les événements se déroulaient. Sayouba Soré a expliqué avoir alors pris peur, pensant que son ami venait pour l’agresser. Cette crainte, selon sa version, l’aurait poussé à se précipiter et à réagir violemment. Ces déclarations constituent ainsi les éléments avancés par l’accusé pour expliquer les circonstances ayant conduit au double meurtre. Une soirée d’horreur qui avait bouleversé Nouna Les faits remontent au dimanche 13 septembre 2026. Ce soir-là, le secteur 4 de Nouna avait été plongé dans une scène de violence qui avait profondément marqué les habitants. Selon les témoignages recueillis après le drame, Soré Sayouba, marchand de bétail originaire de Dara et âgé de plus de 40 ans, aurait d’abord agressé son épouse, Afousétou Soré, âgée de 26 ans. Étudiante à l’Université Nazi Boni de Dédougou, où elle avait validé sa deuxième année en économie et mathématiques avec une moyenne de 14/20, la jeune femme était également mère d’une fillette de quatre ans. Elle aurait été poursuivie par son mari avant d’être mortellement agressée à son domicile. Daouda Zallé également tué Dans la foulée, Daouda Zallé, un ami du mis en cause, aurait été attiré sur les lieux. Il aurait à son tour subi une violente agression avant que son corps ne soit retrouvé parmi les engins incendiés. Un autre ami, nommé Souley, aurait également échappé de peu à l’agression. Appelé sur place, il aurait découvert Soré Sayouba armé d’une machette et d’une daba. « Il m’a dit qu’il avait tué sa femme. Il tenait une machette et une daba avant de se jeter sur moi. Je me suis sauvé dans un champ de maïs », avait-il témoigné, encore profondément marqué par la scène. L’intervention déterminante d’un dozo Alors que la violence se poursuivait, un dozo identifié comme Kassoum Dama, originaire de Sanso, serait intervenu. Il serait parvenu à maîtriser puis à ligoter Soré Sayouba. « Lorsque j’ai pu le ligoter, il m’a dit de le terminer pour de bon », avait rapporté le dozo. Son intervention aurait permis de mettre fin à la série d’agressions et d’éviter potentiellement d’autres victimes. Une tentative de suicide après les faits Après les violences, Soré Sayouba aurait tenté de mettre fin à ses jours en se blessant à l’aide d’une machette et d’une pioche. Grièvement blessé à la gorge et à la tête, il avait été pris en charge au CMA de Nouna avant d’être confié aux forces de sécurité. Au lendemain du drame, l’émotion était particulièrement vive à la morgue, au cimetière municipal et dans les familles des victimes. Afousétou Soré et Daouda Zallé avaient été inhumés dans la matinée du lundi 14 septembre au cimetière municipal de Nouna. Un mois après le drame, la justice tranche Près d’un mois après cette soirée tragique, le TGI de Nouna a donc rendu son verdict. Soré Sayouba est condamné à 30 ans de prison ferme. Une décision qui vient clore le volet judiciaire de cette affaire, sous réserve de l’exercice éventuel de son droit d’appel dans le délai de dix jours. Madi Sidparaadye Kébré Burkinaweb.net L’article TGI de Nouna : Soré Sayouba condamné à 30 ans de prison ferme après avoir tué sa femme et son ami au secteur 4 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Gov’t begins 175-hectare Anunuso irrigation project to raise rice production
items.description: The government has commenced work on a 175-hectare irrigation scheme at Anunuso Valley near Brofoyedru in the Sekyere East District of the Ashanti Region, as part of efforts to expand year-round rice production. The Anunuso Water Conservation Scheme, being implemented through the West Africa Food System Resilience Programme (FSRP), is expected to provide reliable irrigation for at least 220 farmers belonging to the Anunuso Rice Farmers’ Cooperative. The project is expected to significantly improve productivity, with technical estimates indicating that rice yields could rise from about 2.5 metric tonnes per hectare to five metric tonnes per hectare. With two cropping cycles each year, the scheme could produce about 1,750 metric tonnes of paddy annually, equivalent to roughly 1,100 metric tonnes of milled rice. The initiative is also projected to generate employment beyond the farm, with about 100 jobs expected during construction and an estimated 2,500 jobs to be created across the rice value chain once the facility becomes fully operational. Speaking at the sod-cutting and site-possession ceremony, the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, said the scheme formed part of efforts to reduce farmers’ reliance on rainfall and create conditions for more predictable agricultural production. He said it was also aligned with the Feed Ghana Programme’s Irrigation for Wealth module. Mr Opoku urged the beneficiary farmers to work closely with extension officers and prospective buyers to align production with market demand. He stressed that improved yields must be matched by proper harvesting, drying, storage and milling to enable locally produced rice to compete effectively. He also directed the contractor, Nathawo Investment Properties and Investment Limited, to adhere strictly to approved specifications and deliver quality work. The Minister called for strong supervision and urged the contractor and technical teams to prioritise local participation and respond promptly to concerns from communities around the project. The Minister further appealed to traditional authorities, the Sekyere East District Assembly and farmers to protect the water resources and catchment areas from encroachment, pollution and erosion. He said consultations were continuing over concerns raised by traditional authorities regarding the land agreements for the project, with the Ministry’s legal team reviewing the issues. The Anunuso scheme forms part of a wider FSRP intervention targeting 4,800 hectares of irrigation and inland valley development. The programme covers the Kpong, Tanoso, Vea and Weta irrigation systems, as well as the Anunuso, Odaho/Odamu, Waamu/Kumi and Kawampe inland valley enclaves. Mr Opoku said the success of the investment would ultimately be measured by whether farmers could plan their production with greater certainty, increase their harvests and improve their incomes sustainably. He subsequently cut the sod to officially commence work on the Anunuso Water Conservation Scheme.

items.title: Unlearned lessons
items.description: THE talks between the government and the opposition were doomed from the outset, even though the fact that the two sides sat face to face at the negotiating table was a positive sign. The meeting took place under the shadow of the PTI’s threatened long march to Islamabad, while the government brandished the option of governor’s rule in KP. The tension was palpable. The capital was sealed off with containers and the highways were blocked. Days before the talks, the military leadership warned against any repeat of a May 9-like situation — a clear message to the opposition not to cross the red line. Some opposition leaders, for their part, wanted a negotiated deal to bring down the political temperature. The prolonged discussions suggested a measure of seriousness on both sides, but mutual distrust and brinkmanship blocked any breakthrough. The two sides gave contrary accounts of why the talks collapsed after a marathon sitting. The government contended that the opposition backed out after agreeing to a final draft; the other side denied this, saying the differences were too wide to bridge. That so-called final draft is not in the public domain, but two major points of difference appear to have defeated the agreement. The PTI insisted on a meeting with Imran Khan, while the government wanted the KP provincial government to give unqualified support to the counterterrorism operation being carried out by the security forces. While conceding to the opposition’s demand that the former prime minister be allowed to meet his family and his lawyers, as ordered by the Islamabad High Court, and agreeing to implement the Supreme Court order to arrange his medical treatment, the government was not prepared to let PTI leaders meet and consult him before finalising the agreement — a condition it found unacceptable. The prevailing political instability has provided greater space to the militants. The real cause of the stalemate, however, was the issue of provincial government support, and taking ownership of a planned counterterrorism military operation in five southern districts, including the merged Fata regions. For the provincial government this was an extremely tricky matter: it had strongly opposed any kinetic operation involving the displacement of the population, and the bitter memories of earlier operations had created intense public opposition to any such action. A multiparty meeting called by the provincial government early this year — whose participants included provincial legislators belonging to PML-N, PPP and ANP — had unanimously opposed any large-scale military operation. Considering this, it was hard for the PTI to take ownership of a highly unpopular action. It may be true that the PTI has no clarity over how to combat the menace of terrorism that has swept a large part of the province. Its inaction, often seen as capitulation, has added to the problem. The ill-equipped police and Counter Terrorism Department have been a major target of militants, resulting in a virtual collapse of the administration in the troubled districts. That inaction could also be attributed to the ongoing confrontation between the PTI and the establishment-backed federal government. Then there is the question of whether we have a coherent, overarching national security policy and counterterrorism strategy to deal with this existential threat. There has rarely been any debate in parliament on internal security policy. It is all left to the security establishment, with hardly any policy input from the civilian leadership. KP has witnessed a strong resurgence of militancy over the last five years, which has claimed the lives of thousands of civilians and security personnel. Last year saw the highest number of terrorist attacks in the province since 2013, despite claims of successful intelligence operations that killed hundreds of terrorists. The prevailing political instability has provided greater space to the militants, who are now better equipped and better organised, and who have extended their activities to other parts of the province. Pakistan has blamed Afghanistan’s Taliban regime for providing sanctuaries and aiding the TTP, and each major terrorist attack is now answered by Pakistani strikes across the border. The closure of the border and of trade between the two countries over the past year has directly affected the local population and added to the tension between Peshawar and Islamabad. There is a serious disconnect in the policy the establishment pursues in dealing with terrorism, and the government needs to address those concerns. There are no two views about the imperatives of a national security policy, but there is also a need to bring all stakeholders on board for an overarching policy that should not rest entirely on kinetic operations. It is important to address the social and economic issues in order to win public support in the affected areas. The widening trust gap between the state and the people, and the politics of confrontation, are the biggest hurdles in combating terrorism. With little hope of the two sides returning to the negotiating table, the confrontation has now escalated: the PTI has begun its protest march from the southern KP districts. It is apparent that the PTI has changed its strategy of marching directly on Islamabad. Instead, the party now plans to mobilise its supporters in the province and camp close to the capital rather than march into the city. It is the first instance of a chief executive leading a protest that paralyses his own province. Meanwhile, the federal government is considering removing the PTI government and imposing a state of emergency or governor’s rule in the province. That would be an extremely dangerous move in a province already facing terrorist attacks, rising nationalism and tension on its border. Any such move by a state already fighting a separatist movement in Balochistan and a revolt-like situation in Azad Kashmir would be disastrous. The province is sitting on a powder keg, and the removal from power of an elected government that enjoys an overwhelming majority in the provincial assembly and broad popular support could ignite it in a way the state would struggle to extinguish. We never learn lessons from our own history, and make the same mistake again and again and expect different results. The writer is an author and journalist. zhussain100@yahoo.com X: @hidhussain Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Accidents de la circulation: 33 morts et 3.232 blessés en périmètre urbain la semaine dernière
items.description: Trente-trois personnes ont trouvé la mort et 3.232 autres ont été blessées, dont 130 grièvement, dans 2.295 accidents de la circulation survenus en périmètre urbain, durant la semaine allant du 28 septembre au 04 octobre, a indiqué la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale (DGSN). Ces accidents sont principalement dus, dans l'ordre, à l'inadvertance des conducteurs, au non-respect de la priorité, à l'inadvertance des piétons, à l'excès de vitesse, à la non maîtrise du véhicule, au changement de direction non autorisé, au changement de direction sans usage du clignotant, au non-respect de la distance de sécurité, au non-respect du feu rouge, au non-respect du stop, à la circulation sur la voie gauche, à la circulation en sens interdit et à la conduite en état d’ébriété et au dépassement défectueux, précise la DGSN dans un communiqué. Concernant les opérations de contrôle et de répression en matière de circulation, les services de sûreté ont enregistré 51.890 contraventions, dressé 8.181 procès-verbaux transmis au Parquet et procédé au recouvrement de 43.709 amendes transactionnelles, selon la même source. Les sommes perçues au titre de ces contraventions ont atteint 9.540.100 dirhams, ajoute le communiqué, faisant état de la mise en fourrière municipale de 5.474 véhicules, de la saisie de 8.181 documents et du retrait de la circulation de 593 véhicules. The post Accidents de la circulation: 33 morts et 3.232 blessés en périmètre urbain la semaine dernière appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Jubilé historique de Lionel Messi : Les Guépards font douter l’Argentine pendant 45 minutes avant l’ultime récital de la Pulga au Monumental
items.description: Opposés à l'Argentine dans l'enceinte surchauffée du stade Monumental de Buenos Aires, les Guépards du Bénin ont livré une première période héroïque avant de s'incliner (3-0) mardi soir. Dans un match marqué par les adieux internationaux de Lionel Messi devant plus de 85 000 spectateurs, la sélection béninoise a contenu les assauts de l'Albiceleste jusqu'à la pause, avant de céder au retour des vestiaires face au génie du capitaine argentin, auteur d'un but et de deux passes décisives pour sa toute dernière apparition sous le maillot national. La soirée promettait d'être historique au stade Monumental de Buenos Aires, et elle a tenu toutes ses promesses. Face à plus de 85 000 spectateurs venus saluer la toute dernière apparition sous le maillot national de leur icône Lionel Messi, les Guépards du Bénin ont fait preuve d'une bravoure remarquable avant de plier en seconde période (3-0). Dès le coup d'envoi, l'Albiceleste a cherché à imposer son rythme, portée par une ferveur populaire indescriptible. À la 10ᵉ minute de jeu, la rencontre a même été momentanément interrompue pour permettre au public du Monumental d'offrir une longue et vibrante ovation à son numéro 10. Mais sur le terrain, la sélection béninoise n'est pas venue en simple spectatrice. Bien organisés et disciplinés, Marcel Dandjinou et sa muraille défensive sont parvenus à contrecarrer méthodiquement toutes les offensives de l'équipe championne du monde. Attentif et inspiré, le portier béninois s'est interposé avec succès sur deux tentatives cadrées de Lionel Messi, maintenant son arrière-garde à flot. À la pause, après 45 minutes d'une résistance acharnée, les deux formations ont regagné les vestiaires sur un score nul et vierge (0-0). La combativité des Guépards a finalement trouvé ses limites dès l'entame du second acte. À la 48ᵉ minute, Nicolás Otamendi est venu débloquer la situation pour l'Argentine en ouvrant le score, parfaitement servi par Lionel Messi. Malgré les tentatives de réaction du Bénin, la sélection argentine a progressivement assis sa maîtrise sur la partie. À la 61ᵉ minute, Nico Paz a accentué l'écart d'une frappe limpide décochée depuis l'extérieur de la surface de réparation, une nouvelle fois consécutive à une passe décisive du capitaine argentin. Le scénario de cette soirée d'adieux ne pouvait s'achever sans la signature personnelle du quintuple ballon d'or. À la 71ᵉ minute, Lionel Messi a obtenu un penalty. Sans trembler, le numéro 10 a pris Marcel Dandjinou à contre-pied pour inscrire le troisième et dernier but de la rencontre (3-0). Avec ce but et ses deux passes décisives, Lionel Messi achève sa carrière internationale par une feuille de match étincelante. Après plus de deux décennies sous la tunique de l'Albiceleste, le champion du monde 2022 et double vainqueur de la Copa América tire sa révérence en tant que meilleur buteur et joueur le plus capé de l'histoire de sa sélection. De leur côté, les Guépards du Bénin quittent Buenos Aires la tête haute, forts d'une première mi-temps de référence face aux sommets du football mondial. items.title: Saudi deployment
items.description: WITH confirmation that members of the Makkah Defence Alliance will be deploying their forces to Saudi Arabia, it appears that the kingdom is preparing for a full-scale war with the pro-Iran Houthi Ansarallah movement. Senior civil and military leaders from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye met in Riyadh on Monday to chart a course forward. Though details are sparse, the three defence allies agreed to ensure “rapid deployment in the Kingdom, in accordance with … the national legislation of the parties.” As collective defence is a central pillar of the trilateral alliance, such developments were expected. Members of the MDA also condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia, particularly alleged attempts to target the holy cities in Hejaz. It is hoped that, from Pakistan’s perspective, these developments only reflect a commitment to defend Saudi Arabia from outside aggression. It would be ill-advised for Pakistan, Turkiye or any other external actor to jump into the Yemeni quagmire. Pakistan has decades-old defence ties to the kingdom, and the pact only reflects a solidification of this relationship. The defence of the holy cities is also a sensitive matter, and Pakistan has in the past contributed troops to protect them. But getting dragged into the Yemeni civil war — which has pit Ansarallah against the Yemeni government, backed by Saudi Arabia — is another story altogether. There was considerable pressure on Pakistan in 2015 from Riyadh to get involved in its operation against the Houthis. Pakistan, thanks to the collective wisdom of parliament, at that time had wisely stayed away from any such undertaking. Similar wisdom is required at this juncture. This country values its deep ties with Saudi Arabia, and should do all it can to protect the kingdom from external aggression. But putting Pakistani boots on the ground in Yemen should be avoided. The fighting in Yemen, both between Ansarallah and the government, as well as between the Houthis and the Saudis, has intensified. At this point chances of a ceasefire seem remote. This conflict has been raging since 2015, and previous external attacks, including by the US and Israel, have failed to dislodge the Houthis. To prevent a fresh humanitarian catastrophe within Yemen, as well as the spread of this conflict across the region, there is an immediate need to end the hostilities. States such as Oman, which has channels open both with the Houthis as well as Saudi Arabia, can perhaps play a mediatory role. The basic requirements of a truce should include an end to all attacks on Saudi Arabia, free passage through Bab al-Mandeb, as well as a halt to all external attacks across Yemen. Only a political process led by Yemenis, and acceptable to all factions in the country, can bring internal peace, as well as guarantee the security of neighbouring states. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Annoh-Dompreh brokers talks as Zoomlion pledges support for Adipa communities
items.description: Concerns over waste disposal at the Adipa Engineered Landfill Site have taken a new turn following a stakeholder engagement involving residents, traditional authorities, local government officials and waste-management operators. The engagement, facilitated following interventions by the Minority Chief Whip and Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP Frank Annoh-Dompreh, has resulted in a package of measures to address concerns raised by communities affected by the landfill operations. Residents of Adipa and neighbouring communities had raised concerns over the transportation of waste from parts of Accra to the landfill site. They expressed concerns about potential environmental and public health impacts and called for greater consultation and measures to protect the communities hosting the facility. The concerns prompted Mr Annoh-Dompreh to push for direct engagement among residents, traditional authorities, local government officials, and the companies involved in waste management operations. The Aburihene and Adontenhene of the Akuapem Traditional Council, Otubour Gyan Kwasi, subsequently convened the stakeholder meeting on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. The meeting brought together Mr Annoh-Dompreh, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group, of which Zoomlion Ghana Limited is a subsidiary, Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, the Municipal Chief Executives of Akuapem South and Nsawam-Adoagyiri, traditional leaders, community representatives and other stakeholders. The discussions focused on the impact of landfill activities and the support required by communities in the area. Dr Agyepong acknowledged the concerns raised by residents and assured them of the company’s commitment to working with the communities and traditional authorities to address the issues. He also apologised for the failure to engage the affected communities earlier. As part of the response, he announced several interventions, including the construction of a health centre and the provision of a water project for the affected communities. The company also pledged to undertake community-wide fumigation and periodic health screening for residents of Adipa and surrounding communities. Dr Agyepong further announced educational support for beneficiaries from the eight affected communities to pursue studies in Russia. He said the company would continue to assess the needs of the communities and take further steps where necessary. The commitments were welcomed by the traditional authorities, who called for cooperation among the company, residents and other stakeholders to ensure their implementation. 17-member committee formed A 17-member committee has been established to oversee the implementation of the proposed interventions and provide accountability. Dr Agyepong is a member of the committee, while the Chief of Nsawam, Nana Kofi Sarh, has been authorised by the Aburihene to chair it. Members of the committee pledged to work to ensure that the agreed projects directly benefit the affected communities. Mr Annoh-Dompreh, who had earlier raised concerns about the waste situation and called for proper consultation with host communities, welcomed the outcome of the engagement. He commended Dr Agyepong for personally meeting residents and listening to their concerns. The MP stressed that waste management remains an important public responsibility, but said that decisions involving the transportation and disposal of large quantities of waste must be accompanied by meaningful consultation with traditional authorities, local assemblies, and affected residents. He said the concerns raised by residents should not be interpreted as opposition to waste management. Rather, he said they represent a legitimate demand for responsible practices, community engagement and protection of residents’ health and the environment. The stakeholder engagement has established a framework for addressing concerns at Adipa, with the newly constituted committee expected to monitor the implementation of the commitments and sustain dialogue among stakeholders.

items.title: US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
items.description: US Vice President JD Vance has said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the country’s seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations. Vance, a longtime sceptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections. Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns. “If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 per cent enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don’t build highly enriched fuel. That’s a very basic threshold issue,” Vance said. “I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity.” Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran’s latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms. Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions. “We’re not going to trade words for actions,” Vance said. Unclear how Iran makes decisions Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran. Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. But it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran’s power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war assassinated Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. “One of the things we picked up on is it’s not totally clear how their country makes decisions,” Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his “biggest problem” is no one knows who is running Iran. Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran’s decision-making system works. “The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials,” Esmaeil Baqaei told a weekly press conference. Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through the waterway. Vance declined to say if he was leading peace talks, though he is frequently cited as the White House’s top negotiator. “We’re certainly involved,” he said. “Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things.” The war and its $3 billion monthly price tag have become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress. Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling voters they should not let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month’s elections. In Alaska, Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play. Before speaking with Reuters , Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around energy. Alaska’s remote locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry. Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly introduced Vance as the president of the US, rather than the vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump in the White House. Vance told Reuters afterwards that he had not decided whether to seek the presidency in 2028. “I’m inherently a procrastinator,” he said. “I really haven’t thought about it much.”

items.title: Account for the old economy before selling us a new one
items.description: The Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, has spent the past few weeks introducing Ghanaians to what he calls the “New Economy.” He has taken it to the Association of Ghana Industries, the Trade Ministry, and the banks, and we are told that the full details will come in the 2027 Budget. The message is that Ghana should produce more of what it consumes and create jobs at home. I agree with that goal, and so would most Ghanaians. Our own government pursued it through One District One Factory and Planting for Food and Jobs. The difficulty is that this administration came to office with a string of programmes it said would deliver exactly this, and almost none of them can show results. Rather than finish what it started, the government is now moving on to a new promise. Before the country is asked to invest hope and money in it, Ghanaians deserve an honest report on the old ones. Where are the results? The 24-Hour Economy was presented as the heart of the NDC’s economic plan. It promised 1.7 million decent jobs by the end of 2028. For 2026, its direct budget allocation was GH¢110 million. When I asked in July what the programme had achieved, the Secretariat pointed to 268 filling stations and 33 manufacturers operating in shifts. Anyone who has bought fuel at midnight in Accra or Kumasi knows those filling stations were open long before this government arrived. The Centre for Policy Scrutiny raised the same concern in its review of the mid-year budget. The Secretariat also spoke of 160,000 jobs from recently signed agreements. I described those numbers at the time as audio announcements, and I stand by it. Until we can see the workers, the firms employing them and the SSNIT contributions being paid on their behalf, Ghanaians have no way of knowing whether those jobs exist. The Women’s Development Bank was one of the most attractive promises of the 2024 campaign. Almost two years on, it has not lent a single cedi. Government allocated GH¢51.3 million to it in 2025, and several hundred million more in 2026, and the Minister told Parliament in July that GH¢400 million had been deposited at the Bank of Ghana as capital. The company was incorporated only in January 2026 and is still awaiting a banking licence. Women’s groups such as NETRIGHT are now publicly asking the government to hurry up. Market women who were told help was coming are still borrowing from susu collectors and moneylenders at the same punishing rates. The One Million Coders Programme promised to train a million young Ghanaians over four years and open pathways to jobs and remote work. The target for 2026 alone was 300,000. By the mid-year review, the Minister reported 140,000 registrations, 40,000 enrolments and about 28,000 people who had completed at least one module. That last figure is the one government now leads with, and it tells us very little. Finishing one module is a long way from being a coder, and there is still no published figure for how many trainees have found work. Then there is Feed Ghana, and in particular its poultry component, Nkoko Nkitinkiti. It was meant to cut our chicken import bill by setting up households in poultry production. In July, the Agriculture Minister told Parliament’s Assurances Committee that some beneficiaries had eaten the birds instead of rearing them. The Poultry Farmers Association called the first phase an “abysmal failure” and said its offer to train beneficiaries for free was ignored. The Minister insists the project is a success and points to falling poultry prices, but he has not published how many beneficiaries are still in production or what has happened to import volumes. Meanwhile, livestock farmers told The Fourth Estate in August that the programme’s promises on cattle, goats, sheep and pigs had not reached them, and government confirmed those components had not yet started. The New Economy, as described so far, will commit about US$10 billion over four years to commercial agriculture, mining value addition, energy and transport infrastructure. Commercial agriculture already sits under Feed Ghana. Agro-processing and energy projects such as the Buipe solar plant are already listed under the 24-Hour Economy. Access to finance for small producers was the whole point of the Women’s Development Bank. It is hard to see what the new label adds, other than a fresh starting point from which the government can measure itself. Whose stability? The Minister credits the government’s “bold reforms” for lower inflation, a steadier cedi and returning investor confidence. It is worth asking which of the NDC’s own ideas produced any of that. On stability, the NDC’s big idea in opposition was to renegotiate the IMF programme. Candidate Mahama told Reuters in 2024 that he would do so. Once in office, his Finance Minister explained that renegotiating would imply the government did not believe in the programme’s parameters, and the idea was quietly dropped. Regarding growth, the NDC’s ideas were those described above. Not one of them has produced results that Ghanaians can measure. What the country is enjoying today grew from seeds the NPP planted. The IMF programme that anchored the recovery was negotiated and secured by the NPP government in May 2023. The domestic debt exchange, which eased pressure on interest payments and maturities, was ours. So was the June 2024 agreement with bilateral and commercial creditors, and the Eurobond exchange that cut the stock of Ghana’s external debt. By the time power changed hands, inflation had fallen from 54.1 per cent at the end of 2022 to 23.8 per cent, and the economy had grown 5.7 per cent in 2024. The NDC inherited that programme, ran it to its final review in July 2026, and has taken the harvest to market under its own label. The fiscal discipline the government now boasts about was built inside that same programme. The IMF framework required Ghana to run primary surpluses, and in 2025 the government wrote a floor of 1.5 per cent of GDP into law. The programme ended in July. Within weeks, the Minister announced that the floor would be cut to 0.5 per cent from 2027 to make room for the New Economy, alongside new revenue measures worth another 0.5 per cent of GDP. The IMF has said the country can still meet its debt target on the lower path, but only if revenue collection, public investment management and the finances of state enterprises in energy and cocoa improve, and none of those has yet been fixed. With about GH¢58 billion in restructured domestic bonds falling due in 2027 and GH¢53 billion in 2028, Ghanaians are entitled to ask whether this government’s discipline was ever its own, or whether it lasted only as long as the IMF was in the room. What Parliament should ask for I would urge the government to put the New Economy on hold and first report properly on the commitments it has already made. It should publish a register of 24-Hour Economy jobs that can be checked against payroll and SSNIT records. It should give Parliament a firm date for the Women’s Development Bank to start lending and publish its lending criteria. It should tell us how many One Million Coders graduates are now employed and commission an independent audit of Nkoko Nkitinkiti beneficiaries. And before Parliament is asked to amend the fiscal responsibility law, the Minister should come with a costed plan for the 2027 and 2028 maturities, evidence of progress on the reforms the IMF has flagged, and a commitment to audited, separate reporting on how the freed-up money is spent. Parliament should not agree to weaken the country’s fiscal anchor to fund a programme whose details have not even been published. Ghanaians voted in 2024 for jobs, for relief from the cost of living, and for the specific programmes the NDC put before them. Two years later, those programmes sit half-delivered while the government invites us to look at a new one. The promises made in 2024 have not expired, and the government should be held to every one of them. ******* The writer, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, is the MP for Ofoase-Ayirebi and Ranking Member, Economy and Development Committee

items.title: ¿Puede volver Puigdemont a España?
items.description: El Tribunal Constitucional ha dado este martes un paso decisivo para que Carles Puigdemont pueda regresar a España. Por siete votos frente a cinco, ha avalado la aplicación de la ley de amnistía al delito de malversación en el caso de la exconsellera Dolors Bassa y ha considerado que el Tribunal Supremo interpretó de forma incorrecta la excepción de la ley referida al “enriquecimiento personal”. El Constitucional ordena al Supremo que revise su decisión. El juez Pablo Llarena ha reaccionado dejando provisionalmente sin efecto la orden nacional de detención que pesaba sobre Puigdemont, Toni Comín y Lluís Puig, pero todavía no les ha aplicado formalmente la amnistía. items.title: Abanga sets 4 million youth-vote target for Bawumia ahead of 2028 election
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fusani Yakubu, says he is targeting four million votes from young Ghanaians for former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the 2028 presidential election. Mr Abanga insists the target is achievable despite questions about whether it is realistic, given that Dr Bawumia secured 4.6 million votes in the 2024 election. He said achieving the target would require hard work, sacrifice and a strong grassroots mobilisation strategy. “It is. You see, it requires hard work. It requires sacrifice. It requires getting the right people on the ground to get the job done,” he said on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday. Mr Abanga said he intends to lead the youth mobilisation effort from the ground rather than operate from the party’s headquarters. “I’ll be moving. I promise them I’m not going to be an armchair National Youth Organiser. I’ll be joining them in their various regions, constituencies very soon,” he said. He said his strategy will involve combining grassroots mobilisation with social media to promote the NPP’s message and Dr Bawumia’s record. “So we preach the gospel of Dr Mahamud Bawumia. It’s the only solution for this country,” he said. Mr Abanga also attacked the government over rising fuel prices and its implementation of the 24-hour economy policy. “Yet today we can’t buy fuel. Prices of fuel have gone up GH¢20 and above,” he said. He questioned how the 24-hour economy could function effectively when an office responsible for regulating it closes at 5pm. “How can an office that is meant to regulate an office that is supposed to operate 24 hours close at 5 p.m.?” he asked. Mr Abanga further criticised the government over cocoa prices, arguing that farmers are now receiving less despite previous promises. “My father is a go-go farmer. My mom is a cocoa farmer,” he said. He claimed that cocoa was previously being bought at GH¢3,100 but that the price had since fallen to GH¢2,000. “They said they were going to buy cocoa GH¢6000. They should not even mention anything about global prices,” he said. The NPP youth leader said these issues would form part of his mobilisation message as the party prepares for 2028. He said the responsibility now rests on him to organise the youth and build an effective campaign for Dr Bawumia. “And being a youth and representing my party as a national youth commander, I must take charge, mobilise the youth, so we can prosecute an effective campaign, so Dr Bawumia wins the 2020 election to save this country,” he said.

items.title: 50-year-old murder suspect slumps, dies during trial in Bayelsa
items.description: A 50-year-old murder suspect, Bethlehem Nwanlia, reportedly slumped and died shortly after proceedings began at the Bayelsa State High Court in Yenagoa on Tuesday. Nwanlia was standing trial alongside two other defendants over alleged conspiracy, kidnapping and multiple murder when the incident occurred at Court 11. He reportedly collapsed in the court’s holding area shortly after Justice Amadise Michael Ekadi adjourned judgment in the case to October 27, 2026. According to people who witnessed the incident, Nwanlia suddenly clutched his chest before collapsing. Officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service, police personnel and lawyers reportedly attempted to revive him, but their efforts were unsuccessful. A medical personnel was subsequently called to examine him, after which his body was taken to a hospital for further confirmation. The Bayelsa State Judiciary’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Enoch Okunobo, confirmed the incident to newsmen on Tuesday evening. He said the deceased’s body had been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) mortuary. “Somebody collapsed and died today. He was a murder suspect, who had been coming to court. His corpse has been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC),” Okunobo said. Nwanlia and the two other defendants were facing allegations linked to the 2022 killing of three people in Kalaba community, Yenagoa Local Government Area of the state. The allegations against the defendants had not been finally determined by the court before Nwanlia’s death. Reports also indicated that the deceased had experienced health complications while in custody. However, authorities had yet to establish the cause of his death as of the time of filing the report. The incident reportedly caused confusion among court officials, lawyers, security personnel and others present at the court premises. When contacted, the Bayelsa State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed, said he was not aware of the incident. Mohammed, however, promised to make inquiries and revert, but had yet to do so as of the time of filing the report. The post 50-year-old murder suspect slumps, dies during trial in Bayelsa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Seized assets: Diezani’s UK acquittal immaterial, EFCC tells court
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—THE Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, has urged the Federal High Court in Abuja to disregard the acquittal of former Petroleum Resources Minister, Diezani Alison-Madueke, by a United Kingdom court, describing the judgment as immaterial to the ongoing forfeiture proceedings involving assets linked to her. The commission made the submission in a further counter-affidavit filed in opposition to Diezani’s application seeking to tender the June 17 judgment of the Southwark Crown Court in London, which discharged and acquitted her of bribery and corruption allegations. Justice Inyang Ekwo had on July 1 granted the former minister permission to present the UK judgment as evidence in the suit. However, the EFCC maintained that the proceedings in the UK had no bearing on the Nigerian case or the final forfeiture orders upon which the disputed assets were disposed of. The anti-graft agency said: “The proceedings before the Southwark Crown Court, London, United Kingdom, and the purported acquittal of the applicant therein, are in respect of a proceeding that is not being prosecuted before any Nigerian court and have nothing to do with the substantive suit before this honourable court.” The commission also urged the court to dismiss the application and the supplementary affidavit filed by the former minister, describing some of the depositions as misleading. According to the EFCC, the forfeiture proceedings relate to assets covered by final orders of Nigerian courts, adding that the orders remained valid and had not been set aside. It said the sale of the properties was conducted pursuant to final forfeiture orders made by Justice C.A. Obiozor of the Federal High Court on July 9, 2019, and another order issued by Justice I.N. Oweibo on September 10, 2019. The commission said it had also published notices in newspapers inviting interested persons to show cause why the assets should not be forfeited before the final orders were made. “The final forfeiture orders pursuant to which the sale of the properties was conducted are still in force and have not been set aside. The forfeited properties were disposed of in accordance with due process of law,” the EFCC stated. Diezani, however, has asked the court to order the EFCC to retrieve properties allegedly sold to third parties. In the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/21/2023, filed through her counsel, Prof. Mike Ozekhome, SAN, she alleged that the commission commenced the sale of assets linked to her without affording her fair hearing. She contended that several final forfeiture orders were obtained through misrepresentation, suppression and non-disclosure of material facts. The former minister further argued that she had never been convicted of any unlawful activity to justify the forfeiture of her properties, insisting that the courts lacked jurisdiction to make the orders without hearing her. She also claimed that she had been outside Nigeria since 2015 while undergoing medical treatment and was not served with relevant court processes. Diezani argued that the forfeiture orders were made on the civil standard of proof, rather than the stricter standard applicable to criminal allegations. She said she had three suits pending against the EFCC in Lagos and maintained that the assets should not have been sold while the forfeiture orders were being challenged. The EFCC, however, said criminal proceedings had been instituted against Diezani in various Nigerian courts following investigations into her activities while she was a public servant. It cited charges including FHC/ABJ/CR/208/2018 and HC/ADYL/56C/2017, filed before the Federal High Court and Adamawa State High Court respectively. Justice Ekwo adjourned the matter until November 11 for hearing of the pending applications. The post Seized assets: Diezani’s UK acquittal immaterial, EFCC tells court appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ATC delays Imaan, Hadi’s indictment in security breach case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) adjourned the indictment proceedings against lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha, until Wednesday (today) after they could not be produced due to a power outage. ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra was scheduled to frame charges against the two lawyers in a case registered at Aabpara Police Station over alleged disruption of the security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. During the hearing, prosecutor Raja Naveed appeared before the court, while junior lawyers represented the accused in the absence of their lead counsel. The junior lawyers sought an adjournment, stating that the lead counsel were busy at the High Court. They also requested copies of the challan and a fresh date for the proceedings. The judge observed that copies of the challan had already been provided and that the court intended to frame charges that day. However, a junior lawyer complained that they were not being allowed to meet their clients. Justice Sipra remarked that the signed powers of attorney had already been received and that proceedings could not be conducted according to the convenience of the lawyers. The court briefly adjourned the proceedings. When the hearing resumed, however, the accused could not be produced through the video link because of power outage at Adiala jail, preventing the court from proceeding with their indictment. The judge directed the jail authorities to ensure the presence of both accused through video link at the next hearing, warning that contempt of court proceedings would be initiated in case of non-compliance. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Vanguard’s mental health advocacy deserves recognition, says APN President, Nyamali
items.description: By Chioma Obinna As the 4th Mental Health Summit organised by Vanguard Newspapers holds on Friday, a Consultant Psychiatrist, Dr Veronica Nyamali and President, Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria has commended Vanguard Media Limited for its sustained commitment to mental health advocacy, public enlightenment and responsible reporting of the issues in Nigeria. Nyamali, who spoke on the significance of the annual Vanguard Mental Health Summit, said the newspaper had consistently provided a platform for mental health professionals, stakeholders and members of the public to engage on emerging and critical issues affecting mental wellbeing. She said mental health was fundamental to giving people “meaning, purpose and direction to life,” stressing that efforts to promote mental wellbeing should go beyond clinical care to include sustained public education and awareness. According to her, Vanguard’s engagement with the mental health community has created valuable opportunities for Nigerians to gain better understanding of mental health conditions, available interventions and emerging developments in the field. “Through its activities, Vanguard creates valuable opportunities to educate the Nigerian public by bringing together relevant stakeholders and experts to address important and contemporary mental health issues,” she said. Nyamali noted that Vanguard’s contribution went beyond conventional news reporting, saying the organisation had over time built strong relationships with mental health professionals and demonstrated an understanding of responsible and professional reporting of mental health matters. She described the annual Vanguard Mental Health Summit as “the peak of these efforts,” noting that the event had become a platform stakeholders and members of the public looked forward to each year. She said: “The annual Vanguard Mental Health Summit stands as the peak of these efforts. It is an event that stakeholders and members of the public look forward to each year, providing an important platform for hearing the latest developments, perspectives and updates on emerging and ongoing mental health issues in Nigeria.” According to Nyamali, the summit provides an opportunity for experts and stakeholders to draw attention to pressing mental health challenges while also exploring practical approaches to addressing them. She commended Vanguard for its broad and balanced coverage of mental health issues, saying the newspaper had remained intentional about bringing important issues to public attention. “Vanguard is also intentional about providing broad and balanced coverage, ensuring that important issues are brought to public attention and that no stone is left unturned when addressing the burning topics of the day,” she said. Nyamali said the newspaper’s sustained commitment to mental health advocacy, education, professional collaboration and responsible journalism deserved recognition. She added that Vanguard had demonstrated that the media could play a significant role in improving public understanding of mental health and reducing the misconceptions and stigma often associated with mental health conditions. “In view of these efforts, Vanguard deserves to be recognised for its outstanding contribution to mental health awareness and advocacy in Nigeria, particularly as a leading mentally aware and mental-health-friendly print media organisation,” she said. The Vanguard Mental Health Summit brings together psychiatrists, psychologists, other healthcare professionals, policymakers, advocates and members of the public to discuss critical issues around mental health and wellbeing in Nigeria. items.title: Junts busca exprimir el regreso de Puigdemont para impactar en la campaña electoral
items.description: La decisión del Tribunal Constitucional de avalar el despliegue completo de la ley de amnistía ha precipitado un efecto dominó al que solo le falta por tumbar la última ficha: el regreso a Cataluña del expresidente de la Generalitat Carles Puigdemont. El líder independentista y los principales mandos de su partido han pasado las últimas semanas haciendo llamadas a la calma, apuntando que no hay que apresurarse a celebrar nada ni anticipar la toma de decisiones hasta tener, papel en mano, la total seguridad jurídica de que un viaje de vuelta a España no implicaría ningún riesgo, por remoto que fuera, de dejar a Puigdemont sentado delante de un juez. Este martes, pocos minutos antes de saberse el levantamiento de la orden de detención por parte del Tribunal Supremo, el abogado Gonzalo Boye hizo unas declaraciones a TV3 señalando que se habían esfumado los motivos para alargar la estancia en Waterloo del expresidente catalán. “Yo no hablaré por él”, dijo Boye, pero dio por sentado que Puigdemont pasará las Navidades en Cataluña. items.title: Sin casa y aún sin decreto: así esperan las medidas de vivienda los desahuciados acampados en Sol
items.description: David Jiménez tiene 52 años y durante los últimos 20 ha vivido en su piso en el Ensanche de Vallecas, hasta hace dos semanas. Ahora no tiene hogar. Fue desahuciado horas antes de que echaran a Maricarmen, de 87 años . Su desalojo fue más silencioso, con un despliegue policial, pero sin resistencia, ni de su parte, ni de su hijo de 21 años, ni de las personas que le apoyaron. Aquel día no quiso que “nadie” se llevase un “golpe” por su “culpa”. Ahora intenta ir todos los días a la acampada de la Puerta del Sol porque cree que la organización ciudadana y la huelga general, que han convocado los sindicatos, son el camino hacia una vivienda digna. El decreto que se votó el pasado viernes en el Congreso, que incluía medidas de protección contra los desahucios, le llegaba “una semana tarde”. Y, después de que PP, Vox y Junts tumbasen las iniciativas que intentaban paliar el problema de la vivienda, ya no tiene ni hogar ni, de momento, las “migajas” que para él suponen ese texto. items.title: PP, Vox y Junts han votado ocho veces juntos contra decretos con medidas sobre vivienda

El presidente, Pedro Sánchez, arguyó este martes tras el Consejo de Ministros, y para presentar los nuevos decretos retocados que irán ahora a una Diputación Permanente todavía sin fecha, que su Gabinete “ha hecho mucho” en esa materia, pero no disponía de una mayoría en las Cortes que lo respaldara. Aludió incluso a que el bloque de la derecha parlamentaria, donde incluyó a PP, Vox y Junts, paralizó muchos intentos de reformas. El Gobierno de Sánchez ha promovido 25 reales decretos ley con actuaciones sobre vivienda desde 2019, 19 han sido convalidados, dos en sesiones de la Diputación Permanente, cuatro no y en ocho ocasiones PP, Vox y Junts votaron juntos en contra . items.title: Reflexiones de un día de matanza interminable
items.description: Los últimos tres años han sido una forma de tortura de una lentitud insoportable, y el espíritu actual aquí, entre el río y el mar, es que el 7 de octubre continúa presente: seguimos viviendo aquel horrible día que se niega a terminar. Los rostros de los rehenes israelíes liberados de Gaza y de los padres afligidos cuyos hijos nunca regresaron a casa siguen llenando nuestras pantallas de televisión. Muchos de ellos también adornan las listas de candidatos de los distintos partidos políticos, junto a generales retirados y reservistas. Hace poco más de una semana, un padre doliente que figura en la lista del Likud, en respuesta a una rehén liberada (una mujer de casi 90 años) que habló en contra del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, le dijo que ojalá pudieran devolverla al cautiverio de Hamás. Son palabras muy duras, pero en la guerra vale todo. Si en Israel alguien se atreve a sugerir que el 7 de octubre ya ha quedado atrás, la gente de alrededor señalará inmediatamente un avión de FlyDubai sobrevolando la ciudad y le reprenderá por decir semejante tontería: “¿Ves?”, insistirán, “todavía nos están masacrando”. Y, aunque las únicas lesiones graves en ese incidente las sufrió el piloto indio, los medios israelíes se apresuraron a presentarlo como un valiente héroe que defendía a Israel, simplemente porque salvó su propia vida al enfrentarse a un terrorista perturbado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tres años de sufrimiento en Gaza: “Aquel 7 de octubre sentí que nuestras vidas acabarían destrozadas. Es lo que ha sucedido”
items.description: “El 7 de octubre de 2023, estaba seguro de que pagaríamos un precio muy alto y de que nuestras vidas acabarían destrozadas. Realmente lo sentía. Y es lo que ha sucedido”. Anwar al Shtat, desplazado desde entonces 12 veces de su Beit Hanún natal, en el norte de Gaza, malvive hoy, con 55 años, en una de las innumerables tiendas de campaña de la atestada capital. Relata su situación con una aguda sensación de olvido, en un espacio pequeño y oscuro junto a calles llenas de aguas residuales. “El mundo entero ve cómo vivimos y, sin embargo, se queda de brazos cruzados. Culpo a los países árabes y también a los dirigentes de las facciones palestinas que están fuera de Gaza. Nuestro destino y nuestras vidas han quedado en manos de esas facciones, pero nadie hace lo suficiente para poner fin a nuestro sufrimiento. Israel no cede, Hamás no cede y el mundo entero nos trata como si no fuéramos seres humanos. A veces siento que solo se acuerdan de nosotros durante el día. Luego, cuando se van a dormir por la noche, dejamos de pasarles por la mente”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tres años después
items.description: Tres años después, Israel ya no es la misma que era hasta el 7 de octubre de 2023 a las 6.29 de la mañana. Tal vez sería más exacto escribir que no es “distinta”, sino que, desde aquel fatídico ataque, ha pasado a ser mucho más de lo que siempre ha sido: mucho más atormentada, trastocada y desconcertada. Esta es la gran diferencia entre el antes y el después del 7 de octubre. Una nueva “normalidad” se ha instalado en este país; una cotidianidad espeluznante, ya enquistada en la piel, donde cada uno de sus habitantes se ha convertido en una víctima andante. Víctima y victimario. Un país en guerra indefinida : invadiendo el sur del Líbano, ocupando una amplia franja dentro de Siria, capturando más de la mitad de la franja de Gaza, dando rienda suelta a huestes de matones que asaltan a aldeanos en Cisjordania y, por si fuera poco, a la espera del próximo ataque a Irán. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Carlos Bardem, actor y escritor: “No existe un acto de amor más potente que pedir una vida digna para todos”
items.description: Carlos Bardem (Madrid, 63 años) entrega su séptima novela, Triángulo (AdN), un texto que, a través de su protagonista, el misántropo escritor Diego Roca, sumido en un bloqueo creativo, es una impugnación al mundo contemporáneo: la crisis urbana y de vivienda, la amenaza tecnológica, las heridas sin cerrar de la Guerra Civil, la violencia sexual o eso que en Gaza los expertos de la ONU llaman genocidio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La historia de la osa que Ayuso inauguró para una rotonda en Miami y que ha acabado de adorno en un restaurante
items.description: A veces se vende la piel de la osa antes de cazarla. Le pasó a la presidenta de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso , en junio de 2022, durante uno de sus viajes a Miami, cuando posó junto a la escultura de una osa roja que, dijo, acabaría en una rotonda de la gran ciudad del sur de Florida. El proyecto ha quedado literalmente aparcado en el pasillo de un conocido restaurante de Miami, el lugar donde reposa como decorado esa osa con aspecto de golosina. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Rita Catrina: “Nos decían que, cuando se notaran los efectos del cambio climático, estaríamos muertas”
items.description: Rita Catrina se ha acordado mucho este verano de su tío, del río de su infancia y del pequeño pueblo del cantón suizo de los Grisones en el que nació hace 67 años. Trun está a orillas del Rin y tiene poco más de un millar de habitantes. “Para nosotros, el Rin ha sido muy importante, era nuestro lugar de juego, el lugar para hacer senderismo... ha sido nuestra naturaleza”. También era la pista de despegue para que la imaginación de una niña volara lejos, desde los Alpes hasta el mar. “Nuestro tío nos explicaba por dónde iba el Rin cuando salía del pueblo, y nos imaginábamos todos esos lugares y su final, cuando entra en el océano. Era muy bonito”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Hispanidad o latinidad: Shakira abre el debate sobre la identidad cultural más allá del idioma común
items.description: Y dijo Shakira : “No hablemos solo de hispanidad: hablemos de latinidad, un abrazo todavía más amplio. La hispanidad es hermosa, pero se queda corta para todo lo que somos. El español es latino; el portugués, el italiano y el francés también. Y todos los latinoamericanos somos latinos”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sissy Spacek no fue solo una adolescente cubierta de sangre: la vida de amor y tragedia de la protagonista de ‘Carrie’
El recurso habitacional
items.description: Oí decir el 23 de septiembre al alcalde de Madrid que su Ayuntamiento iba a ofrecer un “recurso habitacional” a Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer de 87 años desahuciada de su piso. Y pensé que en ese momento el asunto le importaba un comino. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cuidado con lo que deseas porque puede hacerse realidad
items.description: Debemos mucho a la hipérbole, sobre todo, habernos hecho reír, porque son los cómicos quienes mejor saben utilizar esa herramienta. En manos inexpertas puede ser muy peligrosa y lograr lo contrario a lo que se pretendía. Por ahí iban los tiros de la conversación tuitera tras la intervención este lunes de José María Aznar en unas jornadas sobre la Guerra Civil española. El nombre del expresidente se hizo un hueco en el competitivo listado del trending topic (los temas o tendencias más comentadas en X) después de advertir que si la coalición actual de Gobierno sigue en el poder tras las elecciones de noviembre, el sistema constitucional y la monarquía “se terminan”. “Es evidente”, subrayó. “Lo tiene que saber el ciudadano español: va a votar sobre eso, no sobre una alternancia de Gobierno”. El moderador repreguntó entonces: “¿Quiere decir que iríamos a una república?”. Y en el momento en el que Aznar podía haber admitido que exageraba, decidió tirar hacia adelante: “Absolutamente”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De Sheinbaum a Meloni: las líderes mundiales impulsan medidas para protegerse de los ‘deepfakes’ con IA
items.description: Jefes de Estado y políticos de todo el mundo están impulsando medidas para protegerse de los deepfakes creados con inteligencia artificial. Algunos promueven normativas que abarcan a todos los funcionarios de sus respectivos países. Otros se limitan a aplicar medidas para evitar que se clonen sus voces. Estas disposiciones echan a andar al tiempo que ha trascendido que al menos 46 diputadas del Parlamento Europeo, una de cada seis, han aparecido en imágenes pornog ráficas hiperrealistas pero falsas de pornografía creada con inteligencia artificial, según una investigación de la organización Agora Digitale Transformation, presentada el lunes en el Parlamento Europeo. Una situación “intolerable y deplorable”, ha denunciado presidenta de la Eurocámara, Roberta Metsola, que ha urgido a los Estados miembros que garanticen la aplicación efectiva de las nuevas normas europeas, que actúen contra las aplicaciones que permiten crear este tipo de contenido y que se persiga la difusión de deepfakes sexuales no consentidos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El juez y la fiscal frenan la contraofensiva de Zapatero en sus cuatro primeros meses como imputado
items.description: El magistrado José Luis Calama, instructor del caso Plus Ultra en la Audiencia Nacional, y la fiscal Elena Lorente, de Anticorrupción, han frenado la contraofensiva impulsada por José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero durante sus primeros cuatro meses como imputado . Tanto el juez como la representante del ministerio público han rechazado las peticiones clave planteadas hasta ahora por la defensa del expresidente del Gobierno —desde el intento de anular toda la causa hasta limitar las pesquisas o bloquear una segunda valoración de las joyas incautadas—; y suman críticas contra su actuación. De hecho, en un reciente escrito, la fiscal le reprocha que busque reiteradas “excusas” para tratar de “encubrir su persistente deseo de limitar la actuación judicial”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ceuta, tras los desalojos: limpieza en las playas, menos asentamientos y migrantes escondidos en las barriadas
items.description: Sobre la oscura arena de El Trampolín ya solo quedan algunos montones de basura. Hay una cacerola con restos de comida, una manta rosa, una caja de tarjeta SIM de móvil y una botella de plástico llena de orina. También muchos, muchos restos de las cañas que crecen en los márgenes de las carreteras de Ceuta y que los migrantes usaron para levantar el enorme asentamiento instalado tras la entrada masiva. Dos excavadoras recogen los residuos y los introducen en un camión para ser trasladados al vertedero. En la faena trabaja una veintena de operarios de la limpieza que, entre los 200.000 kilos de desperdicios, ha recuperado un centenar de “aletas” y “trajes de buzo”. Nadie tiene claro si fueron usados para entrar a nado en la ciudad autónoma o si han servido de equipamiento para pescar durante los más de dos meses que el poblado ha vivido su rutina paralela. Y que ha terminado con cientos de “retornos voluntarios” tras ser desalojados por la Policía. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La lucha desesperada por enviar comida con drones a la ciudad ucrania bajo ocupación rusa que se muere de hambre
items.description: “Gracias a nuestros queridos soldados. Os esperamos en nuestra inquebrantable ciudad”, reza una nota manuscrita junto a latas y otros alimentos recibidos para hacer frente al hambre en Oleshki , ciudad ocupada por Rusia. “Gracias”, repite otra junto a un envío de café, infusiones y chocolatinas. Las fotos con estos mensajes y otras con diversas muestras de gratitud han llegado al móvil de Roman Chuhalov, de 44 años, uno de los militares ucranios que, mediante el envío de ayuda con drones, tratan de romper el cerco por la falta de comida en esta localidad de la región meridional de Jersón, en la que sobreviven unas 2.000 personas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Rosalind Franklin sí había visto la hélice: una foto olvidada cambia la historia de la estructura del ADN
items.description: Durante décadas, una de las historias más conocidas de la ciencia se contó como una película. En 1953, con 23 años, James Watson visita el laboratorio de Maurice Wilkins en el King’s College de Londres. Allí, Wilkins le enseña una fotografía de ADN que había tomado Rosalind Franklin y Watson tiene una epifanía. “En cuanto vi la imagen, me quedé boquiabierto y mi pulso empezó a acelerarse”, escribe Watson en La doble hélice: una reseña autobiográfica sobre el descubrimiento del ADN , el libro en el que el científico contó quince años después cómo él y Francis Crick desentrañaron la estructura del ADN. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La mejor estrategia contra las superbacterias: esperar 48 horas para iniciar el antibiótico y solo tomarlo si los síntomas empeoran
items.description: La llamada “prescripción diferida” es un comodín avalado por la evidencia científica, pero muy poco utilizado en España frente al mal uso de los antibióticos y el desarrollo de las superbacterias, responsables de 1,2 millones de muertes al año en el mundo . Esta estrategia consiste en que el médico prescribe el tratamiento al paciente con una infección respiratoria, pero le pide que esté atento a su evolución y espere hasta 72 horas antes de ir a buscarlo a la farmacia y empezar a tomarlo. Si los síntomas remiten en este tiempo —como suele ocurrir con los procesos víricos detrás de la mayoría de las consultas—, se evita tomar un antibiótico innecesario . Si se mantienen o agravan, el paciente ya tiene la receta que necesita sin tener que volver a pedir cita. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Naira depreciates to N1,362/$ in parallel market
items.description: *As interbank turnover rises by 338% By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Naira yesterday depreciated to N1,362 per dollar from N1,357 in the parallel market on Monday. But the naira appreciated to N1,331.5 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira fell to N1,331.5 per dollar from N1,332.9 per dollar on Monday, indicating N1.4 appreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets widened to N30.5 per dollar from N24.1 per dollar on Monday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased sharply by 334.8 percent to $313.6 million from $72.12 million on Monday. The post Naira depreciates to N1,362/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gold edges lower with focus on Fed minutes, rate path clues
items.description: Gold prices slipped on Wednesday as investors looked ‌to minutes from the US Federal Reserve’s September meeting for indications on whether policymakers remain inclined to raise rates further. Spot gold eased 0.3% to $4,150.23 per ounce by 0145 GMT. US gold ​futures edged 0.2% lower to $4,177.60. Minutes of the latest Federal Open Market Committee meeting are ​due later in the day. “The yellow metal is likely to ⁠remain relatively stable with a mild downside bias,” said Frank Walbaum, a market ​analyst at Naga.com. “Minutes will clarify the Fed’s monetary policy and the degree of support ​among policymakers for further rate increases and could reshape upcoming hike odds. Subsequent moves in long-term Treasury yields, the dollar, or oil prices triggered by any Middle East developments would ​then amplify the directional impact (on gold),” Walbaum said. Recent comments from Fed officials underscored ​the US central bank’s commitment to bringing inflation under control. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said whether further ‌rate ⁠hikes are needed depends largely on whether the factors pushing up inflation fade or persist, while Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said rates still need to rise further to bring inflation down. While recent soft economic data has dampened expectations of ​an October rate ​increase, traders still ⁠price in an 85% chance of a hike by December. In a high interest rate environment, investors tend to favour yield-generating assets over ​gold. Separately, delegates attending the London Bullion Market Association’s annual conference in Sorrento, ​Italy, forecast ⁠that gold could reach $5,013 an ounce over the next 12 months. Elsewhere, US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction ⁠in ​its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands ​and end the seven-month war. Spot silver fell roughly 1% to $61.12, platinum rose 0.2% to $1,704.25, while palladium lost ​0.3% to $1,168.20.
