items.title: NAF plane crash: Swampy terrain stalls evacuation of victims, 24 hours after
items.description: ***Navy cordons off crash site By Dayo Johnson, Kingsley Omonobi, Henry Umoru, Joseph Erunke & Ozioruva Aliu AKURE — Swampy and near-inaccessible terrain has stalled evacuation of remains of victims of the Nigerian Air Force plane which crashed at Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State on Monday, more than 24 hours after the crash. The terrain also made it impossible for locals to either help rescue or evacuate victims in the aftermath of the crash of the NAF ATR-42 aircraft. These came as the Nigeria Air Force yesterday released the manifest of the 25 crew and passengers who perished in the crash. Co-pilot of the plane, Squadron Leader Ahamefule Man-Ugwueje, got married in Abuja only two weeks ago. The ATR-42 aircraft, marked NGR 931, is said to be deeply submerged in the swamp, making rescue operations extremely difficult. Sources at the scene said the thick mangroves and murky waters have hampered access to the exact location of the wreckage.Consequently, the black boxes which would be give an indication of what led to the crash are yet to be recovered. Journalists were denied access to the crash site, located about 500 metres east of the Naval Base, which had been cordoned off by the Navy. Some television journalists were arrested by Naval authorities for allegedly accessing the site without clearance. State Police Commissioner, Felix Ohagwu, who described the terrain as very challenging, said: “What happened yesterday (Monday) was quite unfortunate. It is a very difficult terrain — the creeks, mangroves. Accessing the site of the crash was not easy. I had to use a canoe to access it. “I thank the OCA, Marine, and the DPO, Igbokoda, who have been on ground since yesterday (Monday) giving us support. “For now, recovery of the wreckage is still in progress. More technical support is being awaited. We are still expecting a bigger machine to be able to pull the wreckage from the water.” The police boss said the command is awaiting response from the National Emergency Management Agency, NEMA, and other relevant agencies to deploy heavy equipment needed to pull the aircraft wreckage from the swamp. Addressing newsmen in lgbokoda, the Ondo State Health commissioner, Dr Banji Ajaka, said he had been in the forest alongside the Commanding Officer of the FOB, Igbokoda, supervising the operation. Ajaka said personnel and ambulances from hospitals in Ilaje and Okitipupa local Government Areas had been deployed on the directive of Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa. “I have been in the forest with the CO, FOB Igbokoda, for search and rescue operations. I have deployed personnel and ambulances from all hospitals in Ilaje and Okitipupa LGAs as directed by Mr. Governor. “The site is about 500 metres east of the Naval Base. People are just videoing and posting all manner of information far away from the site. I was at the place till around 11 p.m. with local divers and the CO and his men,” Ajaka said. He described the incident as a national tragedy that should not be politicised and urged members of the public to avoid spreading unverified information. “This is a national disaster that we shouldn’t play politics with. Please, let’s tarry and wait for verified information. He added that swamp buggies and other rescue equipment will be deployed to continue the operation early today. The commissioner commended the Commanding Officer of FOB Igbokoda, his men, local divers and medical personnel from the State Specialist Hospital, Okitipupa, General Hospital, Igbokoda, and Comprehensive Health Centre, Igbokoda, for their efforts. We sailed in canoes but couldn’t rescue anyone; wreckage buried in swamp — Locals Also on the difficult terrain, some residents of Igbokoda said though they raced to the crash scene on time, they could not however, access the exact spot of the crash for search and rescue because of the difficult terrain. One of the local divers, who identified himself as Jomiloju, said: “I was trying to have my bath when I heard a loud noise. It was very frightening. I rushed out and met other people in my area who heard the loud sound and equally rushed out of their houses to ascertain what happened. “We rushed towards the direction the sound came from and met many of our people there looking towards the swampy area within the community. We had to sail to the location in canoes to have a glimpse of the crashed plane. “But all we saw was the wreckage. The larger part of the plane was deep inside the swamp. After we discovered that we couldn’t help rescue any of the occupants, we sailed back to the river bank. The naval officers and police also sailed to the location in their speed boats.” Another resident, Lucky, said: “We have tried our best to rescue them but the aircraft was deeply buried inside the swamp. Our people here have tried a lot. Even the women and men took their canoes and crossed to that place to rescue them. We tried our best, but unfortunately we could not help the occupants. They were buried inside the swamp.” Similarly, Bolajoko Ayeni said: “Immediately it happened, there was nothing we could do. We just ran to the place. When we got there, we saw some human parts. Then we just did some videos. We couldn’t rescue anybody because the plane had already entered the swampy area. NEMA activates search team, deploys director, technical team to Igbokoda However, the National Emergency Management Agency, NEMA, has activated a specialised search-and-rescue team to intensify operations, following the crash. NEMA Director-General, Mrs Zubaida Umar, directed the Director of Search and Rescue, Air Commodore Bature Usman, to lead a technical team to the crash location as part of efforts to reinforce ongoing search and recovery operations. The deployment comes as NEMA personnel already at the scene continued to work with other emergency responders involved in the operation. Umar said the agency’s intervention is aimed at strengthening coordination and providing additional technical and operational support to the teams responding to the incident. She commended the prompt activation of search-and-rescue operations and reaffirmed NEMA’s readiness to deploy the necessary resources to support the ongoing response. The NEMA chief also expressed deep sadness over the incident, describing it as a painful loss to the nation and acknowledged the sacrifices made by Nigerian Air Force personnel in the service and defence of the country. Air Force releases names of officers, civilians killed in NAF plane crash While the search and rescue efforts are ongoing, the Nigerian Airforce yesterday released the names of the 25 souls onboard the ill-fated plane. They included five crew member and 20 passengers, comprising military officers, Non-Commissioned officers and some family members. According to the manifest released in a statement by Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, spokesman of NAF, the crew included Squadron Leader MI Aburime (Flight Captain); Squadron Leader AP Man-Ugwueje (Co-pilot); Flight Lieutenant IS Bako (Co-pilot); Warrant Officer Abubakar A (Aircraft Technician); and Corporal Uguru HC (Aircraft Technician). The 20 passengers onboard were Flight Lieutenant TL Lazarus; Flight Lieutenant M Akinloye; Flying Officer IM Adeshina; Master Warrant Officer Onwuka F; Master Warrant Officer Matini BA; Warrant Officer Nuhu FS; Flight Sergeant James RB; Flight Sergeant Mohammed AI; and Sergeant Ani AE. Others were Sergeant Izibenikien SI; Sergeant Alafuka C; Sergeant Mbadugha AN; Lance Corporal Ugwuba FC; Lance Corporal Eledan GE; Mrs Ezeh Nneka; Godstmine Tarabina; Joy Michael; Sunday Michael; Ukeme David; and Gideon Omotola. The statement read: “The Chief of the Air Staff, CAS, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has expressed profound condolences to the families of the personnel and passengers who lost their lives following the accident involving Nigerian Air Force, NAF, ATR 42 aircraft, NAF 931, in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State. “The CAS described the incident as a deeply painful moment for the Nigerian Air Force and the nation, expressing heartfelt sympathies to the families, loved ones and colleagues of those who lost their lives. He assured the bereaved families of the Service’s full support during this difficult period. “NAF 931 had 25 persons on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred. Search-and-rescue procedures were immediately activated, with response efforts conducted in coordination with relevant authorities to locate and account for all persons on board. “No survivors have been found. CAS has directed a comprehensive investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. “The Nigerian Air Force will continue to provide timely and verified updates as the investigation progresses and urges the public to refrain from speculation and the circulation of unverified information, while respecting the privacy and dignity of the affected families. “A condolence register has also been opened at Headquarters Nigerian Air Force, Abuja, for senior government officials, members of the diplomatic corps, heads of security agencies, and other well-wishers who may wish to pay their respects and convey messages of sympathy to the families of the deceased and the Nigerian Air Force.” Pilot of crashed plane, Masters student of UNIBEN Also, many post-graduate students of the Department of Mass Communication, University of Benin were in sober mood yesterday when they heard that the pilot of the ill-fated Air Force plane was a Masters student of the department. It was gathered that he was in school last Friday for a make-up test by one of their lecturers. His Class Representative, Desmond Odiah, described him as a gentle student who, despite his busy schedules, always found time to attend classes. “We were currently doing our Masters together, but we actually started from Post-graduate diploma. We did PGD together for one year and after the results, we went for Masters together too. “I became closer to him when I became the Class Rep for the Master’s programme. He was always reaching out to me privately about classes, anything that has to do with academics. “He didn’t have issues. Every single time he was in the class, he was always at the back with his cap on. So he was a perfect gentleman that didn’t want issues, didn’t want any problems. “Regardless of his tedious work and responsibility, he was able to try as much as possible to attend classes. He was even around on Friday for a makeup test. “I actually reached out to him about the test, so that was the last time we spoke. He told me he was in school already for the makeup test. He was somebody who believed in due process,’’ Odiah said. Co-pilot wedded 2 weeks ago in Abuja Vanguard gathered yesterday that one of the co-pilots who flew the crashed plane, Squadron Leader Ahamefule Man-Ugwueje, got married to Flight Lieutenant Damilola Adekunle only two weeks ago in Abuja. A Squadron Leader in the Nigerian Air Force is equivalent in rank to a Major in the Nigerian Army. He is survived by his young wife, parents, and family. According to information on his Facebook profile, Man-Ugwueje’s home town is listed as Umuahia, Abia State, while Abuja is listed as his current town/city. Crash victim visited mother to wish her birthday before trip It was also learned that one of the victims of the crash, Flight Lieutenant M. Akintoye, reportedly visited her mother whose birthday was yesterday and informed her that they were on their way to Lagos and that turned out to be their last encounter. Vanguard gathered that his mother, Professor Emily Akintoye, is a staff of Benson Idahosa University in Benin City. Flags flew at half mast at the Air Force Military base and at the Air Force Military Hospital in Benin yesterday. A source close to the family said: “They were coming from a programme and stopped over in Benin City. Tuesday (yesterday) being the birthday of his mother, he rushed to the house in one of their Air Force vehicles to wish her happy birthday and informed her that they were on their way to Lagos. A few hours after, news of the disaster came. “Everybody is devastated, including senior officers because of the number of personnel involved in the disaster. His mother is in distress obviously and it is a bad day to celebrate birthday. “This is something that would be with her for life that whenever it is her birthday, she will remember the tragic death of her son,” the source said. DHQ begins investigations Meanwhile, Defence headquarters has begun investigation into the crash, even as it extended heartfelt condolences to the families and loved ones of all persons involved in the unfortunate air mishap. Major General Samaila Uba, Director of Defence Information, who disclosed this in a statement, said: “The Defence Headquarters has received with deep shock the news of the unfortunate crash of a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft near the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ondo State. “The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos with military personnel and some members of families on board. “On behalf of the Armed Forces of Nigeria, the Defence Headquarters wishes to extend heartfelt condolences to the families and loved ones of all persons involved, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Nigerian Air Force, NAF, and the entire Armed Forces family. “This is, indeed, a painful loss to the entire Armed Forces and the nation at large. Our personnel give their all daily to keep Nigeria safe. Their courage and sacrifices will never be forgotten. “In compliance with the directive of the Commander-in-Chief, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, investigation will be conducted to ascertain the cause of the accident, while Search and Rescue efforts by the NAF, in collaboration with sister services and emergency agencies, continue at the site. “The leadership of the Armed Forces wishes to assure all Nigerians that the Armed Forces will remain resolute and committed to our constitutional mandate of securing the nation, despite this painful setback. “The sacrifice of our fallen heroes will continue to inspire our service to the nation. We appeal to the general public to refrain from speculations and to respect the privacy of the families affected in this difficult moment while official procedures continue. “May the souls of the departed rest in perfect peace, and may God grant their families the strength to bear this profound loss.” Senate postpones National Security Summit Following the crash, the Senate yesterday postponed its planned two-day National Security Summit earlier scheduled for Monday, October 12 and Tuesday, October 13, 2026, until further notice. In a statement he personally signed yesterday, Leader of the Senate and Chairman, Senate Ad hoc Committee on the National Security Summit, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), said a new date for the summit will be communicated in due course, and appealed to all stakeholders to take note of the national disaster and bear with the Senate during this period of national mourning. Recall that the Senate had convened the security summit to review the country’s perennial security challenges and propose pragmatic solutions that could guarantee security of lives and property across the federation. According to Bamidele, the ad-hoc committee had already concluded plans to hold the summit after completion of zonal public hearings. He noted that the crash of the NAF plane suddenly necessitated the postponement of the national security summit earlier scheduled for Monday. FG won’t abandon bereaved families, says Shettima In his response to the crash, Vice President Kashim Shettima yesterday assured families of victims of the crash that the Federal Government’s responsibility to them “will not end with words of condolence.” In a statement signed by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communications, Stanley Nkwocha, Shettima said the nation owed an “enduring debt of gratitude” to the fallen personnel and would stand beside their families beyond the period of mourning. He said: “Thirty-two of our compatriots left on a routine mission in the service of their country. They were colleagues, friends and comrades. But beyond the uniforms they wore and the ranks they held, they were husbands and wives, fathers and mothers, sons and daughters, brothers and sisters. “Somewhere today, there is an empty chair. Somewhere, a family is still trying to comprehend the sudden silence left by someone who was expected to return home. These are the human faces of the supreme sacrifice we speak about as a nation.” Shettima reasoned that a nation that asked its citizens to serve “must also remember those who pay the ultimate price in that service.” He said the loss imposed a lasting obligation on the country to honour both the service of the deceased and the loved ones they left behind. “We cannot ask the bereaved to be strong today. Grief does not obey instructions. We can only assure them that Nigeria remembers, Nigeria mourns with them, and Nigeria will stand beside them beyond these days of mourning,” Shettima noted. He extended his condolences to officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force, saying the tragedy had taken from the service members of “a professional family bound together by duty and sacrifice.” He said: “To the men and women of the Nigerian Air Force, we know that this loss is yours in a particularly personal way. “Your fallen colleagues have paid the supreme price. A grateful nation honours their courage, their service and the families who shared them with Nigeria.’’ The Vice President prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased, and for comfort and strength for their families, colleagues and loved ones. He also reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s response to the tragedy. The post NAF plane crash: Swampy terrain stalls evacuation of victims, 24 hours after appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Situationer: THE LONG ROAD TO ATTOCK
items.description: A roughly two-hour drive east from Peshawar brings us to Attock, on the banks of the Indus. On the Punjab side, the inescapable Att­o­ck fortress, an imposing 16th century structure, dominates the relative lowlands of Khairabad in Khyber Pakh­tun­khwa’s Nows­hera district — the venue of PTI’s renewed campaign to secure the release of their jailed leader, or at the very least seek some relief for him. Connecting the two provinces via the N-5 — or Grand Trunk Road of yore — is the 701-metre new bridge at Khairabad, which sits not too far from its 119-year-old two-tiered steel truss road bridge that is now abandoned. It is here that the PTI wants to converge its protest march, which began in Gandi Chowk, Lakki Marwat on October 4. Here, things are bound to get interesting. Consider the route of the march first; the participants will reach the southern fringes of Peshawar’s Mattani by Tuesday night and stay overnight before resuming their march via the Ring Road. From there, they plan to take the M-1 motorway and continue all the way to Swabi — the last district adjoining Punjab. In leading the protest march, Sohail Afridi has taken perhaps the biggest risk of his political career. When it comes time to pay the piper, he may yet find himself standing alone at Khairabad Here, the marchers plan to exit the motorway and continue towards Khairabad via the Swabi-Jehangira Road. At least, that’s the plan so far. But no one has been able to explain why the organisers plan to take such a circuitous route, switching from the motorway to GT Road, when all they would have to do is cross the M1 bridge over the Indus and enter Punjab? What could possibly be the strategic reason for this switch? There are many theories and speculation abounds, but no one, not even some key party figures, have a definitive answer. That is unless, of course, they want to keep their cards close to their chest. Crossing the Rubicon At least two senior figures in Islamabad have told Dawn that in principle, the decision to proclaim a state of emergency in KP has been taken. However, whether it comes to pass or not depends entirely on whether the PTI march attempts to force its way into Islamabad. All those who ‘need to know’ have been conveyed the consequences of forced entry into Islamabad, and its fallout, in no uncertain terms. Could this, and the Islamabad High Court ruling, be the reason for the diversion from M-1 to GT Road? Speak to any party figure and they would tell you that they do not plan to put up any resistance or resort to violence to push their way through walls of steel containers. No slingshots, no nailed sticks, let alone any firearms. “We will be at our peaceful best,” commented one lawmaker. This is mainly why the planners have decided to take this long detour — exit at the Swabi Interchange on M-1 to bypass Nowshera cantonment, which lies astride the GT Road — to avoid any direct contact. So what is the endgame for the PTI protest march? Will it funnel through the lines of containers on Khairabad Bridge to confront and clash with riot police waiting on the other side of the Indus? Or, will the participants camp in the plains of Khairabad on the KP side, and continue their protest in a peaceful manner? If so, then how long will they be able to keep it up? Will it even be logistically possible for them to sustain a sit-in, notwithstanding the implication of economic fallout for the people of KP, much of whose fuel and food comes via the GT Road? No one seems to have an explanation, unless of course, this is a deliberate deflection tactic. In the words of a senior party lawmaker, ‘war-gaming’ is not in the PTI’s DNA, but there is still some hope within the senior political leadership that despite the deadlock and the breakdown of negotiations in Islamabad, things can still be sorted out through dialogue. Hence the long detour, to drag things out and delay ‘D-Day’ for as long as possible. The possible political fallout In the absence of a charismatic leader to mobilise and lead the march, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has clearly emerged as the party’s new poster boy. But at 37 years of age, with little political experience and surrounded by a council of so-called ‘wise men’ with no real political authority — including the party’s political committee — the firebrand former student leader also runs grave risks to his political career. Losing his office through a possible disqualification case before the Election Commission of Pakistan, currently stayed by the Peshawar High Court, or through a pending petition filed by Sher Afzal Marwat before Federal Constitutional Court, are the two likely scenarios. But even some senior party figures privately concede that by taking responsibility for leading the march, Sohail Afridi has taken perhaps the biggest risk of his political career. If he is able to pull it off, i.e. bring the federal government to its knees and extract major concessions for his jailed party leader, he would emerge as the undisputed leader of the PTI. But while success will have many fathers, failure is an orphan; failing to achieve any of the stated goals of this march will have its implications. And when it comes time to pay the piper, Afridi may yet find himself standing alone at Khairabad. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Oil prices rise as storms and air strikes threaten supply
items.description: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of ​Middle East crude. Brent futures rose 93 cents, or 0.92%, to $101.51 a barrel by 0022 GMT. ‌US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 82 cents, or 0.92%, to $90.25. US forecasters said on Tuesday a storm forming in the Gulf of Mexico would become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days and would likely hit oil and gas producing facilities. The offshore ​areas in the Gulf in the storm’s path produce 15% of US crude oil and 5% ​of the country’s natural gas. KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said the storm was an “unwelcome ⁠complication for crude, raising the prospect of production and refining disruptions at a time when the market ​already has enough supply-side headaches”. The storm could affect six refineries. Refineries in US Gulf states account for about 50% of ​the national capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd). US crude oil and gasoline inventories fell, while distillate stocks rose marginally last week, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ended ​October 2. Supply had been rising as the East-West pipeline hit 5.8 million barrels a day, according to Saudi ​Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman on Tuesday. Around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of ‌refined products ⁠were leaving the Middle East on tankers in the last 7 to 10 days, the head of Vitol said . However, Saudi Arabia’s airports in Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, the Saudi aviation authority said , as hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis escalated. The attacks occurred as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pressed a ​major offensive to retake territory ​from the Houthis, after ⁠weeks of rebel advances, with Riyadh stepping up airstrikes in support of the campaign. Attacks and refinery outages are “likely to keep the cracks elevated and scarcity will transmit to ​crude. Prices will stay elevated near a $100 level without any material de-escalation emerging,” ​said Mukesh Sahdev, ⁠chief oil analyst at X Analysts in Sydney. US-Iran relations are no closer to repair with US President Donald Trump saying on Tuesday that nobody knew who was running Iran during the eight-month US-Israeli war with Iran. “Their leaders are gone, their ⁠second group ​of leaders are gone, and the biggest problem I have is ​nobody knows who the hell is running the country,” Trump said. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman said on Sunday Washington knows very well who their ​counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in Iran works.

items.title: Israel razes five-storey building in Jerusalem without warning
items.description: • Ben Gvir ‘gleefully’ drives bulldozer at demolition site; residents not even allowed to gather belongings • Settlers attack photojournalists in occupied West Bank JERUSALEM: Israeli bulldozers on Tuesday demolished a five-storey residential building in annexed east Jerusalem, which was home to about 70 people, in a move the local Palestinian authority said was aimed at “forcible transfer”. Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, who gleefully oversaw the demolition, said the building had been constructed without a permit. “I love hearing this noise. We demolish what is illegal,” Ben Gvir said in a video posted on X, which showed him inside the cab of one of the bulldozers. Densely populated east Jerusalem faces a severe housing crisis, with thousands of homes built without permits, which its Palestinian residents say are near impossible to obtain from Israeli authorities. The Jerusalem Governorate, the Palestinian local authority for the area, condemned Tuesday’s demolition which it said was “a dangerous escalation in the policy of home demolitions and forcible transfer… and the imposition of a new demographic and urban reality”. Hanine Hreibat, a teacher and mother of four who was renting one of the 10 apartments in the building, said a large Israeli police force arrived in the At-Tur neighbourhood in the early hours of the morning, accompanied by three bulldozers. They stormed the apartments and gave residents 10 minutes to leave, she said. Hreibat told AFP she had woken up to the sound of her husband shouting at the police, asking them not to enter the bedroom where she was, adding she had endured “five minutes of terror, with weapons pointed at our heads”. She said police officers had allowed her to take only medicine, money, her handbag and ID card. Among the rubble, residents collected gas cylinders and filled plastic bags with clothes they had managed to pull out from the huge mound of debris. Hreibat said she had nowhere to go following the demolition. “We’ll look for a second home. Today we’re at my in-laws’ and tomorrow at my parents’,” she said. Settlers attack photojournalists Also on Tuesday, Israeli settlers beat a photojournalist and fired in his direction during coverage of ongoing settler violence against West Bank olive farmers. Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, a veteran photographer for the AFP news agency in the Palestinian territory, suffered bruises to his head and torso and was taken by ambulance to a hospital. Ashtiyeh and another AFP photographer, John Wessels, were near the northern village of Aqraba where they noticed an Israeli soldier detaining a man as local Palestinians picked olives. A quad bike suddenly raced towards the photojournalists on top of the hill and a man from it opened live fire, with one Palestinian dropping to the ground. He was also hospitalised, with a gunshot to the foot, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society. At least six other people then rushed towards the AFP personnel, firing guns. As Ashtiyeh attempted to enter a car, two men jumped on him and beat him repeatedly with guns. Ashtiyeh, who is Palestinian, is conscious and under 24-hour supervision at a hospital in Nablus, where he will undergo X-rays, said his son, Zain Jaafar. The assailants also took his camera equipment, Wessels said. The violence took place despite the presence of at least a dozen fully equipped Israeli soldiers around 500 metres away. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo opens door for Portugal return, apologises for walk-out
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed his continued availability for Portugal after explaining his decision to leave the national team camp and accusing head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking an agreement over his playing time. The 41-year-old Al Nassr forward had raised questions about his international future following his departure from the squad, but said he remained committed to representing Portugal. “If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,” Ronaldo said in a statement shared with Reuters. Ronaldo also apologised to his teammates and the Portuguese public for leaving the camp, adding that he would accept any disciplinary action imposed by the Portuguese Football Federation. The forward left the squad after remaining an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2-1 away victory over Norway in the Nations League on September 27. According to Ronaldo, he and Jesus had previously agreed that he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches as part of a plan to manage his fitness. However, Ronaldo said the coach changed the arrangement on the day of the Norway match and told him he would play for 30 minutes. “Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” he said. “The manager had broken his word to me.” Ronaldo said it was the second time he believed Jesus had failed to honour an understanding between them and that the coach’s public comments did not correspond with their private discussion. “It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises,” he said. Jesus, however, denied after Portugal’s victory over Norway that he had reached such an agreement with Ronaldo, while leaving the door open for the veteran forward to return to the national team. Ronaldo also rejected suggestions that he had interfered with tactical or technical decisions during his international career. “Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career,” he said. “I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.” Addressing speculation about a possible farewell to international football, Ronaldo said he expected to have one or more farewell matches in the future but remained focused on competing for Portugal. “I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that. But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing,” he said. Ronaldo, Portugal’s record goalscorer and most-capped player, has scored 146 goals in 234 international appearances. He also recalled remaining with the Portugal squad following the death of his father during an international camp, saying his commitment to the national team had remained strong throughout his career. The dispute between Ronaldo and Jesus has cast uncertainty over the forward’s immediate international involvement, but his latest statement makes clear that he intends to remain available for Portugal, subject to his fitness and any disciplinary sanction. The post Cristiano Ronaldo opens door for Portugal return, apologises for walk-out appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Messi se despide de la selección argentina ovacionado por una multitud: “Es el día más triste de mi carrera”
items.description: “El último tango”, repetían los carteles electrónicos del estadio. Los más de 85.000 espectadores que llenaban el Monumental, en Buenos Aires, los millones que miraban por televisión desde tantos otros lugares del país y del mundo, sabían que esa imagen que se hizo costumbre durante 21 años ya no se repetiría: Lionel Messi pisaba el césped con la Albiceleste, con los colores que hizo brillar. Desde el primer minuto del juego que enfrentó a Argentina con Benín, la nostalgia de lo que pasó y no volverá merodeaba las tribunas repletas. Pero sin el lamento tanguero de lo que pudo ser y no fue, porque en su carrera Messi hizo posible lo imposible , cosechó todos los trofeos y batió todos los récords con el celeste y el blanco, más partidos jugados, más goles marcados, más asistencias entregadas… Por eso, por una vez, el tango compartió su tristeza por la despedida con la alegría de una multitud agradecida que celebró a su héroe del fútbol. items.title: Maroc-France: Une forte volonté politique de promouvoir un partenariat culturel
items.description: L'ambassadeur de France au Maroc, Philippe Lalliot, a affirmé, mardi à Rabat, l'existence d'une forte volonté politique visant à insuffler une nouvelle dynamique au partenariat culturel maroco-français, portée par la vitalité de la scène culturelle et l'énergie créative des jeunes dans les deux pays. S'exprimant lors de la cérémonie de lancement de la nouvelle saison culturelle de l'Institut français du Maroc, Lalliot a souligné que la coopération culturelle est appelée à constituer un levier majeur pour dynamiser l'ensemble des volets de la coopération bilatérale. Devant un parterre de figures de la culture, des arts et des médias, Lalliot a indiqué que la nouvelle saison 2026-2027 place les jeunes au centre de sa programmation, notant que cette édition propose des initiatives novatrices visant à les immerger dans la création culturelle bilatérale et à les associer aux réflexions sur les enjeux de leur avenir. L’ambassadeur s’est, en outre, réjoui que cette nouvelle saison représente ce que la France et le Maroc savent faire de mieux lorsqu'ils unissent leurs talents, leurs langues, leur créativité et leurs imaginaires. Lalliot, qui a salué la dynamique de la scène artistique marocaine et la richesse de son patrimoine, a présenté les trois axes prioritaires appelés à structurer la programmation de cette nouvelle saison. La première priorité porte sur la promotion du dialogue des langues et des imaginaires à travers le programme « Jossour », dédié au soutien à la traduction entre l’arabe et le français, en partenariat avec le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication. La deuxième s'attache à encourager les synergies entre les jeunes talents des deux pays, via l’accompagnement de projets artistiques émergents (musique, arts plastiques, danse, théâtre) et l'appui à l’essor des industries culturelles et créatives (ICC). Quant à la troisième priorité, a-t-il poursuivi, elle vise à étendre la programmation culturelle aux différentes régions du Royaume pour en apprécier la diversité, aller à la rencontre d’un public pluriel et interagir avec une jeunesse avide de culture, en dynamisant le rôle des antennes de l’Institut français et de l’Alliance française. The post Maroc-France: Une forte volonté politique de promouvoir un partenariat culturel appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: A case for the “Igbo ranch”, by Ochereome Nnanna
items.description: This is a necessary sequel to my article last week titled: “Owo Ranch: Attention, Gov. Peter Mbah!” You may have, like me, wondered why Governor Mbah would carve out over 10,000 hectares for the ranch project at his hometown, Owo, in Nkanu East LGA of Enugu State. Since his government has remained mute on the many issues surrounding the project, we are free to speculate. If he actually intends it for corporate, professional ranching, all I need to add is that he should ensure that the youths of Enugu State are strong stakeholders for their ownership, empowerment, and security. But if he has Fulani herdsmen in mind to appease the Sultan of Sokoto, it will be the greatest sell-out of all time. He would be creating a colony for ISWAP jihadists, who sometimes masquerade as Fulani herdsmen and bandits to target non-Muslim areas like the Middle Belt, South East, South-South, and Christian-majority South West states, Ondo and Ekiti. Mbah’s unacceptable “peace” gesture to the sultan has given rise to the thinking that the Owo Ranch is part of the “peace” offering to the chief jihadist of Nigeria. This speculation is not far-fetched. Some Igbo politicians believe that their political ambitions are greatly enhanced when they prostitute themselves to Fulani interests. Mbah is very ambitious beyond his quest for a second term. Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s sickening theatrical displays against Peter Obi are linked to post-gubernatorial ambitions of being considered as Vice President to the next President from the North. Mbah could also be eyeing the same thing, what with his rising profile as a top performer. It was the same motivation that pushed Senator Orji Uzor Kalu who, as governor of Abia State, gave away a huge parcel of land in Lokpanta, Abia State, to northerners. They went on not only to turn the place into a Northern city; it also became an arena of barbaric crimes such as kidnapping for ransom and the slaughtering of victims, mostly travellers and abducted locals. It took Governor Alex Otti to neutralise that crime scene. During Muhammadu Buhari’s regime, the killings in that axis were officially attributed to IPOB and ESN. It is a well-established fact that many Igbo politicians are ready to sell or even sacrifice their mothers on the altars of their political ambitions. I am not accusing Governor Mbah of selling out Owo, Enugu, and the Igbo people to Fulani jihadist expansionists for ambition. I am only hoping aloud that he does not do so. These articles serve to call for vigilance to ensure that the Owo Ranch project remains strictly for ranching, and not a giveaway for a Fulani Ruga. We all (not just Enugu people) must strongly resist any attempt to invite our violent, sworn enemies to take their place among us. After last week’s article came out, a friend and colleague from Enugu State wrote to me and opined that Gov. Mbah should scrap the ranch project and instead convert it to a farm estate for the cultivation of crops. Mbah’s administration already has a robust vision for agriculture, of which the ranch is a part. I am not opposed to the ranch per se. We in the East need them, for several reasons. Our years of dependence on the North for food have imposed an existential threat on us. The jihadists in the North have devised many insidious strategies to poison and rapidly depopulate the South, especially the Christian-majority Eastern Region. Almost every food item produced in the far North, especially beans, fish, and fruits, is poisoned with dangerous insecticides, particularly the killer poison known as “Sniper”, before they are trucked down to Southern markets. Some fruits are deliberately injected and sold to unsuspecting consumers. Those who do this either do it for profit or as part of their demonic religious agenda. There are countless stories of how some herdsmen have sex with their animals, which are later slaughtered in abattoirs and sold to unsuspecting buyers. Most of them were born and raised in the bush and have little to zero exposure to ethics of any sort. It is high time that Southerners, and the Igbo in particular, retook full control of their agricultural resources. We must encourage our youths to abandon urban poverty and return to farm the land and practise animal husbandry as we used to do before the Civil War. We have our local varieties of goats, chicken, cows, peppers, tomatoes, groundnuts, and fruits, which are even more delicious and nutritious than their Sahel counterparts. If we cultivate our lands with modern farming techniques, we will end food dependence on the North. We have arable land in abundance. Indeed, with the Chinese now given free entry to dump their cheap goods on us by direct retail, agriculture offers a viable alternative. The massive involvement of our youths in agriculture will come with many benefits. One of them is the full control of our security. Over 50 years of rural–urban drift created a lot of ungoverned spaces which the herdsmen and their armed kinsmen, the jihadists, now occupy and with which they threaten our communities, with very little challenge. We must change that situation. We must reclaim our lands and prosper from them. Only fools depend on their self-sworn enemies for their food supply. When we return to our land, we will be able to restore our genuine culture, not the fake occult trends that fraudsters now peddle as Omenala. We will ranch with improved varieties of livestock on an industrial scale. This will include breeding the dwarf native Muturu cows, which give organic prestige to the Ogbuefi title. You cannot kill a long-legged Sahel N’dama cow and call yourself Ogbuefi. People are only doing it because of the scarcity of the right kind of cow. It is scarce because we abandoned breeding it. Let us bring Igbo ingenuity into the livestock business, and show them how it’s done! The post A case for the “Igbo ranch”, by Ochereome Nnanna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘How can an office…close at 5pm?’ – Abanga questions 24-Hour Economy
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fusani Yakubu, has questioned the implementation of the government’s 24-hour economy policy. He said the policy raises questions when an office expected to regulate its implementation closes at 5pm. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Mr Abanga challenged the government to explain how businesses operating late into the night will be monitored. “Right. They promise a 24-hour economy, and the 24-hour economy, which even the office itself closes at 5 p.m. How can an office that is meant to regulate an office that is supposed to operate 24 hours close at 5 p.m.?” he asked. He questioned who would monitor businesses operating during the night. “Who is going to monitor the rest of the people that be working at dawn, at 2 a.m., at 12 midnight and stuff?” he asked. Mr Abanga accused the government of misleading Ghanaians over its policies. “These are all scam lies that they lie to the Ghanaian people,” he said. He also accused the government of using social media to undermine the record of the previous NPP administration. “They use social media to sway away from the good policies and initiatives ex-President Akufo-Addo, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia did for this country by propagating lies and fake propaganda,” he said. Mr Abanga further cited fuel prices as part of his criticism of the government. “Yet today we can’t buy fuel. Prices of fuel have gone up GH¢20 and above,” he said. He also raised concerns about the decline in cocoa prices, comparing the current price to what he said was paid under the previous administration. “My father is a go-go farmer. My mom is a cocoa farmer,” he said. “As I go further, Dr Mahmoud Baomia was buying cocoa for 3100 Ghana cedis. Today, cocoa prices have gone down. Now they are buying cocoa for GH¢2000.” Mr Abanga rejected explanations based on changes in global cocoa prices, arguing that such factors were known when the promises were made. “They should not even mention anything about global prices. I don’t want to hear that, but they knew there was something called global prices whilst they made those promises,” he said. He said the NPP must now intensify its grassroots campaign ahead of the 2028 elections. “It requires hard work. It requires sacrifice. It requires getting the right people on the ground to get the job done,” he said. Mr Abanga said he would personally lead the party’s youth mobilisation effort across the country. “I’ll be moving. I promise them I’m not going to be an armchair National Youth Organiser. I’ll be joining them in their various regions, constituencies very soon,” he said. He said the ultimate goal was to mobilise enough support for former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia to win the 2028 election. “It’s the only solution for this country,” he said.

items.title: Time for Digital Connectivity? By Okoh Aihe
items.description: The way forward looks much clearer now. This is no time for semantics and big talks or even prevarications and over-reliance on legacy achievements of an industry that recorded exponential service deployment in over two decades. The time has come for the next level of growth to address the challenges of the industry and meet the ever-mounting service demands by the subscribers. The new field, according to Dr Aminu Maida, EVC of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), is digital connectivity, which is what matters to a trader waiting for payment transactions to go through, to the student joining an online class or even the businessman serving customers across the country. They all need a digital connection at that time. He noted that as cloud services and artificial intelligence become more widely used, dependence on digital connectivity will deepen. Is connectivity simply replacing inclusivity? Last week, a stellar cast of characters gathered in Abuja for the Nigeria Connectivity Investment Forum to address the subject of digital connectivity without emotions and with all their knowledge, to proffer bold solutions on how best to enhance connectivity in the country and release a fresh burst of service provisioning, creativity and usage in the telecom ecosystem. After two days of detailed deliberations, the forum came to some audacious decisions and resolutions, even giving timelines to meet some targets set for the industry while portioning out responsibilities to the various stakeholders. Drawn from government and the various industries to discuss the theme, Unlocking Infrastructure Investment through Data, Transparency and Partnerships, participants included: Dr Jumoke Oduwole, Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment; Dr Bosun Tijani, Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, who was represented; Bolaji Balogun, Chief Executive Officer of Chapel Hill Denham, who provided an investor’s perspective on Financing Digital Infrastructure; and Bismarck Rewane, Chairman of the Board of FCMB and Managing Director of Financial Directives Company, who provided insights on the broader economic and financial environment for infrastructure investment. The forum also enjoyed the support and participation of Swedfund and Ookla, credited with providing independent evidence which reduces investor uncertainty in the nation’s telecom industry, and Ericsson, which, in a presentation, suggested sundry rollout possibilities to manage cost, declaring that investment logic demands that “the decision is not more technology – it is the right coverage model for the investment need.” Looking at Connectivity to Economic Value, GSMA said, “Africa’s biggest connectivity challenge is now usage, not coverage.” The problem, however, is that connectivity has to happen for usage to follow. A little recall may be needed here. Balogun was a pioneer founder of Econet, which today operates as Airtel, and is roundly equipped with all needed information from the telecom industry as well as the financial sector. He said in his presentation that “one hand cannot tie a bundle,” so funding in the industry would always demand partnership. Rewane maintained a profound voice in finances and investment and, only last week, simply ridiculed the nation’s energy capacity, which hardly rises above 5,000 megawatts of electricity for a nation of about 230 million people. He would always speak truth to every situation, and this is just one of them. It may serve our interests to take a closer look at the effect of such energy provision on digital connectivity. After two days of information download and digestion, the forum came to some hard observations, which are stated in a communique as follows: Demand is outgrowing the networks – Nigeria consumed about 1.6 million terabytes of data in July 2026, an increase of almost 47 percent in twelve months, and subscriptions are projected to grow from about 195 million towards 350 million within ten to fifteen years. Cloud computing and artificial intelligence will place further demand on networks, data centers and, above all, power; Digital Connectivity is economic infrastructure – Telecommunications and information services accounted for 9.72 percent of Nigeria’s real GDP in the second quarter of 2026, and mobile contributed about $240 billion to Africa’s economy in 2025; Usage, rather than coverage, is now the larger gap – Mobile broadband covers about 90 percent of Nigerians, yet smartphone ownership stands at about 27 percent and broadband penetration is at 57 percent against a 70 percent target. Device affordability, digital skills and trust are the binding constraints, and coverage investment alone cannot close them. The forum therefore made the following calls: The Federal Government should accelerate the delivery of Project BRIDGE, the 90,000 km national fibre backbone; The Nigerian Communications Commission should sustain the reforms already improving investment conditions; State Governments should cut and harmonise Right of Way and site permit charges; Operators, infrastructure and technology companies should pursue shared-infrastructure and neutral-host models that lower cost of rural and indoor coverage; and Investors and development finance institutions should match long-life assets with long-tenor naira capital. A novel outcome of the forum is that it also released Priority Actions and Partnership Pathways, which had timelines of various actions and who should take them. For instance, it says, within six months: secure funding for community co-owned rural networks powered by renewable energy in zero-connectivity communities, through partnership with the Universal Service Provision Fund, State governments and the Rural Electricity Agency. There are other timelines. While I am not too excited about the outcome of the Forum, which, some participants say, was a resounding success, I want to observe here that the real outcomes will start to count when we begin to measure the deliverables by their timelines. The forum has set the targets. Even as I credit them for their bold decisions, I want to state here very clearly that we shall judge them by the targets they have set for themselves. The post Time for Digital Connectivity? By Okoh Aihe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: When adult petulance becomes a campaign strategy, by Rotimi Fasan
items.description: Considering the reaction of the main opposition parties’ leaders to the Independence Day speech of President Bola Tinubu, I think I’m beginning to see the lineaments of the campaign for the 2027 general election. The shape the campaigns would take is getting clear. This is why I’m returning once again to a theme I have pursued in this space and on which I have commented at least twice in the last five weeks or thereabouts. I’m talking about the nature of the 2027 presidential campaign. While the energy (so far low-key) brought to it may be different, what may not be different is the quality of the debates, which is not likely to be elevated. The leading opposition candidates seeking to unseat the president do not look ready to stay on message. That’s if they have any message other than the ad hominem utterances they retail to their followers. I have mentioned the opposition candidates not so much because I believe the next election would be a coronation for the president or that the party in power has no need to justify its programme. It is rather because it is the opposition that is at this point claiming to sell an alternative vision and offering change to the people. The ruling party can stay on its Renewed Hope agenda and simply continue to call attention to the milestones it believes it has achieved in three and a half years. And that was precisely what the president did in his Independence Day address by itemising the highlights of his administration’s programme and explaining to Nigerians how we got to the position where we are right now, with the key reforms of removing the subsidy on petrol, unifying the foreign exchange market, and enabling the floatation of the naira. These are the steps that have headlined the activities of the Tinubu administration since it came into office. They are the culprits Nigerians have held responsible for their immiseration and the parlous state of the economy. These policies are, not surprisingly, the target of the opposition leaders, who have in their different ways vowed to roll them back. Since they must posture as people who know the essence of politics, the address they gave in response to the president’s speech is much in line with democratic practices elsewhere. It is what the rebuttal speech of opposition parties’ leaders to the State of the Union address of an American president is all about. It is a practice that dates back to the 1960s. In the Nigerian case, one of the opposition leaders said outright that he would restore the subsidy on petrol and was only forced to clarify (split hairs is more like what he did) his position days later when Nigerians questioned the practicality of his plan. It was then that he qualified his claim and restricted his planned subsidy restoration to a so-called production side of the oil sector. The other candidate, who initially said he would not restore the subsidy on petrol, shortly after had to over explain what he meant, perhaps after he observed what seemed like a positive response in some quarters to his counterpart’s promise. At least it generated national conversation that apparently drew attention, if not momentum, to that first candidate’s campaign. The other said he would remove the subsidy on petrol after he had fought and defeated corruption. Which is another example of his typical verbiage. In this instance, it is a time-wasting, circuitous way of saying he would not restore petrol subsidy. Or how else, or when, does he hope to put an end to corruption in his government, not to mention ending corruption in Nigeria? In summary, therefore, the attitude of these two men and their supporters to the campaign was made clear by their responses to President Tinubu’s October 1 speech. What one of them did was to tread the same old path of issuing what basically amounts to promissory notes. He repeated the worn lines of his insanely outlandish promises. Either approach of these two opposition candidates—I won’t call it strategy, because there was none to it—smacks of desperation. The boring repetitiveness of their message at different fora is jarring. There you have the summary of the respective stance of each of these candidates. Their responses to the president’s speech were remarkable precisely for their emptiness. In the case of the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, the only thing that many observing Nigerians came away with was the former VP’s attempt at mudslinging. He repeatedly and disrespectfully calls the president by his first name. It was unbecoming behaviour that diminished the gravity of the occasion, not his speech, which I have said was remarkable for its emptiness. Huge on grandiloquence, it offered no concrete alternative and, quite deservedly, received no praise. As were the whataboutisms of Paul Ibe, his media sidekick, who doubled down on his master’s unpresidential antics. The post When adult petulance becomes a campaign strategy, by Rotimi Fasan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JUI-F urges govt to let PTI protest
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman on Tuesday advised the government not to obstruct the PTI long march heading towards Islamabad, as protests were a democratic right enjoyed by all political parties. Speaking to the media alongside opposition leaders outside his residence, the JUI-F leader also urged the government to trust the PTI’s intention regarding a peaceful protest. When political parties say they will remain peaceful, their word should be trusted, he said in a comment on measures taken by the government to stop the PTI protesters from entering the federal capital. A delegation of opposition parties, including Senate opposition leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Asad Qaiser, Akhundzada Hussain, Salman Akram Raja and other leaders, arrived at Maulana’s residence, while the JUI-F side included Maulana Fazlur Rahman, Senator Kamran Murtaza and other party leaders. The JUI-F leader claimed that the dialogue between the government and the opposition could have been successful if ‘behind-the-scenes forces’ had not participated in the process. According to the veteran politician, any dialogue required mutual give-and-take to move forward. Maulana Fazl said democratic and political forces believe in dialogue, adding that the opposition parties held consultations in parliament but the attitude of those in power towards the opposition was visible to all. Without naming the cabinet members who questioned the loyalty of the PTI members towards the country, Maulana Fazl said, “We are all Pakistanis, and we are all patriots. We stand with the Constitution and the state. Nobody’s loyalty to the country is in doubt and there should be balance in the country’s political landscape.” The JUI-F chief said he received an invitation from the delegation of the opposition parties to participate in the multi-party conference. “We asked the opposition to consider this in detail, and we, too, will consider it within our party,” he said, adding that a joint agenda should emerge through the consultation of all parties. Maulana Fazl also countered the talks of an anti-terrorism operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying operations had been conducted from Swat to Waziristan, but the people there had not been able to return to their homes due to unrest. He said the provincial government in KP had been paralysed due to ongoing lawlessness, adding that the situation in the province continued to deteriorate. “How long will we continue to conduct operations on the pretext of fighting terrorism?” he added. Speaking on the occasion, Senator Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said that the delegation arrived at Maulana’s residence soon after he returned from Umrah to congratulate him and invite him to participate in the conference. “We are all children of Pakistan; we cannot remain indifferent to the difficulties facing this country. The situation in Pakistan is deteriorating day by day,” he said. He added that the opposition sought a consensus-based agenda, since an agenda formulated through consultation would contain solutions to the problems facing the entire country.He said extremist tendencies flourish where the political process is halted and added that Maulana Fazl rejected the imposition of the governor’s rule and a state of emergency in KP. Salman Akram Raja, PTI secretary general, said that a rift has been created between the public and the state through coercion. “The struggle of Imran Khan is a fight for the Constitution and the rule of law. We will win this fight,” he added. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: NSITF exposes fake recruitment scam, cautions Nigerians against fraudsters
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA —The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) has issued a public warning over the spread of fraudulent employment advertisements and forged appointment letters being used by scammers to deceive job seekers. The warning was contained in a public notice issued by the Fund and circulated to regional and branch managers via a memorandum dated October 5, 2026, signed by Samaila Abdu, Esq., Executive Director, Administration. According to the notice, the NSITF said it is not currently recruiting for any position and described employment advertisements circulating on social media, particularly Facebook, as fake The Fund stated that the fraudulent advertisements reflect a growing trend of individuals and groups falsely claiming to represent the NSITF in recruitment exercises. NSITF urged members of the public to disregard such advertisements and avoid making payments to anyone over purported employment opportunities. The Fund emphasised that it neither charges fees for employment nor conducts recruitment through unofficial social media platforms or channels. It added that any genuine employment opportunities would be announced through its official channels. “Stay alert, stay safe,” the Fund urged, advising members of the public who encounter suspicious recruitment advertisements or requests to avoid responding and report them to the appropriate NSITF authorities. As part of measures to protect the public and safeguard the integrity of its recruitment process, NSITF management has directed all Regional and Branch Managers to prominently display the public notice at strategic locations within their offices. The directive covers reception areas, main entrances and exits, notice boards, SERVICOM desks and other conspicuous locations accessible to staff and members of the public. The Fund said the notice should be displayed immediately and kept visible to ensure that members of the public are adequately informed and protected from fraudulent recruitment activities. NSITF urged Nigerians, particularly job seekers, to exercise caution and verify every recruitment claim through the Fund’s official communication channels before taking any action. The development comes amid growing concerns over fraudulent online recruitment schemes targeting unemployed Nigerians with promises of government jobs in exchange for money or personal information. NSITF’s latest warning underscores the need for job seekers to remain vigilant, as legitimate public-sector recruitment does not require applicants to pay individuals or unofficial agents for employment. The post NSITF exposes fake recruitment scam, cautions Nigerians against fraudsters appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Heavy losses reported as Yemen fighting escalates
items.description: • 115 govt troops, 160 Houthi fighters killed in 24 hours • Rebels claim attack on Riyadh airport, deny losing territory • Riyadh claims intercepting missile • Over 184,000 people displaced by fighting • Pakistanis in Saudi Arabia urged to avoid sharing sensitive footage SANAA: Fighting across Yemen has killed more than 270 government troops and Houthi fighters over the past day, sources on both sides said on Tuesday. Houthis also claimed an attack on the Saudi capital’s main airport and on Tuesday denied being pushed back by government forces. Fighting has intensified in Yemen since the internationally recognised government launched a counter-offensive aimed at recovering territory seized by Houthi fighters last month. Government sources told AFP on condition of anonymity that 115 troops had died over the past 24 hours, and that dozens of others were wounded in fighting, and by Houthi missile and drone attacks. The focus of the violence is on southwest Yemen, around the Bab al-Mandab strait that is crucial to global energy flows. Houthi military sources meanwhile told AFP that they had lost 160 fighters over the past day, mainly in Saudi strikes on areas under their control. On Monday, the Houthis said they had struck Riyadh airport and a refinery belonging to Saudi state oil giant Aramco. Loud explosions rattled the Saudi capital on Mon­day evening. They were followed by another explosion on Tuesday that echoed through northern par­ts of the city, residents said. Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport is facing frequent temporary closures of its airspace, according to tracking website Flightradar24. Saudi authorities have not publicly acknowledged the closures or confirmed any strikes targeting the facility. But on Tuesday the civil aviation authority said at least three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border a day earlier. The Saudi-led coalition also said on Tuesday that its forces intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southwest. The coalition’s spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said on X it “intercepted and destroyed” the missile launched towards Khamis Mushait, which is home to an airbase. Meanwhile, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group still held all territory seized last month when they swept through coastal areas along the Red Sea. Houthi fighters “have full control over all their advances on the ground”, he posted on Telegram. Saree said they had carried out dozens of strikes in the past few hours targeting government forces in Yemen’s Al-Jawf and Marib regions, while also attacking Taiz governorate. The Houthis’ health ministry said on Tuesday that a Saudi air strike killed six members of the same family, including four children, in a village in Hajjah governorate, bordering Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia, the main backer of the Yemeni government, has been providing air support for the counter-offensive launched by government forces. ‘Mocha is a war zone’ Government forces claimed late on Monday that they had achieved “victories on several fronts”. But military sources with the government refrained from confirming Mocha’s recapture, only saying they had cut the one supply route to the area. They also said they expelled the Houthis from several areas in Taiz in the southwest, where fighting has surged in recent days. Mohammed, a 33-year-old charity worker who fled from Mocha to Aden, said “people there are terrified”. “Life in Mocha has come to a complete standstill — there is no movement at all. The city has become a war zone,” he told AFP. Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade. Yemen’s civil war flared up again in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the wider Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The Houthis last month seized control of Yemen’s entire western coastline along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years. They have regularly targeted oil and military installations in Saudi Arabia and declared a maritime blockade on its ships. Pakistan and Turkiye on Monday pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defence pact following weeks of Houthi attacks. The Yemen conflict caused a major humanitarian crisis that left most of the population dependent on aid. The Houthis’ campaign around the Red Sea coast forced more than 184,000 people to flee their homes, according to the United Nations. A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting”. He condemned Houthi cross-border attacks on Saudi Arabia. Pakistanis in KSA cautioned Pakistan Ulema Council Chairman Tahir Mehmood Ashrafi on Tuesday urged Pakistanis in Saudi Arabia to exercise caution and refrain from sharing images or videos of Houthi drone and missile attacks, interception operations, debris, security installations or other sensitive locations. He asked the community to comply with Saudi laws and official directives, avoid circulating unverified information or rumours and rely only on official Saudi sources for information about security incidents. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: ‘4 million is possible’ – Abanga unveils NPP’s youth-vote battle plan
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fusani Yakubu, has defended the party’s ambitious target of securing four million youth votes for Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the next presidential election. I promise them I’m not going to be an armchair national youth organiser. I’ll be joining them in their various regions, constituencies very soon,” he said. According to him, the NPP’s youth mobilisation strategy will also rely heavily on social media to challenge what he described as misinformation against the party. “So we preach the gospel of Dr Mahamud Bawumia. It’s the only solution for this country,” he said. Mr Abanga also used the interview to criticise the government over rising fuel prices and its implementation of the 24-hour economy policy. “Yet today we can’t buy fuel. Prices of fuel have gone up GH¢20 and above,” he said. He questioned how the government could effectively regulate a 24-hour economy when an office expected to oversee it closes at 5 p.m. “How can an office that is meant to regulate an office that is supposed to operate 24 hours close at 5 p.m.?” he asked. He accused the governing NDC of using social media to undermine the achievements of the previous NPP administration. “They use social media to sway away from the good policies and initiatives ex-President Akufo-Addo and Dr Mahamudu Bawumia did for this country by propagating lies and fake propaganda,” he said. Mr Abanga also pointed to cocoa prices as another issue the NPP would use in its campaign. He said his parents are cocoa farmers and questioned the reduction in the producer price of cocoa. “Dr Mahmoud Baomia was buying cocoa for GH¢3100. Today, cocoa prices have gone down. Now they are buying cocoa for GH¢2000,” he said. He also criticised the government over its previous promise on cocoa prices. “They said they were going to buy cocoa GH¢6000,” he said. Mr Abanga said the NPP must now take its campaign to the grassroots and mobilise young voters ahead of the next election. “It’s the government that we are feeling today. We are suffering, and being a youth and representing my party as a national youth commander, I must take charge, mobilise the youth, so we can prosecute an effective campaign, so Dr Bawumia wins the 2020 election to save this country,” he said.

items.title: 19-year-old survives emergency brain surgery in Abia
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — A 19-year-old motorcycle accident victim has survived emergency brain surgery at the Abia State Specialist Hospital and Diagnostic Centre, Umuahia, after doctors evacuated more than 100 millilitres of blood clot compressing his brainstem. The victim was reportedly brought to the hospital on Sunday, October 4, in a deep coma with a Glasgow Coma Scale, GCS, score of six out of 15, which later deteriorated to five. The four-hour operation was performed after investigations revealed massive bleeding inside the victim’s skull. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this on Tuesday while briefing journalists at Government House, Umuahia, on the outcome of the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti. Giving details, the Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Uche, a neurosurgeon, said the bleeding was compressing the patient’s brainstem, making immediate surgery necessary. He said transferring the patient to another facility could have proved fatal, given the severity of his condition. “Because we now have facilities to undertake brain surgery, and then we have brain surgeons in the state employed by His Excellency, that surgery was done,” Uche said. He disclosed that more than 100ml of blood clot was evacuated from the patient’s brain, adding that the young man had subsequently started moving his limbs while recovering in the Intensive Care Unit. Speaking with Vanguard, the Chief Medical Director of the hospital, Dr Chimezie Okwuonu, described the procedure as the facility’s first brain surgery. He said the successful operation demonstrated the growing capacity of the hospital to manage complex medical conditions locally. Okwuonu said the surgery was performed by a multidisciplinary team led by Uche, the hospital’s neurosurgeon, Dr Kalu and other specialists. He disclosed that the hospital, which had only one specialist consultant when the current management assumed duty, now has 28 consultants. According to him, the expansion was part of efforts to strengthen specialist manpower and improve healthcare infrastructure in the state. Okwuonu said the hospital would build on the development by expanding its capacity for brain and spine surgeries and providing specialised neurological care within Abia. He added that the development would complement the state’s efforts to reduce medical tourism, citing the commencement of kidney transplant services as another area in which the state was building local capacity. Other health interventions Meanwhile, Kanu disclosed that the state had paid N502.1 million as counterpart funding under the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund, a requirement for accessing Federal Government intervention for vulnerable residents. He also said specialised trauma equipment for orthopaedic, brain and spine surgeries was being attracted to the state through collaboration with a Swedish organisation. Kanu said health interventions had commenced in flood-affected communities to prevent disease outbreaks. He added that no cases of Lassa fever, Ebola, diphtheria or COVID-19 had been recorded during the period under review. Also, the Administrator of the Abia State Eye Health Management Bureau, Dr Betty Emeka-Obasi, said the state had commenced activities to mark the 2026 World Sight Day. She said free eye screening for commercial drivers was among the programmes being implemented under the campaign, themed “Safe Eyes, Safe Roads and Safe Lives.” According to her, the campaign would run until October 15, with the bureau collaborating with the Ministry of Transport, the Federal Road Safety Corps and transport unions. Emeka-Obasi also disclosed plans to establish a vision corridor at the Nnenna Otti Bus Terminal, where commercial drivers would be able to conveniently assess their eyesight. She said the initiative was aimed at reducing road risks associated with poor vision among drivers. The post 19-year-old survives emergency brain surgery in Abia appeared first on Vanguard News .
