items.title: Power loom sector reels under imports, rising costs
items.description: Power looms are displayed for sale after closure of businesses in Faisalabad.—Courtesy Council of Loom Owners Association • 100,000 workers lose jobs in Faisalabad amid closure of 40pc units • Loom owners blame cheaper Chinese yarn, grey cloth, finished textile products • Industry body seeks stronger Customs checks to curb ‘under-invoicing’ LAHORE: A large number of small power loom units have shut down as the industry struggles with rising imports of yarn and grey cloth from China, and higher utility bills and taxes. The situation has worsened in Faisalabad and adjoining towns — a hub of power looms and allied industries, including sizing — where thousands of workers have lost their jobs. Around 40 per cent of units have shut down in a sector comprising nearly 800,000 looms, Dawn has learnt. “This small industry is in great trouble these days because it is no longer competitive in a market dominated by Chinese yarn, grey cloth and even finished cloth being imported in bulk,” Textile, Power Loom and Garment Workers Union Faisalabad President Aslam Meraj told Dawn on Tuesday. He said imported textile products were cheaper than locally produced goods, while rising utility bills and taxes had made it increasingly difficult for power loom operators to survive. “More than 100,000 power loom workers have become jobless. Power looms are being closed on a daily basis and workers are being terminated,” he claimed, criticising the government for failing to protect the local industry. Faisalabad, often described as the Manchester of Pakistan because of its concentration of textile and allied industries, has nearly 800,000 power looms operating in establishments ranging from small workshops to factories housing between 1,000 and 5,000 looms. Power looms manufacture grey cloth from yarn after it is processed at sizing units. Industry representatives said yarn imported from China was largely polyester-based and was being used by exporters to manufacture grey cloth, some of which entered the domestic market when exports declined. They argued that cheaper imported yarn, grey cloth and finished products had put local power loom operators at a disadvantage. “The industry, especially small power looms and sizing mills, is facing serious problems at the moment,” Faisa­labad Sizing Mills Association President Shakil Ansari said. He said locally produced yarn, ranging from counts 40 to 100, was used to manufacture products from grey cloth to finished garments for men and women, but Chinese imports had increasingly captured the market. Mr Ansari also said border closures had disrupted the movement of locally produced cloth to Afghanistan and Central Asian states, while road closures, particularly on routes leading to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, had affected trade in grey cloth. Payments from traders in KP had also been delayed because of the disruption in business, he said. “All these issues, coupled with high utility bills and taxes, have brought the industry to a grinding halt,” Mr Ansari said. Muhammad Sabir, who owns a unit comprising 44 power looms in Faisalabad, criticised the government for allowing imports of yarn, grey cloth and finished textile products from China. “I don’t know why the government has allowed imports of Chinese thread and other textile-related goods at the cost of its own businesses,” he said while talking to Dawn . He also complained about high utility bills, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) taxes and labour inspections. “What to do, where to go?” he asked. Tighter import checks sought Meanwhile, the Council of Loom Owners Assoc­iation has written to Commerce Minister Jam Kamal, seeking stronger import valuation controls through verification of export declarations. The association said under-invoicing in imports, particularly of fabrics, yarn and other textile products from China, remained a serious concern for domestic manufacturers. It alleged that some goods were being exported from China at higher declared values but lower values were being declared when they entered Pakistan to reduce duties and taxes, resulting in unfair competition for domestic manufacturers and loss of government revenue. “Pakistan and China alre­ady have an Electronic Data Exchange mechanism bet­ween their Customs administrations to address misdeclaration and under-invoicing. How­ever, the mechanism needs to be strengthened for consignment-level verification of values and particulars declared in Pakistan against the corresponding export declaration filed with Chinese Customs,” the association said in its letter. It proposed that importers be required to submit, along with the Goods Declaration filed in Pakistan, a copy of the corresponding Chinese Exp­ort Customs Decl­aration or Customs Declaration Form for Export Goods. The declared value, HS code, description, quantity and other shipment details in the Chinese export declaration could then be reconciled with the Pakistani goods declaration and supporting commercial documents, it suggested. Any material discrepancy could become the basis for further scrutiny, while allowing for legitimate differences on account of freight, insurance and terms of trade. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Ralph Obioha: Life of a man who lost much, fought on, and left his mark on Nigeria
items.description: By Chioma Gabriel There are lives that can be measured by what a man accumulated, and there are lives that must be measured by what he was prepared to lose for an idea. Chief Ralph Obioha belonged to the second category. For a man who built businesses, entered politics, sat in the House of Representatives, helped organise one of Nigeria’s most consequential pro-democracy struggles and spent years in exile, his life was a remarkable intersection of enterprise, public service, political conviction and sacrifice. Obioha died on October 3, 2026, at the age of 80. His family, announcing his death on October 6, described him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather, brother and friend, as well as a patriot, elder statesman, political leader and businessman committed to Nigeria’s progress. But beyond the formal descriptions lies a more compelling story: that of a man who moved from the world of business into politics and, eventually, into the dangerous theatre of the struggle against military dictatorship. Born into enterprise Ralph Obioha was born into the influential Obioha family of Arondizuogu in present-day Imo State. His father, Chief Louis Nwakire Obioha, was a prominent businessman and industrialist whose entrepreneurial activities became part of the economic history of the area. He established NIPROC, a large-scale palm-kernel processing enterprise at Arondizuogu. It was a background in which enterprise was not merely about personal wealth. Business was also a vehicle for employment, community development, and social influence. Ralph inherited that entrepreneurial instinct. Before he became known nationally as a politician and NADECO leader, he had already established himself as a businessman with interests across several sectors. At one point, his business empire included First African Trust Bank, Safari Brewery, Castle Cement’s cement-bagging operation in Port Harcourt and a vegetable-oil company. The scale of those enterprises offers an important window into the man he was before politics consumed much of his life. In a 2018 interview, Obioha said his businesses had employed about 2,700 Nigerians and 17 expatriates. He would later lose virtually all of them as a consequence of his involvement in the struggle for democracy. That loss became one of the defining chapters of his life. Politics and the Second Republic Obioha’s political journey began long before he became associated with NADECO. He served as a member of the House of Representatives during Nigeria’s Second Republic. A profile of his political career also records that he chaired the House Committee on Finance during that period. But the political turbulence that repeatedly interrupted Nigeria’s democratic journey would eventually pull him into a far more dangerous form of politics. The annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election transformed the country’s political landscape. For Obioha, it was not simply another disagreement between politicians. He regarded the annulment of what he believed was Moshood Abiola’s electoral mandate as an assault on democracy itself. That conviction would change his life. The June 12 struggle Obioha became one of the prominent figures associated with the National Democratic Coalition, NADECO, the movement that emerged as a major force against military rule and demanded the restoration of the June 12 mandate. When General Sani Abacha’s regime intensified its crackdown on pro-democracy activists, Obioha went into exile. He became a leading figure in NADECO’s activities in Canada and the United States, campaigning internationally against military rule and for the restoration of Abiola’s mandate. It was a decision that came at an extraordinary personal cost. The businessman who had built companies and employed thousands of Nigerians was suddenly separated from his businesses, his country and, for a period, his normal family life. In his own recollection, he had expected the exile to last months. Instead, it lasted years. He eventually returned to Nigeria in 1998. Looking back years later, he was remarkably unapologetic. He lost the bank. He lost the brewery. He lost the cement operation. He lost the vegetable-oil company. But he insisted he did not regret the struggle. “I will never regret being part of the struggle,” he said in an interview, describing the experience as a wider sphere of experience for him. That perhaps captures the paradox of Ralph Obioha’s life: a man who lost much materially while believing that he had gained something larger in the service of his country. The price of exile The story of Nigeria’s pro-democracy struggle is often told through its most famous names — Abiola, Kudirat Abiola, Alfred Rewane, Wole Soyinka, Gani Fawehinmi and others. But there were men and women whose contributions were made away from the cameras. Obioha became one of those voices abroad. From Canada and the United States, he helped keep international attention on Nigeria’s political crisis. His argument was simple: the military could suppress activists at home, but it could not easily silence those speaking to the international community. He later recalled that the struggle was motivated by both patriotism and what he described as the denial of a mandate freely given by Nigerians. For him, democracy was not an abstract word. It was a principle worth paying for. The politician after exile When Nigeria returned to democratic rule in 1999, Obioha did not disappear from public life. He remained politically engaged and became national chairman of the Justice Party. The party later fielded Rev. Chris Okotie as its presidential candidate in the 2003 election. He also became involved in affairs concerning Ohanaeze Ndigbo and served as chairman of its caretaker committee at one stage, although his involvement in the organisation was accompanied by disputes over its leadership and representation. His politics was often outspoken. He spoke about power, corruption, insecurity, tribalism, the condition of the South-East and the wider question of Nigerian nationhood. But beneath many of his interventions was one recurring belief: Nigeria’s problems could not be solved by merely replacing one ethnic group with another at the top. He repeatedly argued for competence, institutional development and leadership capable of producing results. A voice on Nigeria’s contradictions Obioha’s later years were characterised by an unusual combination of nostalgia and criticism. He remembered a Nigeria that, in his view, possessed enormous economic promise, yet he was deeply frustrated by the country’s failure to convert its human and natural resources into prosperity. In his 2018 conversation with Vanguard, he identified electricity, employment, education, healthcare and functioning institutions among the issues holding Nigeria back. He was particularly concerned about tribalism. His argument was that Nigeria should search for its best people irrespective of whether they were Igbo, Yoruba, Hausa, Ijaw, Efik, Kanuri or from any other ethnic group. It was a striking position from a man who was himself an important voice in Igbo affairs. His nationalism did not require him to abandon his identity. Instead, he appeared to believe that ethnic identity and Nigerian citizenship could coexist without one destroying the other. The elder statesman Even in old age, Obioha remained politically engaged. In January 2026, shortly before his death, he spoke forcefully against the description of the January 1966 coup as an “Igbo coup”. Having lived through the era, he argued that the coup should not be collectively attributed to the Igbo people. He acknowledged the prominent participation of Igbo officers but rejected the idea that the Igbo as a people had organised or authorised the coup. It was characteristic of the older Obioha: still argumentative, still willing to enter difficult national conversations and still convinced that historical narratives mattered. His voice remained recognisable — measured, sometimes blunt, but deeply concerned about Nigeria’s direction. Recognition that came late In 2026, President Bola Tinubu included Obioha among Nigerians selected for national honours for their roles in the June 12 struggle. But Obioha declined the honour, according to reports, citing concerns including insecurity and the continued detention of Nnamdi Kanu. There was something symbolic about that decision. The man who had spent decades demanding justice for a political mandate had reached the twilight of his life still insisting that the country had unfinished business. What remains Ralph Obioha’s life cannot be reduced to NADECO. Nor can it be reduced to his businesses, his parliamentary career, his political disagreements or his role in Igbo affairs. His story is ultimately about the choices a man makes when personal comfort collides with public conviction. He had something to lose, and he lost it. He had businesses to protect, and they collapsed. He had a country to return to, but exile became his temporary home. He had opportunities to remain silent — yet he chose to speak. And when the struggle ended, and democracy eventually returned, he did not pretend that Nigeria had suddenly become the country the pro-democracy activists had imagined. He continued to question it. He continued to criticise it. He continued to believe in its potential. That may be the most enduring thread in the life of Ralph Obioha. He was a businessman who entered politics, a politician who became a dissident, a dissident who became an elder statesman, and an elder statesman who never quite stopped being an activist. His life traversed some of Nigeria’s most turbulent decades. And in the final reckoning, his greatest possession may not have been the businesses he built or the political offices he occupied. It may have been the conviction that Nigeria was worth fighting for — even when the fight demanded that he give up almost everything he had. Ralph Obioha died at 80. But the questions he spent a lifetime asking about democracy, justice, leadership and the Nigerian project remain very much alive. The post Ralph Obioha: Life of a man who lost much, fought on, and left his mark on Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘I never gave up’ – Abanga Fusani reflects on journey to NPP Youth Organiser victory
items.description: Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fusani Yakubu, says hard work, consistency and sacrifice helped him overcome previous defeats to secure a decisive victory in the party’s recent elections. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Mr Abanga reflected on his political journey, which has been marked by several setbacks before his latest breakthrough. He recalled that his political career began at the University of Ghana, where he served as a TESCON organiser and aspired to become TESCON president. However, he and his opponent, Appiah Ofosu Prince, popularly known as Political Prince, were both disqualified from the contest. He said the setback opened another opportunity when NPP National Chairman John Boadu invited him to work at the party’s headquarters. “I served him at the headquarters from 2015 to 2022,” he said. His next major challenge came in 2019 when he contested the NPP parliamentary primaries in Aowin. “I lost by six votes,” he recalled. Three years later, he returned to contest for the position of National Youth Organiser but lost to Salam Mustafa Ibrahim. “I was second, if you recall. So I never gave up, even though I lost,” he said. Mr Abanga then returned to Aowin and contested the parliamentary primaries, winning close to 70% to become the NPP’s parliamentary candidate for the 2024 election. Despite the NPP’s nearly 6,000-vote advantage over the NDC in the constituency, he lost the parliamentary election by just 103 votes. He said those experiences strengthened his resolve ahead of the latest NPP national elections. “One thing that I’ve realised about our party people. They believe in hard work. They believe in consistency, sacrifice, and this time they decided to reward me because I’ve been consistent and I’ve worked hard over the years,” he said. Mr Abanga said he returned to the party’s grassroots and engaged members, presenting his vision, policies and programmes. He said the delegates eventually concluded that he was the right candidate and gave him an overwhelming endorsement. “That’s why they endorsed me overwhelmingly,” he said. Abanga Fusani believes his consistency also helped build trust among delegates. “You see, if you are consistent in politics, one sympathy vote counts as well, and with dedication and consistency, people begin to believe every day you are preaching one message, one message, one meaning. You mean it. You are honest. You are sincere. They want to try you and see,” he said. Mr Abanga said his victory ultimately demonstrated the confidence the NPP’s youth have placed in his leadership.

items.title: World Bank maintains Ghana’s growth rate forecast at 4.8% in 2026
items.description: The World Bank has maintained its forecast of Ghana’s growth rate at 4.8% in 2026, its October 2026 Africa Economic Update has disclosed. It is however projecting a 4.9% GDP growth for Ghana in 2027. According to the Bretton Woods institution, the growth will be driven by the services sector, a recovery in oil and gas activities, and ongoing performance tied to structural and fiscal reforms under national programmes. “In Ghana, economic activity remained robust in the second quarter of 2026, although growth moderated slightly. Real GDP expanded by 6.0% year-on-year, down from 6.6% in the same period in 2025”, it said. On the expenditure side, the Bank said ahead of the Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, that growth was underpinned by strong domestic demand, with investment surging by 53.0% and domestic demand rising by 11.2%, signaling continued strength in private and public spending. On the production side, services remained the main engine of growth, expanding by 8.0% and accounting for nearly three-fifths of overall GDP growth, with ICT activity rising by 30.9%. Industrial growth strengthened to 4.3% from 2.4% a year earlier, supported by a sharp increase in oil and gas production. In contrast, agricultural growth slowed to 3.9% from 7.1%, reflecting a steep contraction in fishing activity. Overall, the World Bank said growth remained concentrated in services, ICT, and hydrocarbons, while momentum weakened across parts of the non-oil economy. Meanwhile, economic growth in the West and Central Africa (AFW) subregion is projected to remain steady at 4.5% in 2026, unchanged from 2025, before strengthening modestly to an annual average of 4.7% in 2027–28. The report said subregional performance continues to be shaped by developments in Nigeria, the largest economy in AFW. Excluding Nigeria, growth is estimated to moderate from a robust 5.4% in 2025 to 5.0% in 2026, before recovering to an average of 5.3% during 2027–28. Also, growth in Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to increase to 4.3% in 2026, but its poverty-reducing impact will likely remain limited.

items.title: Pakistan drives regional rise in poverty levels
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Projecting Pakistan’s economic growth at 3.8 per cent and fiscal deficit at 3.5pc for the current fiscal year, the World Bank on Tuesday said the country was home to almost half of the extremely poor population in the entire Middle East, North Africa and Afghanistan-Pakistan (Menaap) region. “Menaap is the only region in the world in which poverty remains above pre-pandemic levels and continues to rise. Pakistan accounts for nearly half of the region’s extreme poor,” the Washington-based lending agency said in its Economic Outlook ahead of the IMF-WB annual meetings next week. A prolonged slowdown in tourism, construction and related services could reduce labour demand and weaken income flows to labour-sending economies, particularly Pakistan and parts of the Levant, it added. It estimated GDP growth would increase from 3.2pc in FY25 to 3.7pc in FY26 and 3.8pc in FY27, as services, manufacturing and livestock production remain resilient despite rising import costs. Higher commodity and transport costs are expected to put pressure on inflation and external balances, but continued strength in domestic activity is expected to outweigh these pressures. World Bank says 48pc of ‘extreme poor’ from ME region are in Pakistan The bank estimated the current account deficit at 0.1pc in FY2026, increasing significantly to 0.8pc in FY2027, while the fiscal deficit was estimated at 2.6pc in FY2026, rising to 3.5pc in FY2027. It reported that food insecurity remained particularly acute in the occupied West Bank and Gaza and the Republic of Yemen, with significant pressures also evident in Afghanistan, Djibouti, Lebanon and Pakistan. A stronger-than-usual El Niño weather pattern predicted for late 2026 could further amplify food-price pressures and hurt the poor. Pakistan is directly exposed through changing monsoon conditions, it said. The burden of poverty was highly concentrated in the region. “Pakistan accounts for about 48pc of the people in the region living below the $3.00 per day poverty line. Afghanistan, the Syrian Arab Republic and the Republic of Yemen together account for another 47pc,” it said. The most recent estimates show poverty rates at the $3.00-per-day line approached or exceeded 20pc in Djibouti, Pakistan, Syria and the Republic of Yemen. In 2024, 14.3pc of the Menaap region’s population lived on less than $3.00 a day, compared with 10.4pc globally, while 26.9pc lived on less than $4.20 a day, compared with 18.9pc worldwide. “The increase was driven primarily by a rise in poverty in Pakistan, where the poverty rate rose by 6.4 percentage points at the $3.00-per-day line and 3.2 percentage points at the $4.20-per-day line between 2018/19 and 2024/25, following a succession of adverse shocks, including the Covid-19 pandemic, the devastating 2022 floods, a macroeconomic crisis marked by high inflation and currency depreciation, and a prolonged period of economic adjustment that weakened real household incomes and employment opportunities.” Economic losses stemming from the US-Iran conflict are also concentrated in the region, but their ultimate scale remains highly uncertain and will depend on how the conflict evolves. Under the baseline assumption that disruptions persist through the end of 2026 without sustained further escalation, the region is projected to contract by 2.1pc in 2026, after growing 3.3pc in 2025. Oil-importing countries — Djibouti, the Arab Republic of Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Pakistan and Tunisia — remain exposed through economic channels, including rising inflationary pressures from higher oil and other commodity prices, loss of fiscal space, a decline in remittances from the Gulf economies and increased borrowing costs, mainly because of higher insurance risk premiums as the conflict persists. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Marriage halls built on J&K state land by ‘occupants’
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Large-scale commercial use of Jammu & Kashmir State land, including construction and operation of marriage halls and other businesses by illegal occupants came under scrutiny on Tuesday as a Senate subcommittee ordered sealing of unauthorised structures and sought five-year record of rent collection and utilisation. The meeting of the subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and States and Frontier Regions was held under chairpersonship of Senator Nasir Mehmood to review system of rent collection from properties on J&K State land and examine encroachments, with focus on transparency, accountability and enforcement. The committee was informed that total J&K State property comprises 34,616 kanals, equivalent to about 4,327 acres and one kanal. Encroachments covering about 318 acres, 8 kanals and 9 marlas had been identified in Sultanpura and Rehmanpura, Lahore, constituting around 7.37pc of total property in identified area. Of this, Sultanpura accounted for 153 acres, 2 kanals and 13 marlas, while Rehmanpura accounted for 165 acres, 3 kanals and 16 marlas. Senate panel tells officials to shutter unauthorised venues, register case if seal is violated The committee took serious note of construction and operation of marriage halls and other commercial activities on state land. The chairman directed officials to seal the unauthorised marriage halls, submit photographic evidence and initiate an FIR in case the seal was violated. Officials briefed on illegal constructions, disputed tenancy matters, unauthorised use and cases involving utility connections. The committee expressed concern over alleged issuance of unauthorised or questionable NOCs for electricity connections and directed proper investigation. Officials said department manages around 3,160 tenancies. Original receipts are issued to tenants, duplicate and voided copies retained for audit. Manual collections are entered in cash book and deposited through treasury challans, while digital payments are credited directly to authorised accounts. Manual receipts, collection statements, cash book entries and deposit records are cross-verified, whereas PayZen system provides automated digital reconciliation. The committee expressed concern over continued practice of cash-based rent collection and sought details of total rent collected, its deposit in banks/government accounts, outstanding dues and record of tenants. Officials said the process was being digitised and efforts were underway to transition large number of tenants to digital system. The chairman directed officials to provide five-year record of rent collection and utilisation, along with details of tenants, rent collected, dates of deposit, outstanding dues and receipts. He said system should be transparent, properly documented and subject to effective checks and balances. Senator Naseema Ehsan asked about reported theft, irregularities and misuse of state property. Officials said that irregularities had been reported in the past and a case was also pending before National Accountability Bureau. The committee sought details of such cases and recoveries. Officials said that J&K State land had been demarcated against revenue records and geo-referenced through PITB-assisted systems. Digital maps, including Aks Shajra, were made available to sub-committee. The chairman directed officials to provide complete details of state land, including demarcation, tenancy, rent collection and encroachments, and said committee would undertake field visits to verify position on ground. He also directed relevant records and receipts be produced for verification. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: FBR introduces rules for electronic scrutiny of taxpayers
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has begun extending the use of artificial intelligence to scrutinise individual tax returns, enabling its automated system to detect factual and legal mistakes and discrepancies before initiating legal or penal action. The draft rules, titled “38-B Procedure for electronic scrutiny and intimation of issues detected by the automated system”, have been proposed through amendments to the Income Tax Rules 2002. The draft rules will be finalised after three days, following feedback from stakeholders. A significant feature of the proposed arrangement is the automated analysis and cross-matching of information available with tax authorities. This will allow the system to compare information declared in income tax returns with other available data and flag potential discrepancies for clarification by taxpayers. The automated system will identify issues in tax returns and send online advice or advance intimation to taxpayers through the IRIS portal, pointing out factual and legal mistakes or discrepancies. The purpose is to allow taxpayers to clarify the issues, rectify errors or take corrective action before legal or penal proceedings are initiated. The detection of a discrepancy by the automated system, however, will not itself result in enforcement action. Tax watchdog to use automated system to detect mistakes, discrepancies Under the proposed mechanism, taxpayers will first be informed electronically about discrepancies detected in their income tax returns and given an opportunity to clarify or rectify them through a prescribed mechanism. The system-generated advance intimation identifying discrepancies may also be sent by the officer of Inland Revenue having jurisdiction over the taxpayer. The intimation will specify a response period of at least seven days during which the taxpayer can clarify or rectify the discrepancy. If the taxpayer fails to respond within the stipulated period, another reminder will be issued, providing a further period of at least seven days to respond. The officer of Inland Revenue having jurisdiction over the taxpayer will analyse the taxpayer’s response, or the absence of a response, before taking appropriate action under the relevant provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance and rules. The proposed arrangement effectively introduces an automated scrutiny layer immediately after processing income tax returns, while retaining the role of the tax officer in determining whether a discrepancy warrants action under the law. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Cedi was worst African currency in quarter 2, 2026 – World Bank
items.description: Amid the Middle East conflict, the Ghana cedi was the worst currency in Africa, depreciating nearly 10% to the US dollar between March 2026 and June 2026, the World Bank has revealed in its October 2026 Africa Economic Update. It was followed by Lesotho loti (over -6%), Namibia dollar (over -6%), South Africa rand (over -6%) and Swaziland lilangeni (over -6%). According to the World Bank, the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East initially exerted broad-based pressure on African currencies. “Most countries with available daily exchange rate data recorded currency depreciations during the second quarter of 2026 relative to end-February, before the conflict intensified. In seven of the 22 countries monitored (excluding the CFA franc zone), the maximum depreciation exceeded 5.0%, including in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana, the Seychelles, and South Africa”. “By end-August, however, much of this pressure had eased, with only 10 currencies remaining weaker than their end-February levels”, it added. It continued that the exchange rate response reflected the interaction of external shocks and preexisting domestic vulnerabilities, stressing, the sharp increase in oil and energy prices raised import bills across net energy-importing economies, increasing demand for U.S. dollars, weakening reserve positions, and intensifying depreciation pressures. At the same time, heightened geopolitical uncertainty triggered a flight to safety in global financial markets, prompting capital reallocation away from emerging and frontier economies. The World Bank said supply disruptions in the Middle East also pushed up the cost of key agricultural inputs, including fertilizers, adding to imported inflation pressures. It added that the currency depreciation further amplified fiscal vulnerabilities in countries with significant external debt service obligations, as the local-currency cost of servicing U.S. dollar-denominated debt increased. Meanwhile, the cedi remained under pressure over the last two weeks, extending its year-to-date depreciation against the US dollar to 10.04%. In the interbank market, the currency weakened by 1.39% to GH¢11.62 to a US dollar but gained 0.70% and 0.47% against the pound and euro to GH¢15.40 and GH¢13.24, respectively. Retail forex market performance was similarly mixed, with the cedi appreciating 0.21% against the US dollar and 0.91% against the euro to GH¢11.93 and GH¢13.73, respectively. It weakened 0.31% against the pound to GH¢15.88.

items.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
items.description: US death row inmate Christa Pike is “conscious and speaking” after surviving a failed execution attempt last week, her lawyers say. Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, her attorneys said in a statement on Tuesday. Pike, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995, survived two failed lethal injections last Wednesday in Tennessee. She was taken to hospital, where she remained unconscious for days as medical staff cleared her body of the injected chemical. Experts and her legal team say her apparent recovery is unprecedented. She is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection. Her lawyers called her progress “medically unprecedented”, and while her prognosis remains unclear, “at a minimum, we expect a long recovery”. Deborah Denno, a criminologist and professor at Fordham Law School, said she was “absolutely astonished” that Pike is conscious and speaking. There were seven other cases where prisoners survived slated executions, but in those cases, executioners were not able to inject anything into the inmates’ veins, Denno told the BBC. Pike “is the only person for whom some kind of toxin has been injected,” she said. “They did everything they were supposed to do as part of the execution process, and it simply didn’t work,” Denno said. “This has never happened before.” Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong after injecting her with the chemical pentobarbital. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year – and the head of prisons in the state said over the weekend that he plans to resign. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens. Pike’s attorneys are scheduled to appear in court in Nashville on Wednesday. They also plan to hold a news conference outside the court. Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike’s defence team, said on Tuesday that the likelihood of recovering from lethal injection is low. “Most people who get lethal injection die from it,” he told the BBC. “In fact, pretty well everyone, except Christa. So, the fact that she survived it … was unusual.” But there remains a lot of uncertainty and many unknowns, he said, including how much of the pentobarbital got into her system, what her blood levels were after the injection and what her recovery will look like. “I would not, in any way, say at this point that all the big risks are behind her,” he noted. Zivot had previously said the two doses of pentobarbital she received last week would have been enough that, had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation, “she would have surely died”. Instead, Zivot said a possible explanation is that instead of entering Pike’s bloodstream, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin. Zivot said last week he thought her ending up with a brain injury was “very possible”, due to the delays in resuscitating her. He also believed it would take about a week to truly understand her condition and do a neurological exam. It’s now been six days since the failed attempt to execute her. Pike’s lawyers previously warned that her medical history and anatomy – including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins – meant there was a risk she would experience “unnecessary” pain and suffering during a lethal injection. They said on Tuesday that she has endured “severe damage” to her arms. In 2022, more than a third of executions across the US were botched or highly problematic, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, which tracks information about such cases. For lethal injections, such incidents have typically occurred due to difficulty obtaining reliable IV access to the veins, though the underlying reason differs from person to person. In cases the centre has documented, all failures happened before the lethal drugs could be administered. The last failed lethal injection that was tracked happened earlier this year – also in Tennessee. The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein for a lethal injection. He was granted a year’s reprieve by the governor.

items.title: Dual citizen? Debarred
items.description: IT was a Friday afternoon in May 2019. State Bank of Pakistan Governor Tariq Bajwa was in Islamabad with the IMF mission, flanked by his technical team I led. Unbeknownst to him, his successor was already in the country. By evening, Bajwa had resigned. The finance secretary at the time told me a new governor would be appointed by nightfall: Reza Baqir, the IMF’s resident representative in Egypt, already in town and ready to assume charge. The notification followed the next day, a Saturday. Within 24 hours, over a weekend, a serving IMF official had been installed at the helm of the central bank, as abruptly as Bajwa’s own 2017 appointment had followed a rupee devaluation. Opacity is not the only problem; law compounds it. The 2022 amendments to the SBP Act, while granting welcome operational autonomy, also imposed restrictions found nowhere in the IMF’s own safeguards assessment: an outright bar on dual nationals, and a requirement that a candidate completes a full five-year term before turning 65. Together, these eliminate precisely the cohort best placed to lead the central bank, favouring insiders over competence. Contrast this with how Britain appoints the governor of the Bank of England: open international advertisement, a shortlist, ministerial interviews, and months of public notice before the transition begins. That is the process that produced Andrew Bailey to succeed Mark Carney in March 2020. In Pakistan, favoured candidates are installed within a day, while everyone else waits months, even years, for a vacancy the law says must be filled within 30 days. Mark Carney’s trajectory sharpens the point further. A Canadian citizen who also held Irish citizenship through family ancestry, he was appointed governor of the Bank of England in Nov 2012, and ran UK monetary policy and financial stability for nearly seven years, through the 2016 Brexit shock. In 2018, while still governor, he acquired British citizenship too, holding three nationalities as custodian of Britain’s currency, with no credible case that he favoured Canadian or Irish interests over British ones. Central banking is one of the few institutions where competence, not compliance, should be the only test. Stanley Fischer, author of three of the most influential economics textbooks, and former first deputy managing director of the IMF, served as vice chair of the US Federal Reserve from 2014 to 2017, while holding two citizenships, from age 70 to 74. More recently, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand appointed Dr Anna Breman, a Swedish national, as its first female governor. Dr Breman’s appointment in Aug 2025 followed a rigorous recruitment process, that even involved a global executive search firm. Baqir is the more contested recent case, but the criticism was never really about a passport; it was that an IMF insider negotiating a Pakistani programme sat ‘on both sides of the table’, a concern about institutional capture, not nationality. The consequences have been predictable. The governor’s post fell vacant in May 2022 and took over three months to fill, breaching the SBP Act’s 30-day requirement; a deputy governor’s post vacant since Nov 2024 was filled only in Aug 2026. Leadership has increasingly gone to candidates with modest qualifications, and qualified economists are either sidelined or leaving the SBP, a brain drain that is entirely self-inflicted. Brain drain is estimated to cost Pakistan roughly $4.2 billion annually. Pakistan’s economy, sustained by remittances, external borrowing, real estate speculation, and import-led consumption rather than exports, demands sophisticated leadership, not a bureaucratic placeholder chosen for compliance. Article 63(1)(c) bars dual nationals from parliament since an elected official answers to voters as the sole political principal, and a second citizenship competes with that loyalty. A central bank governor is not elected, but appointed, and constrained by statute, audit, parliamentary review, and a monetary policy committee, an accountability built on expertise, not a mandate. That is why dual nationality has long been lawful for the wider civil service, precisely because competence, not electoral legitimacy, is what those roles select for. A 2025 Senate report counted roughly 2,365 civil servants or their spouses holding dual nationality under that lawful regime. Extending the Article 63 logic to appointed posts applies a rule built for one office to a fundamentally different one. The government’s 2026 policy, read past the headline, already leans this way: the Civil Servants (Disclosure and Regulation of Foreign Nationality) Rules require employees to disclose foreign citizenship annually, treating concealment, not citizenship itself, as misconduct. It is a disclosure regime, not a blanket bar. A second passport is often acquired for reasons of economics and convenience, educating children, or freedom to travel, not disloyalty. The genuine concerns — divided loyalty, foreign leverage, capture by a foreign employer — are real, and better addressed by targeted tools than a passport count: disclosure of foreign assets, recusal where a conflict is shown, and cooling-off periods after work for a foreign government or an institution like the IMF. The US Federal Reserve applies this to its officials. It also catches the single-passport holder who has taken money from a foreign government, someone a citizenship test would wave through. Pakistan need not start from scratch. In 2022, the prime minister notified the ISI as the Special Vetting Agency for public office holders. The mechanism only needs streamlining to run on specific safeguards, not opaque “cleared” or “not cleared” verdicts that strip the federal government’s own statutory appointment authority. It is time to remove the dual-nationality bar and age restrictions on appointments to the governor, deputy governor, and Monetary Policy Committee positions. Central banking is one of the few institutions where competence, not compliance, should be the only test. The question worth asking of any candidate is not how many passports are in their drawer, but whether their record and enforceable safeguards assure they will act in the country’s interest. A passport count answers none of that. Performance, integrity, and disclosure do. The writer is the author of The Shady Economics of International Aid, and holds a PhD in economics from the University of Cambridge. He has served as chief economist of the State Bank and senior advisor to the IMF. Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

items.title: Lagos to deepen creative industry support — Hamzat
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has pledged continued government support for the creative industry through skills development, expanded training opportunities and provision of infrastructure to drive the sector’s growth. Hamzat spoke on Tuesday at the official commissioning and grand opening of Euphoria360 Hub, established by actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, in Oregun, Lagos. He said the state was committed to developing a sustainable pipeline of skilled creative professionals capable of competing and earning in the global market. According to him, Lagos has no shortage of creative talent but needs the right structures and opportunities to harness its potential. “The state is already investing in creative infrastructure, which includes the development of theatres in Ikorodu, Badagry, among other divisions. “Besides, the government is exploring further opportunities to expand training in areas such as filmmaking, acting, photography and other creative disciplines, as well as training up to one million Lagosians across various fields,” he said. The deputy governor said the government’s focus should go beyond training young people to creating a sustainable pipeline of globally competitive talent and linking skills development directly to employment opportunities. He said the objective was to create an enabling environment where creative professionals could showcase Nigerian culture to the world while earning commensurate economic value from their work. Citing the growing global influence of Nigerian films and storytelling, Hamzat said the country’s productions had become an important means of projecting Nigeria’s identity and culture across Africa and beyond. “I want to challenge you, our elders and stakeholders in the creative industry, to identify the major barriers limiting growth and work with the government to develop practical solutions, particularly in areas such as intellectual property, contracts and skills development,” he said. Hamzat congratulated Adebayo, the Chief Executive Officer of Euphoria360, on the establishment of the mega audio-visual project, describing it as an important contribution to the growth of Lagos’ creative ecosystem. Also speaking, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communication, Mr Sunday Dare, described Nigeria’s entertainment industry as a powerful force that had significantly enhanced the country’s visibility and global influence. Dare said government needed to support and strengthen the creative sector, noting that the industry had significant economic potential and could create jobs for a large number of young people. Earlier, Adebayo said the vision behind Euphoria360 Hub was to establish a one-stop facility where producers, filmmakers, creators, film enthusiasts and event planners could access quality facilities and professional services needed to bring their projects to life. He said the hub was designed to bring everything required to produce and deliver world-class projects under one roof, adding that it would become a landmark destination for creativity, collaboration and excellence in the entertainment industry. Adebayo said the facility brought together key players across the entertainment value chain while providing access to modern facilities and professional services needed to develop and deliver world-class productions. items.title: La Philharmonie de Paris consacre un week-end à la diversité des musiques marocaines
items.description: La Philharmonie de Paris consacrera, du 29 au 31 octobre, un week-end à la richesse et à la diversité des traditions musicales marocaines pour clore la Saison Méditerranée 2026. Selon les organisateurs, cette séquence artistique entend mettre en lumière la pluralité des expressions musicales du Royaume, nourries de traditions anciennes et d’influences multiples. La programmation s’articulera autour de plusieurs rendez-vous consacrés notamment aux musiques gnaoua, amazighe, andalouse et aux traditions musicales du monde rural marocain. Le coup d’envoi sera donné jeudi 29 octobre avec « Transes gnaouas » , une soirée réunissant le maâlem Abdelkébir Merchane et la jeune espoir de cet art ancestral Hind Ennaira. Vendredi 30 octobre, la soirée « Traditions marocaines » proposera un dialogue entre les musiques du monde rural marocain, le flamenco et le blues. L’Ensemble Lâabat de Ben Slimane et la chanteuse amazighe Chérifa Kersit en seront les principales figures, aux côtés notamment de la danseuse Florencia Oz, du chanteur Manuel Pajares et du guitariste britannique Justin Adams. La programmation se poursuivra samedi 31 octobre avec « Couleurs du Maroc » , un concert-promenade au Musée de la musique. Le public sera invité à découvrir, à travers différents instruments traditionnels, les univers de la musique soufie, des musiques gnawa et de la musique d’Andalousie. Le même jour, un spectacle familial intitulé « Paroles de cœur » proposera un voyage musical de l’Atlas marocain aux plaines de l’Atlantique, autour du patrimoine artistique des femmes amazighes. Le point d’orgue de ce week-end sera la « Soirée Andalouse » , prévue samedi soir dans la Grande salle Pierre Boulez. Sous la direction du maître Mohamed Briouel, l’orchestre marocain de musique Al Ala accompagnera cinq chanteuses venues du Maroc, du Liban, d’Espagne, de Grèce et d’Italie, dans un parcours musical allant du Levant au Maroc et mêlant répertoires traditionnels sacrés et profanes. Cette programmation est également prolongée par l’exposition consacrée à l’artiste marocain Hassan Hajjaj, présentée au Musée de la musique du 22 septembre 2026 au 25 avril 2027. The post La Philharmonie de Paris consacre un week-end à la diversité des musiques marocaines appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Rentcom targets Lagos workers’ housing gap with 1,000 apartments
items.description: By Prince Osuagwu, Hi-Tech Editor A group of tech-savvy youths under the aegis of Rentcom, has promised to plug the housing deficit in Nigeria with homes run mainly by technology. The young lads say they were worried by the lack of quality accommodation for professionals, particularly in Lagos and therefore launched a project to develop 1,000 furnished and serviced apartments across the city. Rentcom said its Workforce Apartments Lagos project would address a gap in the city’s housing market by providing professionally developed accommodation in major employment corridors. The first phase will comprise 100 apartments across three locations. Rentcom founder, Dr Adeosun Williams, said the project was designed to connect housing demand with investment in rental infrastructure that could generate income over time. “We are interested in financing infrastructure that can sustain itself through the revenue it generates,” he said. “Our systems are specifically directed towards projects where there is a demonstrable supply deficit and a corresponding demand for the infrastructure.” Williams said the company was approaching the apartments as an income-generating asset intended to meet an identified need. “We are not approaching Workforce Apartments simply as an apartment development. We are financing rental infrastructure,” he said. “The objective is to create an asset that addresses a real economic need while generating recurring revenue over its useful life.” The 100 apartments in the initial phase will form the basis of Rentcom’s planned 1,000-unit programme. The company said the accommodation would be fully furnished and serviced for professionals seeking housing near Lagos’ employment and commercial centres. Rentcom said its model was to identify infrastructure shortages, arrange capital for development and create assets whose revenue could support their long-term operation. It said the approach could also be applied to other infrastructure projects with clear demand and sustainable revenue potential. The project was flagged off on September 25. According to the company, the wider programme is intended to expand access to serviced rental accommodation while building a portfolio of income-generating assets. The post Rentcom targets Lagos workers’ housing gap with 1,000 apartments appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Normalisation avec Israël : Le PJD replonge dans ses fractures autour d’El Otmani
items.description: Près de six ans après la reprise des relations entre le Maroc et Israël, un dossier que le Parti de la justice et du développement (PJD) croyait relégué au second plan continue de hanter ses dirigeants. Une récente intervention d'Abdellatif Ouahbi, ministre de la Justice et figure du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), a suffi à remettre sur le devant de la scène un débat sensible : celui de la responsabilité politique de Saad Dine El Otmani dans la signature de l'accord tripartite conclu en décembre 2020 entre Rabat, Washington et Tel-Aviv. L'épisode a surtout mis en lumière les difficultés du PJD à solder l'un des chapitres les plus controversés de son passage au pouvoir, tout en révélant des divergences persistantes entre son secrétaire général, Abdelilah Benkirane, et l'ancien chef du gouvernement. Invité récemment par Hespress , Abdellatif Ouahbi s'est étonné du traitement réservé par Benkirane à certains soutiens politiques extérieurs au parti, tout en rappelant que Saad Dine El Otmani avait, lui, signé l'accord de normalisation avec Israël et assumé, selon ses termes, une responsabilité « officielle, politique, morale et historique » dans cette décision. Le responsable du PAM a également souligné que l'ancien chef du gouvernement avait participé à des activités électorales du PJD lors des dernières échéances, sans faire l'objet de la moindre sanction. Ces déclarations ont trouvé un écho rapide au sein du parti des « Frères » . Lors d'une rencontre organisée dimanche dernier dans la province de Nouaceur, Abdelilah Benkirane a adressé un message direct à son ancien compagnon de route, l'invitant à se retirer de la vie partisane active et à se consacrer à ses travaux académiques. Dans une intervention marquée par l'émotion, le secrétaire général du PJD a estimé que la présence d'El Othmani dans certaines activités du parti offrait à ses adversaires une occasion de rappeler un épisode qui continue de peser sur l'image de la formation. « Aujourd'hui encore, on nous reproche cette signature alors que nous n'y étions pour rien et n'en avions aucune connaissance », a-t-il lancé devant les militants. Cette sortie a immédiatement suscité des réactions, d'autant qu'elle contrastait avec les positions défendues par Benkirane au moment de la signature de l'accord avec Israël. À l'époque, le dirigeant islamiste avait refusé de faire porter à El Otmani la responsabilité exclusive de cette décision, estimant que le chef du gouvernement agissait dans le cadre des institutions de l'État et ne pouvait s'affranchir des orientations arrêtées au plus haut niveau. Dans plusieurs interventions publiques, Benkirane avait alors plaidé contre toute remise en cause de son successeur à la tête du gouvernement, mettant en avant la nécessité de préserver la stabilité des institutions et rappelant que le contexte diplomatique ayant conduit à la reprise des relations avec Israël dépassait les seules prérogatives du chef de l'exécutif. Face à la polémique, le secrétaire général du PJD a rapidement entrepris de désamorcer la crise. Deux jours après ses déclarations, il a présenté ses excuses à Saad Dine El Otmani, affirmant que les propos largement relayés avaient été sortis de leur contexte et qu'il ignorait la participation de ce dernier à la récente campagne électorale du parti. Benkirane a insisté sur les liens qui l'unissent à l'ancien chef du gouvernement, évoquant plusieurs décennies de travail commun et réaffirmant le respect et l'estime qu'il lui porte malgré leurs divergences d'appréciation. Il a toutefois maintenu son opinion selon laquelle certaines apparitions publiques d'El Otmani peuvent être exploitées par les adversaires du PJD pour relancer la polémique autour de la normalisation. L'affaire a néanmoins ouvert un débat plus large au sein du parti. Plusieurs responsables ont pris position pour défendre l'ancien chef du gouvernement et rappeler que le dossier avait déjà fait l'objet de nombreuses clarifications officielles. Mohamed Yatim, membre du secrétariat général du PJD, a ainsi jugé inutile de revenir sur une décision prise au nom de l'État marocain. Selon lui, la question relève davantage des règles institutionnelles et protocolaires que d'une initiative personnelle de Saad Dine El Otmani. Dans une publication sur Facebook, il a estimé que la signature du chef du gouvernement s'inscrivait dans l'ordre protocolaire de l'État et qu'il aurait été difficile, pour tout responsable politique placé dans une situation similaire, de refuser une décision émanant du Cabinet royal. Le même responsable a également rappelé qu'El Othmani avait exprimé à plusieurs reprises ses réserves vis-à-vis de la normalisation et soutenu que rien ne permettait d'affirmer qu'il avait eu connaissance du contenu exact du document au moment de sa signature. D'autres voix ont appelé à dépasser la polémique. Khalid Samadi, ancien secrétaire d'État chargé de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, a plaidé pour une lecture plus sereine du dossier, tenant compte à la fois du contexte politique de l'époque et des conséquences des différentes options qui s'offraient aux décideurs. Au sein de la jeunesse du parti, Mohamed Amine Dahhaoui a, quant à lui, appelé les responsables du PJD à privilégier la médiation et la cohésion interne. Estimant que les défis politiques à venir nécessitent davantage d'unité, il a exhorté les dirigeants à régler leurs différends dans les cadres institutionnels du parti plutôt que sur la place publique. Au-delà de la controverse du moment, cet épisode illustre les difficultés persistantes du PJD à tourner la page de la normalisation avec Israël. Un dossier qui continue d'alimenter les critiques de ses adversaires politiques et de raviver, à intervalles réguliers, des débats que la formation islamiste peine encore à refermer. items.title: Élections législatives : six recours déposés devant la Cour constitutionnelle
items.description: La Cour constitutionnelle de Rabat a reçu, jusqu’à mardi après-midi, six recours contestant les résultats des élections législatives du 23 septembre 2026, a appris Hespress de sources informées. Selon les mêmes sources, six dossiers de recours avaient été déposés directement auprès de la Cour constitutionnelle à 14h00 mardi, contestant les résultats du scrutin annoncés par le ministère de l’Intérieur. Ce nombre pourrait toutefois augmenter dans les prochains jours. Le délai légal pour contester l’élection des membres du Parlement devant la Cour constitutionnelle est fixé à 30 jours à compter de la proclamation des résultats, soit jusqu’au 25 octobre. Les mêmes sources expliquent que le faible nombre de recours enregistrés à ce stade s’explique notamment par le fait que plusieurs candidats souhaitant contester les résultats n’ont pas encore reçu les procès-verbaux électoraux. La préparation des dossiers nécessite également du temps, notamment pour examiner les procès-verbaux, rassembler les enregistrements vidéo et autres éléments de preuve et procéder à leur transcription, conformément aux conditions requises pour le dépôt d’un recours. Certaines candidatures pourraient également être liées à l’évolution des consultations politiques en cours pour la formation du prochain gouvernement dirigé par Fatima Ezzahra Mansouri. Des responsables de partis pourraient ainsi chercher à éviter de contester l’élection de candidats appartenant à des formations susceptibles de devenir leurs partenaires au sein de la future majorité. Par ailleurs, certaines formations politiques auraient entrepris de regrouper les recours électoraux et de les soumettre à l’examen de leurs commissions juridiques avant leur transmission à la Cour constitutionnelle au cours de la semaine prochaine, ce qui pourrait entraîner une hausse du nombre de recours. Les sources citées par Hespress précisent que les six recours actuellement recensés correspondent uniquement aux dossiers déposés directement auprès de la Cour constitutionnelle. Certains candidats pourraient avoir déposé leurs recours auprès des préfectures et provinces concernées, une procédure également prévue par la loi. Elles écartent par ailleurs l’hypothèse selon laquelle la grève des avocats expliquerait le faible nombre de recours. Des sources au sein du barreau affirment que les cabinets restent ouverts depuis plusieurs semaines aux candidats souhaitant engager une procédure devant la justice. Un délai de 30 jours pour contester les résultats L’article 32 de la loi organique n° 066.13 relative à la Cour constitutionnelle dispose que les recours contre l’élection des membres du Parlement doivent être introduits dans un délai de 30 jours suivant la proclamation des résultats. Selon l’article 33 du même texte, la Cour constitutionnelle statue sur les recours relatifs à l’élection des membres du Parlement dans un délai d’un an à compter de l’expiration du délai de dépôt des recours. Elle peut toutefois dépasser ce délai par une décision motivée, notamment en fonction du nombre de recours dont elle est saisie ou de la nature du contentieux. L’article 34 prévoit que le recours est introduit par une requête écrite déposée auprès du secrétariat général de la Cour constitutionnelle, du wali de la région ou du gouverneur de la préfecture ou de la province où se sont déroulées les opérations électorales, ou encore auprès du greffe du tribunal de première instance dans le ressort duquel l’élection a eu lieu. Un récépissé mentionnant la date du dépôt et la liste des documents et pièces produits à l’appui du recours est alors délivré au requérant. Les autorités et juridictions ayant reçu les requêtes en informent le secrétariat général de la Cour constitutionnelle et lui transmettent les dossiers concernés. items.title: Les Éditions du Soleil ouvrent avec « Dabakh, la pédagogie de la bonté » de Sidy Diop
items.description: Les Éditions du Soleil ont été officiellement lancées ce mardi 6 octobre 2026 au Musée des civilisations noires de Dakar. Pour cette première parution, la nouvelle maison d’édition du quotidien national a choisi l’ouvrage du journaliste Sidy Diop, intitulé « Dabakh, la pédagogie de la bonté ». La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de plusieurs autorités gouvernementales et religieuses, ainsi que de nombreux fidèles. Les premières pages de cette nouvelle « fabrique des mots » portent ainsi la signature de Sidy Diop, journaliste au quotidien national Le Soleil et formateur au Centre d’études des sciences et techniques de l’information (CESTI). Avec « Dabakh, la pédagogie de la bonté », il signe son troisième ouvrage et rend hommage à une figure religieuse dont l’héritage continue de marquer la société sénégalaise. En 244 pages réparties en huit chapitres, l’auteur s’intéresse à la personnalité et aux valeurs de Cheikh Abdou Aziz Sy Dabakh, ancien khalife général des tidianes. « La vie des hommes comme Abdou Aziz Sy Dabakh semble écrite dans une langue que le monde a oubliée », écrit-il dès les premières lignes de l’ouvrage. À travers cette phrase introductive, Sidy Diop donne le ton d’un livre qui entend moins dresser un portrait hagiographique que mettre en lumière les valeurs incarnées par Dabakh. Pour l’auteur, « le livre ne prétend pas raconter la vie d'un saint au sens convenu du terme. Il ne cherche pas à dresser une statue ni à multiplier les éloges. Il veut simplement approcher un homme qui fit de la bonté une science, de l'humilité une force et de la foi un chemin accessible à tous. » La bonté comme fil conducteur La bonté constitue ainsi le fil conducteur de l’ouvrage. Sidy Diop revient sur une valeur qui, chez Dabakh, dépassait le simple discours pour s’inscrire dans une manière de vivre et de se comporter avec les autres. L’auteur présente notamment un homme « élevé dans la rigueur, un disciple formé par les meilleurs maîtres, un guide qui refusa toujours d'être un trône. » À travers ces pages, le journaliste du Soleil dit vouloir faire découvrir, notamment aux nouvelles générations, l’homme et les valeurs qu’il incarnait. Son ambition est de permettre à « ceux qui n’ont pas eu la chance de le connaître » de mieux comprendre la personnalité de Dabakh et l’empreinte qu’il a laissée dans la société sénégalaise. Le choix de consacrer cette première publication des Éditions du Soleil à Cheikh Abdou Aziz Sy Dabakh revêt également une dimension personnelle pour l’auteur. Sidy Diop revendique un regard nourri par l’admiration et la proximité avec l’héritage spirituel du défunt khalife. « Je voulais d’abord faire un témoignage avec un niveau accessible à tous. Regrouper humblement les valeurs qu’il représentait dans un ouvrage qui puisse inspirer tous sans exception », explique-t-il. Avec « Dabakh, la pédagogie de la bonté », les Éditions du Soleil entendent ainsi inscrire leur première publication dans une démarche de transmission et de préservation de la mémoire. Une manière, dès leur lancement, de donner corps à une ambition : transformer l’information et les témoignages en récits destinés à traverser le temps. Boubacar DIOP

Guichet unique des services publics : le ministre Bourouno mobilise les maires de Conakry pour rapprocher l’administration des citoyens
items.description: Le ministre de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, Faya François Bourouno, a rencontré, ce mardi 6 octobre 2026, les maires des 13 communes de Conakry. Au centre des échanges : le projet de mise en place de guichets uniques des services publics, une initiative destinée à faciliter l’accès des citoyens aux prestations administratives et à rapprocher davantage l’administration des populations. À l’occasion de cette rencontre, le ministre Faya François Bourouno a présenté aux élus locaux les grandes lignes de ce projet porté par le gouvernement. L’objectif affiché est de modifier l’approche de prestation des services publics afin de réduire les contraintes administratives et d’améliorer la satisfaction des usagers. « J'ai eu cette belle rencontre avec les maires, les 13 communes de Conakry pour leur présenter un projet du gouvernement, le projet du guichet unique des services publics conformément à la vision du chef de l'État, le président Mamadi Doumbouya, le gouvernement a décidé de changer d'approche de prestation des services publics pour mieux rapprocher le service public des citoyens et créer toutes les facilités permettant désormais aux citoyens guinéens d'accéder facilement aux services publics, mais aussi d'améliorer leur niveau de satisfaction, mais au-delà des citoyens également améliorer aussi les démarches administratives en faveur du secteur privé », a expliqué le ministre. Selon le ministre Bourouno, l’implication des communes est essentielle dans la réussite du projet, compte tenu de leur proximité avec les populations et de leurs responsabilités en matière de services publics locaux. « Compte tenu du rôle et des responsabilités des communes en matière aussi des prestations de services publics pour leurs citoyens, il était important de partager les enjeux, les objectifs du projet et faciliter cette mobilisation pour qu'ensemble nous puissions travailler dans la mise en place des premiers guichets de services de guichets unique de services publics dans les différentes communes de Conakry », a-t-il ajouté. La prochaine étape consistera notamment à identifier les premiers sites pilotes devant accueillir ces guichets. Le ministère entend ainsi travailler avec les communes afin de définir les modalités pratiques de leur opérationnalisation. « À partir de maintenant, nous aurons l'appréciation des différentes communes et nous allons ensemble nous investir pour identifier les premiers sites pilotes et nous allons continuer à collaborer pour travailler afin d'opérationnaliser ces services et nous travaillerons aussi pour mobiliser les citoyens afin désormais de considérer que l'État a changé d'approche de prestation pour prendre en compte leurs préoccupations et donc faire de ses guichets uniques les principaux centres de prestations de services publics dans les différentes communes », a précisé le ministre. Pour le ministre, la mise en place des guichets uniques ne signifie pas une modification de la nature des services proposés par l’État, mais plutôt une transformation de leur mode d’accès. « On va les orienter et ça changera pas la nature des services publics. Ça va changer la méthode de prestation donc ça va faciliter l'accès et également il y aura toute une communication sur les nouvelles modalités de prestation de services publics envers ces populations », a-t-il indiqué. Du côté des communes, l’initiative est accueillie avec intérêt. Le maire de la commune de Lambanyi, Baba Alimou Barry, s’est dit satisfait de la présentation faite par le département. « Nous sommes très satisfaits de la rencontre et de la qualité de la présentation que nous avons suivie aujourd'hui. Le projet est innovant que le gouvernement inie aujourd'hui pour la population est très salutaire est très bénéfique pour nos concitoyens », a-t-il déclaré. L’élu communal estime que le guichet unique pourrait contribuer à réduire les tracasseries liées aux démarches administratives, notamment pour certains documents et services auxquels les citoyens doivent régulièrement accéder. « Avec les tracancéries administratives, avec le guichet unique, tout est facile et tu peux rester à table à la maison, tu fais Tu commandes pour ton passeport, tu commandes pour ta carte d'identité et je pense que ça serait une pri donc et tout le monde sera satisfait du service », a-t-il souligné. Pour accompagner la mise en œuvre du projet, les autorités communales entendent également jouer un rôle dans l’information et l’orientation des citoyens. À Lambanyi, le maire annonce déjà des démarches pour identifier un site approprié et mobiliser les relais locaux. « Le premier travail que nous allons faire, c'est de trouver le site c'est en très bonne voie à certains endroits. Communiquer à travers différents chefs de quartier, de différents chefs qui sont nos démembrement au niveau local tous les services parce que tout le monde vient à la commune et les orienter à ses sites au niveau de ce sites qui sera vraiment un centre qui va regrouper tous les services de l'État », a expliqué Baba Alimou Barry. items.title: Titres de séjour dans l’UE : les Marocains en tête avec plus de 2,23 millions de personnes
items.description: Les Marocains constituent la première communauté étrangère titulaire de titres de séjour au sein de l’Union européenne, avec plus de 2,23 millions de personnes, selon les données récemment publiées par l’Office statistique de l’Union européenne, Eurostat. Les citoyens Marocains arrivent en tête en termes de permis de séjour devant les Turcs et les Ukrainiens et leur nombre connait une augmentation progressive depuis 2021. Selon les chiffres, leur nombre est passé de 2,02 millions en 2021 à 2,07 millions en 2022, puis à 2,08 millions en 2023. À la fin de 2024, ce nombre dépassait 2,16 millions de personnes. Quant au total des personnes titulaires d’un permis de séjour dans les États membres de l’Union européenne, leur nombre s’élevait à environ 27,8 millions à la fin de l’année dernière. Sur ce nombre, plus de 32 % d’entre elles étaient originaires de pays tiers, c’est-à-dire de pays situés en dehors de l’Union européenne. En termes de pays européens qui accueillent le plus de citoyens de pays tiers titulaires de titres de séjour, l’Allemagne se positionne en première place avec près de 6 millions de titres de séjour, suivie de la France avec environ 4,4 millions, puis de l’Espagne et de l’Italie, avec 4,3 millions de permis chacune. Concernant les citoyens marocains, les autorités espagnoles ont délivré plus de 42 % des titres de séjour européens qu'ils détiennent. Les données démontrent plus largement que les titres de séjour dans l’Union Européenne sont principalement liés à la famille, au travail et à la protection internationale, tandis que les études représentent une part beaucoup plus faible. Ainsi, il apparait que plus de 32 % de l’ensemble des permis de séjour valides accordés aux ressortissants de pays tiers l’ont été pour des raisons familiales. La deuxième raison de l'octroi d'un permis de séjour est liée à l’emploi et au travail, avec environ 22,3 %, puis l’asile et la protection subsidiaire (14,7 %), et enfin les études et la formation, avec environ 4,7 %. L’office statistique européen précise également que plus de 92 % des permis de séjour délivrés dans l’Union européenne étaient valables pour une durée de 12 mois ou plus, contre 5,5 % valables de 6 à 11 mois et 2,1 % valables de 3 à 5 mois. Il ressort par ailleurs que la France a accordé le plus grand nombre de titres de séjour aux Algériens pour 81,8 % des titres détenus en Europe, tandis que l'Allemagne a délivré un total de 68,7 % des titres de séjour détenus en Europe pour les Syriens. Enfin, les données d'Eurostat soulignent que le nombre de permis de séjour accordés à des ressortissants de pays tiers a augmenté de 4,6 % entre fin 2024 et fin 2025 avec les plus fortes hausses enregistrées en Roumanie, à Chypre, en Bulgarie et à Malte. Et huit pays ont enregistré une baisse du nombre de permis délivrés aux ressortissants de pays tiers, il s'agit notamment de la Pologne, la Hongrie, la Croatie et de la Lituanie. The post Titres de séjour dans l’UE : les Marocains en tête avec plus de 2,23 millions de personnes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Solar power transforms lives in remote Amazon communities
items.description: Solar panels are transforming lives in remote Amazon communities as El Niño threatens to worsen drought. In Nova Sociedade, deep inside a protected area of Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, solar power provides clean water and enough electricity to meet the daily needs of 36 families. The community previously relied on diesel generators, but fuel is costly and polluting, while power is limited and unreliable. So far, similar systems have been installed in 29 other communities. The technology is also providing electricity to schools, health centers and local businesses. items.title: Partenariat d’excellence entre l’hôpital Abderrahmane Mami et l’Institut Curie
items.description: L'Hôpital Abderrahmane Mami de l’Ariana a eu le plaisir d'accueillir aujourd'hui le 6 octobre 2026 une délégation de l’Institut Curie – France, dans le cadre d’une rencontre consacrée au développement de nouvelles perspectives de coopération médicale, scientifique et académique. Cette rencontre s’est tenue en présence du Directeur Général de l’Hôpital Abderrahmane Mami, de la Présidente du Comité Médical ainsi que des Chefs des différents Services Hospitaliers, témoignant de l’importance accordée au développement des partenariats internationaux et au partage d’expertise. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur plusieurs axes structurants de coopération : Accueil de stagiaires associés, afin de favoriser les échanges professionnels et le partage d’expériences. Développement de Master Class destinées aux médecins seniors, autour de thématiques médicales spécialisées et des pratiques innovantes. Développement de stages pour les jeunes assistants hospitalo-universitaires, leur permettant d’acquérir de nouvelles compétences et de les valoriser au sein de leurs services à leur retour. Accompagnement dans les essais et la recherche clinique, ainsi que le développement des compétences en biologie moléculaire, en appui aux activités diagnostiques et de recherche. Développement des actions de prévention et de promotion de la santé, notamment à travers le projet « Hôpital sans tabac », en cohérence avec l’engagement de l’hôpital en faveur d’un environnement de soins sain et sécurisé. Cette rencontre ouvre ainsi des perspectives concrètes pour une coopération durable, fondée sur la formation, l’innovation, la recherche, le partage des compétences et l’amélioration continue de la qualité des soins. L’Hôpital Abderrahmane Mami réaffirme, à travers cette dynamique, sa volonté de consolider ses partenariats nationaux et internationaux au bénéfice des professionnels de santé et, avant tout, des patients.
